## TU1 blockers, round 2 (main, round mainpool5)

- **`dst[0] = c; dst++;` is not `*dst++ = c;`.** `func_0204d5bc` (tag parser) was 39 diffs. The extended type scan (`scratchpad/ovhi16/t/ts.py`) found `long i` for the `'o'` loop index, which fixed the `q`/`i` swap (`r8`/`sb`) and left 20: in both inlined copies of `TextWin_CopyParen`, `j` and `dst` were in each other's scratch registers (`r0`/`r1`), and the target kept `j` apart from the return value (`add r0, r1, #1`). Writing the copy loop body as `dst[0] = s[j++ + 1]; dst++;` (and `dst[0] = 0;` after it) matched. The two forms give the same instructions, but in the target `dst` ends up coalesced with the return value instead of `j`. So when an inlined copy loop has a scratch-register swap between the index and the pointer, try splitting the post-increment store into a store and a separate increment. The same change on `func_020508f4`'s copy loop made it worse (13).
- **A new draft matched by climbing the declaration order: `func_0204f804`.** This 0x448-byte text typewriter step (one glyph per call into a VRAM block) had no draft. The first draft was 63 aligned diffs. The case order (`0x14`, `0x11`, `0x12`, `0x10`, from the jump-table targets), `TextWin_SetOrigin` for the two `GfxMgr` stores, `c = ' '` before `pad = 8`, reading `data_02097ce0->unk_00c` back before the `numBlocks` increment, and the 24 orders of the 4 end-of-page statements (`page++; unk_3d8++; flag25 = 1; unk_18 = 0;`) took it to 19. What was left was a stack-slot swap (`font`/`pad`) and a register swap (`fn`/`stop`). The type scan found nothing. `hc.py` (hill climb over the lines of a block, `scratchpad/ovhi16/t/hc.py`) on the 9 declarations found an order with 0 diffs in under 5 minutes. Moving one declaration at a time had only reached 19, so let the climb swap pairs too.
- **The same climb found nothing for the other blockers.** It ran on the declarations of `020508f4` (14 lines), `02051a34` (11), `0204ffdc` (12, with `textwin.patch`) and `0204e5d4` (31), 120–150 rounds each. The type scan improved `0204e5d4` from 57 to 40 (`s16 sh`, which holds `bp & 0x1f`, and `long outline`; draft `scratchpad/mainpool5/d/e5d4_40.cpp`). What is left there is stack-slot assignment and a `bp`/`w`/`sh` rotation in the pixel loop. Block-scoped `w`, `sh` and `t` did not change it.
- **`func_0204ffdc` (52): the target's zero register is not a constant operand.** Besides the `r7`/`sb` swap of the zero register and the line pointer, the target computes `y` as `add r2, sb, r0` (zero register plus the offset), where we fold `dy = 0` into `add r2, r0, #0`. Writing `dy` first in the sum folds it away completely (58). A second `dy = 0` in the loop changes nothing. Something keeps the target's `dy` from constant propagation. Finding that may also fix the swap.
- **No new leads on the VRAM-free rotation (`0204f524`, `0204f5bc`, `02051210`).** If/else and `switch` forms for the base, a `VramBase` inline (ternary, early return, `int kind` parameter, `void *` result), the sum written in other orders, `win->numBlocks = i = 0`, `for (win->numBlocks = i = 0; ...)`, a `do { } while (0)` around the loop and an extra earlier function using the same inline all gave 12 (10 in `02051210`). Every compiler version gives the same 12. In `02051210` the target materialises both constants in the entry block, interleaved with the first loads, so they come from something above the `delete` block. Locals initialised at the top of the function are propagated and do not do it.
- **`func_02050ebc` (2) still folds `0x3c0 + 0x12` into `0x300 + 0xd2`.** These also fold: a member function on the sub-object, a second base class (with or without a vtable) and an inline member call through it, an inline returning `&o->sub`, `owner->sub->id` with a one-element array, a constant or runtime-zero index (`[n - 4]`), a volatile pointer cast, and `id` as a 16-bit bit-field. An inline that takes the sub pointer and the name gives 14.

## Sphere triangle tests and CSE of sign extensions (itcm, round itcm2)

- **Write every fixed-point product as `(s64)a * b`, with no `s64` locals, and let CSE choose `umull` or `smull`.** `func_01ff9f9c` (sphere against one triangle) mixes the two forms in a way that looks random. The projection `p = center - dist * n` uses `umull; mla; mla` for x and `smull` for y and z. The first edge dot uses `smull`, and the second and third edges use `umull` with the high words of `n.y`/`n.z` spilled. A small test (`scratchpad/itcm2/x4.cpp`, `x6.cpp`) shows that plain casts give exactly this. MWCC turns the sign extension of the first plane-dot term (`n.x`) into a 64-bit common subexpression, and that CSE then needs the full multiply. Each later repeat of a cast that has already been seen also uses the full multiply. `s64 nx = tri->n[0];` locals (the ray functions' trick) turn every projection and edge product into `umull` (only the plane dot keeps `smull`), so do not use them here.
- **An address-taken stack vector can get a second, scalar copy.** In the sphere test the projected point is stored twice per component (`str [sp, #0x10]` and `str [sp, #0x10c]`). That is one variable `p`, later reused as the hit point and passed to `MTX_MultVec43`, not `hit = p`. A separate `hit` copy put the scalar copies somewhere else. The edge tests read `p` back from the low copy.
- **The info block differs between the sphere tests.** `func_01ff9f9c` reads the hit point into three locals before scaling it by `owner->scale` (all three `ldr`, then `str x, y, z`, like `HitMulVec33`). It keeps `HitTriOwner *owner = q->owner;` for both `distSq` and `MI_Copy48B`. `func_01ff9060` uses the ray functions' form instead.
- **Control flow in the closest-feature part.** Edge 0 writes its closest point straight into `p`. Edges 1 and 2 build a temporary and copy it when `found == 0 || s <= dist`. Edge 2 does not set the flag; it ends with `goto found`. The vertex tests run only if `found == 0`, and when vertex 2 is out of range the function returns, even if vertex 0 or 1 hit. Write it that way.
- **What did not change anything.** The order of the edge-local declarations and of the three cross-product lines (all 36 orders gave the same code: single-use locals move to their use). Ten spellings of the rounding constant (`0x800LL`, `(s64)0x800`, `(1LL << 11)`, `(u64)`, ...) all give `adds #0x800; adc #0` on their own. The target's `mov rX, #0x800` and zero register in `adc` come from constant CSE across the function, not from the macro.
- **Drafts.** `scratchpad/itcm2/9f9c.cpp` (9f9c: register-masked seqdiff 154, 922 instructions against 923) and `9060.cpp`, which `gen9060.py` builds from the 9f9c body inside the quadtree walk of `func_01ff868c` (masked 320). In 9f9c the target keeps the zero in `r3` from the entry, so most registers in the first half differ. The frame is 0x124 against 0x118.
- **`ae08`/`868c` (still 13 and 36 diffs).** None of these changed the hit-position store order: multiply-assigned function-scope temporaries (`f`/`t`) instead of fresh locals, `fx32 *` stores (`pos[0..2]`, `*pos++`), every `HitVecScale*` inline, `VecFx32 *pos` locals, reading `p` into locals first (49). Nor did these change the `origin - pos` loads: `HitDistSq`, `HitVecSub` + `HitDot`/`HitMagSq`, swapped term order or a `VecFx32 *pos` local. `mover.py` on the eight statements around both spots, the type scan with `fx32` added, and 25 minutes of the permuter (about 100 iterations a minute when nothing else runs) found nothing either.
- **Tool.** `scratchpad/itcm2/sd.py src func itcm -m` masks registers and stack offsets in the sequence diff. On a fresh draft of a large function it is a better guide to structure than the raw count, which register noise dominates (691 raw against 154 masked for 9f9c).

## Constructed locals, `.rodata` as `const` and moving a pointer into a loop (ov000, round big8)

These took the ov000 mini-map marker function `func_ov000_021675ec` (1912 bytes, `src/ov000/MiniMap_021675ec.cpp`) from 245 aligned diffs to a match. It had been on the ov000 skip lists since round lo5.

- **A local with a constructor stays on the stack.** The target stores the player's x/z into an 8-byte stack object once at the top. The first loop uses the stored registers, and the two later loops reload the values from the stack before the loop (`ldr r4, [sp, #0x18]; ldr fp, [sp, #0x1c]`). Plain struct locals were always split into registers, whatever accessed them: a pointer passed to an inline, a nested inline, an aggregate initialiser, a two-element array, a struct copy inside the inline or a by-value parameter (that added one copy per call). A struct-returning `MkPos()` kept it in memory, but with an extra 8-byte temporary. `struct Ctr : Pos { Ctr(s32 a, s32 b) { x = a; y = b; } };` declared as `Ctr c(pl->x, pl->z);` gave exactly the target's frame (136 to 50 aligned). If the frame is 8 or 12 bytes larger than the draft's and the target reloads a small vector from the stack, try a class with a constructor.
- **Mixed declarations set the slot order.** With `c` constructed in mid-function, the function-scope `Pos m;` took the higher slot. Declaring `Pos m;` right after `c` (C++ allows it) swapped the two slots, as in the target (50 to 16).
- **Index a struct array instead of `base + i * 4`.** `ents[i * 4]` and `*(u16 *)(ents + i * 4 + 2)` shared one address register. The target computes the address again after the branch, which only came from `struct { u8 kind; u8 pad; u16 id; } *ents` with `ents[i].kind` and `ents[i].id`.
- **`automover.sh` found the last register rotation.** Moving the loop-invariant `buf = (Oam *)(w + 0x64c);` from before the loop into the loop body (just before `u8 n = w[2]++;`) fixed the rotation of four callee-saved registers (21 to 2). Writing it as `&((Oam *)(w + 0x64c))[n]` does the same. Declaration-order climbs and the type scan had not changed it.
- **Declare `.rodata` symbols `const`.** The last 2 diffs were a struct copy from `data_ov000_021c9a9c + 0x74`: the target loads both words before either store, the draft interleaved them. That symbol lies in ov000's `.rodata`, and declaring it `extern const u8 data_ov000_021c9a9c[];` let the loads move above the stores. Check `delinks.txt` for the section ranges: any data symbol in `.rodata` can be `const`, and a load that the target hoists above an unrelated store is a sign of it. Statement orders, temporaries, pointer locals and inline setters did not reproduce it.
- **`G2_SetOBJShape`-style masks.** Setting two OAM bitfields as `e->shape = 0; e->size = 1;` gave `bic; bic; orr`. The target's `ldr =mask; and; orr #0x40000000` came from one word operation: `attr = (attr & ~0xc000c000) | 0x40000000`. An unsigned shift needs `(u32)(u16)x >> 12` (the round big5 note), or MWCC uses `asr`.
- **`func_ov000_02166be8`: a shared check as an inline made declaration order matter.** In the same class's update function (draft `scratchpad/big8/6be8/best29.cpp`) every diff was one permutation of callee-saved registers: the target colours the hoisted zero and `k` first (`r4`, `r5`) and `self` fifth (`r8`), the draft gave `self` `r4`. Declaration order (400 hill-climb steps), the type scan, a copy of `self`, the body as an inline, `const` on the table and 12 minutes of the permuter changed nothing at all. Writing the "paused" test that cases 4 and 7 both open with (`skip = FALSE; if (!player) skip = TRUE; if (Has(q, 9) || Has(q, 10)) skip = TRUE;`) as one `static inline BOOL Skip()` moved `self` to `r8`, and after that the declaration order did matter: a hill climb went from 109 to 40 aligned diffs. When declaration order changes nothing, look for a repeated block that should be an inline.
- **A struct-copy local declared after a statement.** Declaring `Pos c = table->pos;` after `tgt = ctx->target;` (a C++ mixed declaration) put the `ctx` load first at the top of the function, as in the target (40 to 33). Assigning `c` as a statement instead split it into registers.
- **A local for a field that is read and then updated keeps the high-word zero out of a register.** The tail computes `dx = ... - w->cbc` and later `w->cbc += FX_MUL(k, dx)`. The target loads `cbc` once and keeps it, and its two `+ 0x800` use `adc #0`. The draft reloaded `cbc` and kept the zero high word in a register (`mov r3, #0` hoisted, `adc ..., r3`). `ox = w->cbc;` used in both places fixed both (33 to 29, no structural diffs left). `w->cc0` is reloaded in the target, so it stays a field expression. The last 29 are the registers of the 64-bit tail (`e`, `dz` and the `sq` low word): moving each tail statement, the type scan, the `sq` operand order and four `FX_MUL` signatures did not fix them.
- **Quick checks on the other big near-misses this round.** `automover.sh` is slow on these (one to three minutes per statement), so it ran fully only on `021675ec`. On `func_ov011_02204428` (6) moving the `FX_Atan2` line, the `VEC_Add` before it and the `Ov011_MulVec33` call to every position changed nothing below 6. On `021fe2a4` (22), `const` on its three `.rodata` externs changed nothing. In `func_ov007_021ce038` (draft `scratchpad/big8/ce038/c.cpp`, 28 structural) the queue scans read `read`/`write` inside the inline (as in ov000's `CmdQueue_Has`), which took 92 to 84 aligned. The target there reloads the queue pointer for each of the four scans but keeps `read`/`write` in registers; the draft does the opposite. `FLD(u16, m, 0xc2) &= ~0x20` gives `and` with a pool constant where the target has `bic #0x20`: a 1-bit field at bit 5 gives the `bic` (`bf.cpp`, 27 structural), but it moves every register (481 aligned).

## TU2 string-pool blockers, round 2 (round mainpool2)

None of the nine TU2 blockers matched this round, so TU2 is still not merged. Drafts are in `scratchpad/mainpool2/d/`.

- **Pointer arithmetic on a constant pointer is only partly folded.** `func_02059c98` (box collision mesh for an `ObjPool` entry) computes its allocation size as `mov r1, #0x10; add r1, r1, #0x9c; add r5, r1, #0x390`. Integer arithmetic in any form (`+=`, separate statements, a loop, `register`, `sizeof`/`offsetof`, `u64`) folds to one constant. Pointer steps of different types do not fold across statements:

  ```c
  u8 *p = (u8 *)0x10;   /* header */
  BoxTri *t;
  p += 0x9c;
  t = (BoxTri *)p;
  t += 12;              /* 12 triangles of 0x4c bytes */
  size = (s32)t;
  ```

  This gives the target's three instructions. `(u8 *)0x10 + 0x9c` in one expression is folded by the front end, and two `u8 *` steps in a row are merged.
- **What `func_02059c98` is.** It calls `func_02059b14`, sets `kind = 4`, and allocates a `"TCOL"` mesh resource (`func_0203de84(0x45c, 4)`). The resource has `ofsHeader = 0x41c`, 12 triangles, a scale matrix (`MTX_Scale43_`/`MTX_Inverse43` at +0x48/+0x78), and `HitBounds` at +0x34. It then builds the 8 corners of the entry's box as `s16` vertices (`FX_Div(size, scale)`, where scale is `0x1000` or `FX_Div(max, 0x7fff) + 0x19a`). Two triangles per face come from `func_0203ff94`, with face values from `0x02082a10` and index tables from `0x02082a78` (4th argument nonzero) or `0x02082b08`. Finally it does `new HitMesh` (`func_0203dd9c(0x98)` + `func_0203f80c`), `func_0203f990`, `func_0203f8d8`, sets a translation-only matrix with `func_0203f9dc`, and returns the entry. The three table addresses are plain `.word`s in the target (no symbols or relocations in `config/`). Together with `data_02082a28` (`StageCmd.cpp`) they look like TU2's `.rodata` (`0x02082a10`..`0x02082b98`; the next TU loads `0x02082b98`). The TU2 merge will have to account for that range. The draft is `9c98_best.cpp` (122 sequence diffs; plain `for` loops, verts declared before the attribute table and matrix for the target's stack layout, `s` used for both the size and the scale as in the target). Still open:
  - the register roles of `res`, `res + size` and `flip`;
  - both face loops are not rotated in the target (`b` to `cmp i, #6`). No `for`/`while`/inline/count-parameter form reproduced this. The only non-rotated constant loop found in matched code is `func_ov006_021e3f10`, where `i` reuses a register that already holds 0;
  - the mesh flag writes are `bic #8; orr #8` and `bic #2; orr #0`. Plain, signed, `bool` and `BOOL` bit-fields, inline setters, manual mask expressions and `static const` values all fold to a single `orr`/`bic`. MWCC only keeps a `bic` plus `orr` pair when it writes 1 to bit 0 of a unit (`n->a = 1` gives `bic #1; orr #1`), or for a signed field in a 32-bit unit;
  - the identity-plus-translation matrix is written with `stm r4!` pairs through a pointer in the target. An inline that takes a matrix pointer did not reproduce it.
- **`func_02060a08` needs a late `& 0xff` on the low byte.** The target masks the fourth key byte twice: once when it is passed as `u8` and once again right before the final `orr`. `*p = (d & 0xff) | ((a << 24) | ((u32)(b << 24) >> 8) | ((u32)(c << 24) >> 16));` inside `Flags_AddSlot(StageFlags *, u8, u8, u8, u8)` gives the target's instruction count (62 to 50 aligned diffs, `0a08_f1.cpp`). Writing `(u32)(d << 24) >> 24` gives `lsl`/`lsr` instead, and `u32` parameters drop the first mask. The remaining diffs are register choices plus one operand order: the target keeps `a << 24` in a register and folds `>> 8` into the `orr`, while ours folds `a << 24`. Bit-field keys (`u32 d:8, c:8, b:8, a:8`) give `bic` sequences, so the key is not a bit-field.
- **`func_0205e29c` (9).** The pool order (`data_ov000_021ccd64` before `data_02149efc`) and the store of `unk_14` follow from a single register swap at the top: the target puts `args[2]` in `r2` and the zero for `unk_80` in `r3`. `automover.sh` on `e29c.cpp` found nothing that helps.
- **`func_0205b68c` (StageRes get/set, 46 to 41).** `rso.py` reordered the declarations in the bit-get loop. Only register allocation in the two bit loops is left (`d/b68c.cpp.rsobest`).
- **`func_0205b1b4` (2).** The target holds the function pointer in `r2` while the zero is in `r1`. Moving the handler assignment after the stores gives `r2`, but it also moves the pool entry and the store (6 diffs). Inline setters, a local function-pointer variable, defining `func_0205bef8` or `data_0208bde8` in the file, and `MI_CpuClear8` changed nothing. The permuter (about 1100 iterations on a minimal C file) found only non-equivalent code.
## Inline return forms in a message dispatcher, and register rotations that would not move (ov000 and ov007, round big9)

`func_ov000_02171478` (3072 bytes, a 22-case message handler that creates task objects with `new`) was drafted for the first time this round (`scratchpad/big9/1478/best22.cpp`, 22 aligned diffs). Each case is `if (a != 0) return; if (Try(task, b, c)) return; self->vfunc_08(a, kind, b, c);`, where `Try` is an existing out-of-line function or an inlined `BOOL` helper. The helpers' return forms decide the code:

- **Two nested `? TRUE : FALSE` inlines give two normalisations.** The target tests one field with `movne r0, #1; moveq r0, #0; cmp r0, #0` twice in a row. `return Inner(q) ? TRUE : FALSE;` around `static inline BOOL Inner(q) { return q->f != NULL ? TRUE : FALSE; }` reproduces it; one inline gives one.
- **Early `return FALSE` lets MWCC predicate a bitfield set.** `if (p == NULL) return FALSE; p->b0 = 1; return TRUE;` gave the target's `ldrne/bicne/orrne/strne` with `moveq r2, #0` / `movne r2, #1`. Writing it as `if (p != NULL) {...; return TRUE;} return FALSE;` or with a result variable gave a branch around the store (16 diffs).
- **A test whose answer is always TRUE stays a test.** In one case the target sets the result to 1 on both paths (`moveq r2, sl` and `movne r2, sl`) and still emits the base call after `cmp r2, #0`. `if (p == NULL) return TRUE; p->b0 = 1; return TRUE;` keeps it. `if (p != NULL) p->b0 = 1; return TRUE;` folds the test and drops the 14-instruction base call.
- **Assignment order of byte and halfword locals sets their spill slots.** Values computed before an allocation and passed to the constructor afterwards go to `fp` or the stack. Swapping two assignments (`lo = b; hi = (b >> 8) & 0xffffff;`) moved them to the target's homes. Declaration order made no difference here (`permblk.py` over the declarations).
- **Load order of a ring buffer's indices.** The inlined `MessageQueue_FindById` in the target reads `writeIndex` before `readIndex`. A local copy of the inline that reads `end` first fixed the load order. The header version reads `readIndex` first.
- **Still open in `02171478`.** In the `FindById` loop the target colours `q, i, index, result` as `r3, r2, r1, r0`. The draft has `r0, r3, r2, r1`. Writing `index` as a ternary (`u32 index = i >= 16 ? i - 16 : i;`, draft `alt14_regs.cpp`, 14 diffs) gives the target's registers for `q` and the result, but `sub; cmp; movlo` instead of `mov; cmp; subhs`. The type scan, declaration order, a `Mgr *` parameter, a result variable, `self->messages + index` and four ways of writing the caller changed nothing. Four more diffs are scheduling in the `0x3c` allocation case.
- **`tools/permuter/cc.sh` writes to `/tmp`** (`mktemp -p /tmp`). Don't use it in sessions that must not write outside the clone and scratch directory.
- **`func_ov000_02166be8` (29, registers of the 64-bit tail) did not move.** `automover.sh` ran over 25 of the 44 statements of `best29.cpp`. The only lower scores came from moving the case 4 call or another case's statement into the tail, which changes the code. A tail variable separate from `e`, reusing `tgt`, no variable at all (re-reading `w->cb4`), `dx`/`dz`/`ox` in a block in all six declaration orders, `sq` as an inline (two forms) and no `sq` variable all gave the same 29. MWCC splits a variable into separate live ranges, so which variable holds a value does not matter there.
- **`func_ov007_021ce038` queue scans.** Reading `write` from the global in the loop condition (`i != ((Ov007MsgQ *)data_ov000_021ccd54)->write`) took the draft from 84 to 58 aligned (25 structural, `scratchpad/big9/ce038/f3.cpp`), but the target loads `read` and `write` once. The target also reloads the queue pointer before each scan. Locals for `read`/`write` with the global read in the loop, a queue parameter and a `volatile` cast on the global all loaded the global only once.
## Inline return types and the extended type scan (all overlays, round ovhi16)

- **Declare a count inline as returning `long`.** `func_ov010_0220dbc0` (10 diffs) and `func_ov010_0220a374` (32) both loop `for (i = 0; i < Count(coll); i++)`, where `Count` is `u8 r = 0; if (c->b0) r = c->count; return r;`. The draft had the loop index and the looked-up id (or object) in each other's callee-saved registers. Declaration order, block-scoped locals, a `while` loop and every type for `i` and `id` changed nothing (an `s16 i` fixed the registers but added a sign extension to `i++`). Changing only the inline's return type to `long` (`static inline long Count(...)`, same body) matched both. `s32`, `int` and `u32` did not. As with the round ovhi15 `long` locals, `long` and `int` are both 32 bits, but the implicit conversion at the comparison changes the allocation order.
- **A `BOOL` inline declared as `s16`.** `func_ov000_0218af9c` (2 diffs since round lo13: the spill store of `on` came after the `lsl`) matched when the early-return "game idle" inline `GIdle` (`if (Busy(g)) return FALSE; if (g->state != 3) return FALSE; return TRUE;`) was declared `static inline s16` instead of `BOOL`. None of the 720 statement orders, the declaration climb or the permuter had found it.
- **`s32` for a local that holds an `s16` field.** In `func_ov003_021d7e58` (ticker interpolation, 7 diffs) `cur = self->cur; v = cur + (s16)FxMul(self->next - cur, 0x1000 / d);` matched once `cur` was `s32` instead of `s16`.
- **The type scan now covers inline signatures.** `scratchpad/ovhi16/t/ts.py` (from round ovhi15) also tries the return type and the scalar parameters of every inline the function uses, and tries `s16`/`u16` on 32-bit locals. All four matches above came from it. Across 100 drafts below 0x500 bytes in every overlay, it also improved `func_ov002_021e0280` (20 to 9, `long i`), `func_ov002_021dedf0` (20 to 9, `s16 w` in the inline), `func_ov003_021d6a3c` (36 to 16, a `long` inline parameter), `func_ov000_021597dc` (34 to 18, `u8 trig`), `func_ov002_021d8d00` (34 to 24) and `func_ov010_0220dbc0`'s twin above. It costs a few seconds per draft, so run it on every new near-miss. Any result that narrows a type (`s16`, `u8`) must be checked by hand for truncation.
- **`automover.sh` found nothing.** It ran on 28 drafts from ov000 low and overlays 2–15. Its few lower scores either changed what the code does (`func_ov002_021e5974`: a store moved above the loop that sets its value) or traded a register swap for a store-order swap (`func_ov003_021ddce4`, `func_ov002_021e2690`).
- **A matching draft that cannot be split: `func_ov000_0214b670`** (solved in round twl2: `0214b68c` is kept with `force_active`). The draft `scratchpad/ov000q/w/b654.cpp` matches, but after it splits out, the gap from `0x0214b68c` to `0x0214b6d0` holds only `func_ov000_0214b68c`. Nothing references that function: its two `bl`s go to TWL-only code (`relocs.txt` has `module:none` for `0x02224e44` and `0x02224eb8`). The linker's `-dead` then strips the gap, and every later function in ov000 shifts. Before `0214b670` was split out, the callers of `0214b670` in ov003 and ov011 kept the gap alive. `func_ov000_0214b438`..`0214b5bc` and `0214b724`/`0214b810` also call TWL-only code and have no drafts.
- **Still open, with this round's attempts.** `func_ov003_021ddce4` (3 diffs; draft `scratchpad/ovhi16/w/dce.c`): MWCC hoists the shared first `bic #1` of both branches out of the `if`, and the target does not hoist it. Swapping `b1 = 0` and `b0 = 0` in the zero branch gives 2 diffs, but then the `biceq`s are in the wrong order. `-1`/`TRUE`/a variable for the 1, a parameterised inline, `!= 0` with swapped branches and pointer-expression variants did not help. `func_ov010_02201bf4` (4): the volatile flag byte must stay in `r1` and the shifted copy go to `r2`. Taking the byte's address (as `func_ov010_02201ad4` does) gives exactly that allocation, but it leaves a stack frame in this leaf function. `func_ov000_0217a1f8` (3): the target materialises `-1` with `mvn` where MWCC derives it from the `0x78` argument (`sub r2, r1, #0x79`), whatever the parameter types are. Its sibling `func_ov000_0217a480` does the same `sub` in the target. `func_ov002_021e2690` (4): two loop-invariant constants (3 and 8) are hoisted into each other's registers. ## Per-scan reloads of a global, and what the type scan did on big functions (all overlays, round big10)

- **A global that the target reloads before every inlined scan: read it through a `volatile u32` lvalue.** In `func_ov007_021ce038` case 5, four inlined ring-buffer scans test four ids. The target loads `read`/`write` once into `r0`/`r1` and keeps them, but reloads the queue pointer (`ldr rX, =data_ov000_021ccd54; ldr r5, [rX]`) before scans 2–4. With `read`/`write` as caller locals passed to the inline, MWCC kept the pointer in a register for all four scans, whether the inline read the global in its header, in the loop or through a pointer parameter. `Ov007MsgQ *q = (Ov007MsgQ *)*(volatile u32 *)&data_ov000_021ccd54;` in the inline header gave the reloads. The form `*(Ov007MsgQ * volatile *)&data_ov000_021ccd54` (a volatile pointer type in the cast) was ignored: the load was still shared. Writing the loop test as `w != i` instead of `i != w` then fixed the registers of the scans (58 to 44 aligned), and the type scan added `long w` for the caller's `write` local (42, `scratchpad/big10/best/ce038_42.cpp`). ## Shifting coordinates in place, and the joint move/type climb (all overlays, round ovhi17)

- **Copy a position into locals first, then shift or offset the locals in place.** Three screen-position functions matched once the coordinate arithmetic was split into a plain copy followed by in-place updates. Writing the arithmetic in one expression gives the same instructions but puts the intermediate values in other registers, or schedules the loads in another order.
  - `func_ov000_021c2e64` (7 diffs): the inline that calls `o->vfunc_20((x + 0x8000) >> 12, (y + ((h - o->unk48) << 11)) >> 12)` matched once its by-value parameters were updated first: `x += 0x8000; y += (h - o->unk48) << 11; o->vfunc_20(x >> 12, y >> 12);`.
  - `func_ov000_021c28cc` (6): `x = ((self->x + 0xa000) >> 12) - 0x80; y = ((((self->h - 8) << 12) + self->y) >> 12) - 0x60;` became an inline with out-parameters, `ScreenPos(&x, &y, self->x, self->y, self->h)`, whose body is `x += 0xa000; y += (h - 8) << 12; *ox = (x >> 12) - 0x80; *oy = (y >> 12) - 0x60;`. Taking the address of the two locals does not force them to the stack once the inline is expanded.
  - `func_ov006_021df5a0` (11): in the loop, `x = out.x >> 12; y = base + (i * 9 + (out.y >> 12) + 8);` became `x = out.x; y = out.y; x >>= 12; y = base + (i * 9 + (y >> 12) + 8);`.
  In each case the original draft was already right except for the registers or the order of the two coordinate loads. Try this split whenever a near-miss computes `(a.x OP k) >> 12` and `(a.y OP k) >> 12` in one statement. It also brought the Caption draw code (`func_ov006_021e0b80`, from 23 to 8 diffs; the same code inlined in `func_ov006_021e1bb4`, from 16 to 5) closer: `ox = self->unk10 + 0x80; oy = self->unk14 + 0x60; x = ...; y = ...; ox += (w - a44) >> 1; oy += (h - a48) >> 1;`. In both, the `y` half still lands in the wrong registers. The final `oy` is computed into the register of `h - a48`, not in place. No variable split tried so far reproduces that.
- **Case order decides how identical `switch` arms are merged.** `func_ov002_021e6508` has a rate inline that is `switch (mode) { case 0: return r; case 1: return r; default: return r; }`. Written in that order, each arm keeps its own `b`. Listing `case 1` before `case 0` gives the target's `beq L; cmp #1; b L; L:` (7 diffs down to 2). The remaining 2 diffs are the loads of `0x7c` and `0x88` in swapped order. Return-type, local and `FX_MUL` operand-order variants did not swap them. Draft: `scratchpad/ovhi17/d/ov002_021e6508/s0.cpp`.
- **`u8 n` is the right type for `func_ov003_021e6274`, but it moves `self`.** The target masks the stage number with `and #0xff` (from 14 diffs, the remaining ones are exactly that). Declaring `n` as `u8` fixes every mask but swaps `self` and the part pointer between `r6` and `r7` (46 diffs). The `Ov003Obj *me = self` trick that fixed those registers for `u16 n` no longer helps. The joint climb below brings the `u8` draft down to 6, but only by moving `n = n - 1;` above the `n == self->unk_93_1` test, which changes behaviour. - **The joint move/type climb (`scratchpad/ovhi17/t/combo2.py`) found nothing new.** It scores every single-line move (within `MAXD` lines) and every type change from `ts.py` together, deduplicates the neighbours by the hash of the compiled code, and looks two steps ahead from the best different-code neighbours. On `func_ov002_021e0280`, `021dedf0`, `021e6508`, `021d6a3c`, `021e1bb4`, `021e0b80`, `0220640c` and `func_ov003_021e6274` it either found nothing or only moved a call (`func_020627dc(4)` in `021e6274`, 14 to 13, which changes the order of side effects). ## TU1 blockers, round 3 (main, round mainpool6)

- **An integer add keeps a member offset from being folded into the field offset: `func_02050ebc` matched** (now at the end of `TextWin_11.cpp`, whose `delinks.txt` entry grows to `0x02050f70`). The target reads the owner's id as `add r0, r4, #0x3c0; ldrh r0, [r0, #0x12]`. Every member, cast, base-class and inline form folds `0x3c0 + 0x12` into `0x300 + 0xd2` (rounds mainpool3 and mainpool5). `((NameOwnerSub *)((s32)owner + 0x3c0))->id` keeps the two parts apart and matches. `(u32)owner + 0x3c0` and `(u8 *)owner + 0x3c0` still fold; only the signed integer cast works. When a large field offset is split at a sub-object boundary instead of at `& ~0xff`, try computing the sub-object address as an `s32` sum.
- **How MWCC orders callee-saved registers, measured on small test functions** (`scratchpad/mainpool6/x/t*.c`, disassembled with `t/odis.py`). Locals get registers in declaration order, so the first-declared local gets the lowest register. Hoisted loop-invariant constants (`mov rX, #imm` in the preheader) get lower registers than every local, and the later-materialized constant gets the lowest. Hoisted non-constant expressions (`n * 3` with a parameter `n`) and parameters get registers above the locals. The target's VRAM-free loop (`0204f524`, `0204f5bc`, `02051210`, `0205592c`) has `i` below both constants (`i` r5, `0x6400000` r6, `0x6600000` r7), which is what we get when the bases are parameters or other non-constant invariants, not constants. `func_02051a34` (the hoisted `0xffff0000` above `win` and `fn`) and `func_0204ffdc` (the zero register above the line pointer, see below) show the same pattern. So in all three the target's constant behaves like a variable or an expression that became constant after hoisting. Nothing found so far does this in a draft. These all still give constant ordering: locals initialised at the top (also `register`, `void *`, `u8 *`, self-assignments, assignment in both arms of an `if`, assignment via `Set(&lo, ...)`), aggregate or array initialisers (these go to the stack), every compiler version under `tools/mwccarm`, `-O4,s`/`-O3`, and the pragmas `opt_strength_reduction`, `opt_lifetimes`, `opt_propagation`, `opt_dead_assignments`, `opt_dead_code`, `opt_unroll_loops`, `optimization_level 1`..`3` and `ipa file`. A struct returned by value from an inline (`VB v = MkVB();`) does keep the bases as variables, but adds a stack temporary. A second use of the constants before or after the loop does not move them to the entry block of `02051210`, and neither do `delete` for the `obj` release or `do`/`while` loop forms. Loop-index types change nothing either.
- **`func_0204ffdc` (52).** The type scan (`ts.py`, 19 declarations) found nothing. Inserting `dy = 0;`, `dy += 0;` or `dy = dy;` at every statement slot (`t/ins.py`) changed nothing either. In our build the add is `add r2, r0, #0`, so the zero reaches the backend as an immediate. In the target it is `add r2, sb, r0`, a register that holds 0.
- **`func_020508f4` (8).** 50 minutes of the permuter (about 2500 iterations, standalone C++ draft `d/08f4p.cpp` without the `TextWin` header), `automover.sh` over every statement, an inline for the copy loop (with parameters in both orders, or a `char **` parameter), calling `font->cbCharSpliter` directly (91) and removing or inlining `tag` all left the `fn`/`dst` swap.

## Copying sibling code into undrafted functions (ov000 and ov003, round ovhi18)

- **Start an undrafted function from a matched sibling.** Five functions matched in this round, four of them at the first or second compile, by copying a matched neighbour's structs and inlines and editing only what the target does differently. Near-misses with many earlier rounds of variants moved much less. Before you start a fresh function, look for one that has the same call sequence (the same `vfunc_XX` offsets, the same `NNS_G3dGeBufferOP_N` command list).
  - `func_ov000_021593b8` and `func_ov000_02158588` (list draw) are copies of `func_ov000_021561f8` (`Lo_02155f68.cpp`) with fewer branches. In `02158588`, two edits fixed the last diffs. First, `if (top->next2 == NULL) k = 0; else k = -1;` written in each branch gives the target's `moveq #0; mvnne #0`. The `? :` form, `k--`, and `!= NULL` with the arms swapped each leave 4 to 8 diffs. Second, the selected item `self->a8` needs its own pointer local (`sel`). Reusing the `top` local swaps two registers.
  - `func_ov000_02155770` (list input) inlines a copy of the `func_ov000_02152294` body. The inlined factory only matched with `void *res = data_02149ef8;` declared before `VObj *p;`.
  - `func_ov000_02153804` (G3 window frame, 17 aligned diffs, `scratchpad/ovhi18/d/3804/s2.cpp`) uses the `G3_Vec`/`G3_Cmd1`/`G3_Vtx`/`G3_VtxXY` inlines of `func_ov000_02155f68`. The `v[n - 1]` index the target keeps in a register is `n = self->unk70 - 1;` computed once. Inline arguments are evaluated right to left, so `G3_VtxXY(V[2].x, -t)` (with `V` the field read, not a local copy) computes `-t` before it loads the array, as in the target. What remains is one swap of `r8` and `sb` between the `FX_Div` result `t` and the divisor `sy`. Declaration-order and type climbs (`hc2.py`) did not move it.
- **Bit tests that look like bit-fields.** `func_ov000_02155770` tests `tst #0x10000` on the flags word. The bit-field `LBIT` form used elsewhere in the file did not match here. Write the mask test, `LFLD(u32, self, 0xc) & 0x10000`.
- **Count the arguments of a virtual call from the registers.** When a `blx` through a vtable slot has `r3` (or a stack slot) set just before it, the method takes more arguments than its siblings. `vfunc_b0`/`vfunc_b8` in `02155770` take `(LFLD(s32, self, 0x20), 0)`. The `0` that looks like dead code is the second argument.

MWCC builds `0x29` from the register that holds `0x2e1` only if `speed = 0x2e1;` comes before `self->vel.y = 0x29;` in the source. In the other order it builds the constants the other way round.

The draft is otherwise structurally complete (`scratchpad/ovhi18/d/b598/s0.cpp`).
- **Small results from this round's near-misses.** In `func_ov003_021e44dc`, passing the `Ov003Big_Load` parameters as `(ext, name)` takes it from 7 to 2 (`scratchpad/ovhi18/d/44dc/v_rev.cpp`). In `func_ov015_021fce94`, writing the stores as "SetFovyND, n, f, dirty" gets the store order right, but it then rotates `r1`/`r2`/`r3` (24 against the base 13; `scratchpad/ovhi18/d/ce94/p0132.cpp`). `func_ov006_021dacb0` (SlotManager create, new draft, 41) is right in structure. ## TU2 blockers, round 4 (round mainpool7)

No TU2 blocker matched this round, so TU2 is still not merged. Drafts are in `scratchpad/mainpool7/d/`.

- **Coloring order of virtual registers.** Small test functions (`scratchpad/mainpool7/exp/`) show the order MWCC assigns registers when nothing is under pressure. Compiler temporaries (constants, CSE and hoisted values) come first, then locals in declaration order, then parameters, last parameter first. Each one takes the lowest free register. A copy `T *p = param;` is coalesced into the parameter and keeps the parameter's place. An inline's parameters and locals rank as locals of the caller. So a parameter only gets a lower register than a local when the graph is under pressure (spills). That is the case in `func_0205a358`, where the target has `pool` in `r4` and the entry in `r5`. Nothing found this round reverses the order there.
- **`func_0205e5c4` (19 to 2, `d/e5c4_best2.cpp`).** Three changes:
  - Declaring `u32 lo;` before `int type;` (assigned separately) moved `id & 0xf000` into `lr` and removed the extra `sb` push.
  - The parameter block is set up by an inline in the style of `SpawnInit021b5dc0` (`src/ov000/Mgr_021b5dc0.cpp`): `LightParam_Init(&param, 0xffff)` writes `key = id`, `mask = id & 0xf000`, clears `unk_04[4]` and sets `unk_0c = -1`. The draft's hand-written `0xffff`/`0xf000` stores and the `-1` written after the key both go away.
  - The two final writes use different shift forms: the key is `lo | ((u32)(type << 28) >> 16)` and the mask is `((u32)type << 28) >> 16`. Because the two expressions differ, they are not CSE'd, which gives the target's `lsr r3`/`mvn ip` registers and its store order.

  `hcm.py` (below) then climbed the function, block and statement orders to 2. The last 2 are the order of `data_02149efc.unk_14 = NULL` and `unk_04 = NULL`. Only the source order `unk_04` then `unk_14` gives the target's registers, but the target stores `unk_14` first. Writing `unk_14` first, a chained assignment, an inline setter or a pointer local each lengthen the life of the `&data_02149efc` register (the second store is scheduled later), and that costs 13–15. With `res = slot->res` and both stores before the `{ id ...}` block (`d/e5/g1.cpp`, 9), the registers and the store order are right, but `id` is then loaded after the stores.
- **`func_02060b18` (21 to 17, `d/b18_best17.c`).** Two changes:
  - The `0a08` trick: a function-scope `StageFlags *f;`, assigned in each branch.
  - Declaring `u32 i;` before `u32 key = ...` in the clear inline (the reverse of what was tried in round 3 without `f`).

  The second branch is now correct except for one `and` pair and an `orr` operand order. The first branch still has `f` in `r3` (target `lr`).
- **`func_0205c234` (2): the load is placed by the scheduler, not by the statement position.** The draft is one instruction early on `ldr r0, [r0, #0x18]`. Wherever `start = data_02149efc.slotStart` goes, the address `ldr` is scheduled at most one store before the value load. In the target there are two stores between them. A pointer local or a `volatile s32 *` to the field, at any pair of positions, a `u16 *args` pointer for the stores, and `args[3]` before the load all keep 2.
- **`func_0205b1b4` (2).** `MI_CpuFill8`'s `0` is coalesced into `r1`. The function pointer moves to `r2` (the target) only when the zero is materialised before the handler store. In the source, that happens only when a zero store comes first, and then the stores come out in the wrong order. Two inlines with reversed parameters (`Init(0, func)`, `Init(&g, func, 0)`) and a `Reset(g, slots)` inline still gave 2. `-O4,s`, `-O3` and the other compiler versions don't help.
- **`func_02059c98`: the `stm r4!` run is `MTX_Identity33_`.** The target's `mov r1, #0x1000; mov r2, #0; mov r3, #0; stm r4!, {r1, r2}; stm r4!, {r2, r3}; ...; stm r4!, {r1}` writes a 3×3 identity into the matrix at `sp+4`, after the translation at `+0x24`. It looks like an inlined asm identity (the real `MTX_Identity33_` is at `0x02011340` and uses the same `stm` pairs). An `asm { }` block with the matrix pointer bound to a register is the next thing to try.
- **Unchanged this round:** `0205e29c` (12), `02060a08` (17) and `0205a358` (71). The `e29c` attempts were reversed `GetArea` parameters, the index as `int`/`u32`, `unk_80 = 0` first, and `Stage_FindObj3D` as a local-variable, early-return or ternary inline (139: the inline shape changes the code). The `0a08` attempts were 192 key and parameter forms combined with the `f` local, and a `u16 v` copy of `args[1]` (29). For `a358`, 40 minutes of the permuter (11 700 iterations) found nothing. So did `hcm.py` on the 10 inline declarations plus `e`/`next`/`pl`, inlines taking `(e, pool)`, the loop in an inline (it then exceeds the inline depth and `CheckBox` is no longer inlined), and `x`/`y`/`z`/`unk_18` as loop-body locals.
- **Tools.** `scratchpad/mainpool7/t/hcm.py src func module iters block1 [block2 ...]` is `hc.py` over several blocks at once. Each step swaps or moves lines inside one random block. `HCCONS="1:2<3"` keeps line 2 of block 1 before line 3. `t/matchx.py` is `match.py` with extra compiler flags from `MWX`. A climb's `.hcN` output file needs the `.cpp` extension back before `match.py` compiles it as C++.
- **Backgrounding.** `cd dir && nohup cmd &` backgrounds the whole `&&` list, so `$!` is a subshell and not the permuter. Run `cd` as its own command, then `nohup cmd &` on its own line, so `$!` is the process you need to stop later.

## TU1 blockers, round 4: the VRAM bases are variables (main, round mainpool8)

- **`func_02051210` and `func_0205592c` matched.** The VRAM-free loop's bases are variables that the optimizer did not propagate, and the loop index is a `long`. The working form defines the bases twice, the second time under a condition that is never true at run time:

  ```c
  long i;
  u8 *objBase;
  u8 *subObjBase;
  objBase = (u8 *)0x6400000;
  subObjBase = (u8 *)0x6600000;
  if ((u32)win & 3) {
      objBase = (u8 *)0x6400000;
      subObjBase = (u8 *)0x6600000;
  }
  ...
  MIi_CpuClearFast(0, (b->kind == 4 ? objBase : subObjBase) + b->addr, b->size - b->pad);
  ```

  The optimizer does not propagate a variable that has two definitions into the arms of a `?:` (it does propagate it into arithmetic, see below). The backend then sees that the second assignment is redundant and deletes it together with the `if` and its condition, so nothing of it is left in the code. A variable gets a register above the locals, which is the target's order (zero, `i`, `0x6400000`, `0x6600000`, then the parameter). This only works with `long i`: with `int i` the index still gets the highest register (`i` r7). A `long` index also does this in small tests where the bases are hoisted non-constant expressions (`q * 3`, `q * 5`), so the index type affects the order whenever the bases are variables. In `02051210` the definitions go at the top of the function, which also puts both `mov`s in the entry block as in the target. In `0205592c` (not a TU1 function; it fills the gap after `FieldMsg.cpp`, whose entry now ends at `0x020559c8`) they go after the bitfield clears.
- **The condition has to leave no trace.** `if (cache)` leaves a `movs`. A condition that loads (`cache->blocks[0]`) or reads the value that is being stored (`cache->count`) is scheduled before the `if` is removed and moves the bitfield code to `r1`. A condition on the bases themselves (`a != c`) pulls the `mov`s above the store. `(u32)cache & 3` and `i == 0x7f` (on the not-yet-initialised index) leave nothing.
- **`func_0204f524` (3) and `func_0204f5bc` (1) do not match yet.** Here the target also stores `numBlocks` from the index register before the bases: `mov r5, #0; strb r5, [win, #0x3bc]; mov r6, #A; mov r7, #B; mov r4, r5`. Every order of the four statements (`i = 0`, the store, the definitions, the `if`) misses one detail. With the `if` after `i = 0` (`ISDU`), the hoisted loop zero is `mov r4, #0` instead of a copy of `i`, because the backend only reuses a register that holds 0 when the definition is in the loop preheader, and the removed `if` leaves the preheader as a separate block until after that pass. In `f524` this also swaps the first two instructions. With the definitions and the `if` before `i = 0` (`DUIS`), the copy is there but the scheduler puts the two `mov`s before the `strb`. Storing `0` instead of `i` before the definitions (`SDUI`, the form that matches `0205592c`) gives the store its own `mov r0, #0`. Things that did not help: a second `i = 0` after the `if`, a duplicate definition of `i`, `if`/`else` with the same definitions on both sides (propagated), redefinitions inside the loop (the backend keeps them), `?:` and self-assignments (folded), address-taken tricks, empty `asm {}`, defining the bases in the loop, and passing them as parameters to an inline.
- **No other way to make a constant into a variable worked.** These were all propagated or folded and gave constant ordering: `static const` (C and C++), `const` locals, single-member and two-member struct locals, unions (these use a stack frame), `u64`, `float` and `s64` casts, `&*(u8 *)K`, `((VramMap *)0x6000000)->obj`, a local plus an offset, inlines that return the base, and conditions that fold only after propagation (`int z = 0; if (z) ...`, because the optimizer runs to a fixpoint). Non-const file statics and globals are loaded. Arithmetic on a two-definition variable is not folded by the backend (`lsl r6, r1, #1` for `v * 2`).
- **`func_0204ffdc` (52): the same trick does not reach `dy`.** `if ((u32)box & 3) dy = 0;` changes nothing: the optimizer still propagates `dy` into `y = dy + ...` (arithmetic uses are propagated even with two definitions), and the backend writes `add r2, r0, #0`. A `long dy` keeps it as a variable but puts the duplicate's block between `dy` and `busy`, so `busy` gets its own `mov r5, #0` and the diff grows to 155.
- **`func_02051a34` (35) and `func_020508f4` (8):** the type scan (`ts.py`, whose type list includes `long`) found nothing for either. In `1a34` the hoisted constant is the mask `0xffff0000` that the compiler makes for the 16-bit `textPos` bitfield store, also used as `-1` via `asr #16`. It does not appear in the source, so the two-definition trick does not apply to it.
## An `s64` accumulator, block-local CSE of a global, and unsigned ring indexes (all overlays, round big12)

`func_ov000_02166be8` matched this round (new file `src/ov000/Lo_02166be8.cpp`). Drafts are in `scratchpad/big12/d/` and `scratchpad/big12/best/`.

- **Build a sum of squares in an `s64` accumulator: `func_ov000_02166be8` matched (29 to 0).** The distance check `sq = (s32)(((s64)dx * dx + (s64)dz * dz + 0x800) >> 12);` gave the target's `smull`/`smlal` order but swapped the registers of `dx`, `dz` and the product. Writing `(s64)dz * dz + (s64)dx * dx` gave the target's registers but the wrong multiply order (19). `{ s64 t = (s64)dx * dx; t += (s64)dz * dz; sq = (s32)((t + 0x800) >> 12); }` matches. A single expression `s64 t = a + b;` does not (29), and neither does accumulating in the other order (36). When a `smull`/`smlal` chain has the right instructions but the wrong registers, try splitting it into an accumulator and `+=` statements.
- **MWCC only CSEs a global inside one basic block. `func_ov007_021ce038` went from 19 to 10.** The four message-queue scans read `data_ov000_021ccd54` again in each scan. The round big11 draft used a `volatile` read in each scan and passed the caller's pointer to the first scan only. That cost one register swap in the first scan. In the target, the first scan's queue pointer and the caller's `q0` are one register, because both loads are in the same basic block. So the first scan is the same inline with a plain (non-`volatile`) read, `Ov007_HasMsgN(r, w, 2)`. The other three scans keep the `volatile` read. Without `volatile` there, MWCC hoists the global into a callee-saved register and every register in the function changes (486). When a reloaded global and a caller's copy of it share a register in the target, read it with a plain load in the first block and with `volatile` in later blocks.
- **Still open in `021ce038`: `Ov007Cam_SetA` (10, `best/ce038_10.cpp`).** These forms kept the reversed order of the four temporaries:
  - every declaration order of `x`, `u16 a = 0xaaa` and `s32 b = 0xeff1` as locals, with `k` as a parameter or as a local;
  - the constants passed as inline parameters in four orders, with `x` declared, split from its declaration or left out;
  - the address as a literal in the body (MWCC then folds `+0x54` into the pool constant);
  - all 24 store orders with literal addresses;
  - `x`/`y`/`k` as caller locals or inline parameters.

  On a 30-line reproduction (`scratchpad/big12/x/a.cpp`, compiled by `t/mc.sh`), 432 combinations of these forms (`x/gen.py`) never gave the target's `k r0, x r1, 0xeff1 r2, 0xaaa r3`. - **`func_ov000_02171478` (11): `u32 index = (u32)i < MESSAGE_QUEUE_LEN ? i : i - MESSAGE_QUEUE_LEN;`** gives the target's `mov r1, r2; cmp r2, #0x10; subhs r1, r2, #0x10` (`best/1478_11t.cpp`). Only the `end`/`index` registers (`r1`/`sl` swapped) and one scheduled `lsr` are still wrong. The `if` form `index = i; if (index >= LEN) index -= LEN;` gives the same instructions, but it moves every register in the scan (23). The type scan and `hc2.py` on that `if` version reached 22. ## TU2 blockers, round 5 (round mainpool9)

`func_02059c98` and `func_0205a358` matched, so 6 TU2 blockers are left and TU2 is still not merged. Drafts are in `scratchpad/mainpool9/d/`. The best ones are `e5c4_best2.cpp` (2), `c234v3.c` (2), `b1b4_min.c` (2), `e29c_g.cpp` (9), `a08x_if.c` (13) and `b18w_16.c` (16).

  ```c
  asm {
      str x, [m, #0x24]
      mov r1, #0x1000
      str y, [m, #0x28]
      ...
      stmia m!, {r1}
  }
  ```

The bit-field writes kept their `bic #8; orr #8` and `bic #2; orr #0` pairs, and both face loops stopped being rotated (`b` to the `cmp`).   - The three tables are now `data_02082a10`, `data_02082a78` and `data_02082b08` in `symbols.txt` (`kind:data(any)`, like `data_02082a28`). They are still in the delinked `.rodata` gap, so the TU2 merge still has to take over `0x02082a10`..`0x02082b98`.

## Constants in branch locals, and `s32` for a bit-field read (overlays 2 and 15, round ovhi19)

- **A constant assigned in both arms of an `if` becomes a variable.** `func_ov002_021e6d4c` (13 diffs, `scratchpad/ovhi18/d/6d4c/a.cpp`) picks `y` and `pal` in an `if`/`else` and then passes `10` as the x of a position inline. In the target, `10` goes to `r0`, the reloads of `data_02097ce0` go to `r1`/`r2`, and the zero for the `+8` store (`r4`) is set before the first store. Declaring `s16 x;` and writing `x = 10;` in both arms (after `y` and `pal`) matches; any type for `x` works. `x = 10;` before the `if`, between the stores, or as an initialiser all stay at 13. This is the same effect as the round ovhi18 `k = 0` / `k = -1` in each branch: a value set in the branches is a variable at the join and is coloured as one, not as a constant that is rebuilt where it is used.
- **`s32` for a bit-field value keeps the shift in the operand.** `func_ov015_021fb25c` (digit glyphs, 16 diffs) reads the 10-bit `w` field of the last glyph and later computes `w - (val % 10) * 2`. `func_ov007_021ce038` matched this round, which completes overlay 7. Drafts are in `scratchpad/big13/best/`.

- **`0x02071160` was `FX_SinCosTable_ + 0x100`, not a literal address. Writing `FX_SinCosTable_[(0x555 >> 4) * 2]` and `[(0x555 >> 4) * 2 + 1]` gives the target's registers and load order directly. When a pool word is near a known table, subtract the table's address and check whether the remainder is an index the code already uses.  
  ```c
  u32 zero;
  zero = 0;

      zero = 0;

  data_0208bde8 = func_0205bef8;
  ```

## Two-definition constants and loop indexes, and loads in tail-merged switch arms (overlays 2 and 3, round ovhi20)

`func_ov002_021e6508`, `func_ov002_021e0ff8` and `func_ov003_021de6b4` matched this round. Drafts are in `scratchpad/ovhi20/d/`.

- **A constant argument can be a two-definition variable too: `func_ov003_021de6b4` matched (6 to 0).** The round mainpool8 trick (define a variable a second time under `if ((u32)ptr & 3)`) is not only for VRAM bases. In this bomb-fuse tick the `0x325` argument came from the pool into `r2`, and the target has it in `r4`, after the three scale-vector constants. `kind = 0x325; if ((u32)self & 3) { kind = 0x325; }`, placed just before the `sc.x/y/z` stores, gives the target's registers. The same definitions at the top of the function, or right before the call, give 4. `t/tdc.py src func module` automates this: for every numeric literal in the function it tries the variable form at every statement position from the top down to the use (`TDNEAR=n` limits the distance, `TDT` the types). It found nothing else this round, but it is cheap to run on any function where a constant has the wrong register.
- **A loop index with two definitions keeps the preheader order: `func_ov002_021e0ff8` matched (2 to 0).** The target sets `i = 0` before `by = y + 0x14` in the loop preheader. Every statement order, `long` types, a `do`/`while` loop and `by` declared in the loop all gave `by` first. `i = 0; if ((u32)self & 3) { i = 0; } by = y + 0x14; do { ... } while (++i < 4);` matches. The two-definition `i` alone (with `for (; i < 4; i++)`) keeps the order right but brings back the entry test (`cmp r6, #4; bge`), because the optimizer no longer knows that `i` starts at 0, so the loop has to be a `do`/`while`.
- **Put a load in every arm of a switch to move it ahead of the join's loads: `func_ov002_021e6508` matched (2 to 0).** The target switches on the mode at `+0x84` with identical arms, then loads `+0x7c` before `+0x88` for an `FX_MUL`. The round ovhi18 draft read `+0x88` in each arm (`Rate6508`) and `+0x7c` after the switch, so the tail-merged `+0x88` load came first. The arms read `+0x7c` (`Ov002Anm_Frame`: `case 1: return FIELD(self, 0x7c, s32); case 0: ...; default: ...`), and the multiply is `f = Ov002Anm_Frame(self); f = FX_MUL(f, FIELD(self, 0x88, s32));`. The later `cmp lr, r0` against `+0x7c` still uses the same register, because the CSE sees the value from every arm. An empty switch is removed completely, and a switch whose arms all set the same index or pointer leaves `b` chains instead of jumping straight to the join. If tail-merged arms load the wrong field first, swap which value comes from the arms.

## TU1 blockers, round 5: where the zero copy comes from (main, round mainpool10)

Nothing matched this round, so TU1 is still not merged. Drafts are in `scratchpad/mainpool10/d/`. The test harness `scratchpad/mainpool10/v/t524.sh 'body'` compiles a small standalone C copy of `func_0204f524` (`d/f524_t.c`, `BODY` replaced by the argument) in about 0.3 s, which is much faster than the `TextWin` drafts for sweeps.

- **The hoisted zero becomes `mov r4, r5` only when `i = 0` is in the block the zero is hoisted into.** The backend replaces a hoisted `mov rX, #0` with a copy of a register that it knows holds 0. That knowledge passes down a chain of single-predecessor blocks, but not into a block with two predecessors, even when both of them leave the register at 0 (`if (c) { ...; i = 0; }` before the loop changes nothing). The join block after the never-true `if` is the loop preheader, so the `ISDU` form of round mainpool8 always gives `mov r4, #0`. Every form with the copy has `i = 0` after the `if`, or has no `if` at all (the plain constant form also has the copy, but with constant ordering). The same knowledge is what lets `func_0204ffdc` use `sb` for every later zero. There it works across joins because the register is assigned only once in the function.
- **Where the base `mov`s end up.** The backend moves the base definitions down to the end of their block. So with `D I S U` (definitions first, then `i = 0`, the store and the `if`), the `strb` still comes out before the two `mov`s. With `D U I S` the definitions and the store are in different blocks. After the `if` is removed, the merged block is scheduled in source order apart from critical-path ties. `mov r5, #0` goes first (it feeds both `strb` and the copy), and the two `mov`s come out before `strb` (3 diffs).
- **Copies of two-definition variables are not propagated.** This gives forms with the copy and the right registers, but the schedule is still wrong:
  - `d/f524_3_basecopy.c` (3): `u8 *ba, *bc` get the two definitions (`ba = A; bc = B; if ((u32)win & 3) {...}`) at the top, and then `i = 0; win->numBlocks = i; a = ba; c = bc;`. It has `mov r4, r5` and the target's registers. Only `strb` is after the two `mov`s.
  - `d/f524_8_zcopy.c` (8) has exactly the target's instructions, but with the registers rotated. `n` gets the two definitions and is stored (`n = 0; win->numBlocks = n; ... if (...) { n = 0; ... } i = n; z = n;`). The loop uses `u16 z` for all three zeros and is a `do`/`while`, because a `for` loop keeps its entry test once `i` is no longer a known constant. Variables joined by a copy share one register, and the group ranks at the later declaration of its members. In 5760 type, declaration and copy orders (`v/g7.py`), the register with the zeros never got `r4`. When the copy got `r4`, it was `i`, and `z` held the zeros. The best is the rotation at 8.
- **Hoisted conversion temporaries.** When `z` is `u32` and still used in the loop, the hoisted `(u16)z` for the `strh` gets `r4`, the lowest register (36: `mov r4, r8` plus an extra `r8`). When every use goes through the conversion, it is merged into `z` and ranks last again.
- **Tried without success:** `if`/`else` with the definitions in different orders (the `tst` stays), `?:` forms (folded), a `goto` from the `if` body into the loop (the branch stays), unconditional or conditional redefinitions at the end of the loop body (kept as copies through scratch registers), `asm { mov a, #... }` (this turns off optimization for the whole function: `i` is loaded from the pool and the loop test comes back), absolute-address objects (`u8 objVram[4] : 0x6400000;` compiles, but gives constant ordering), a `volatile` store, and narrow loop-index types.
- **`func_0204ffdc`.** `dy` behaves like the zero register of round mainpool8: a two-definition `dy` defined far from its `if` keeps the `tst` (the backend only removes the `if` when the definition is in the same block chain). Next to the definition, it breaks the zero copies in the blocks after the join (`busy` gets `mov #0`). `long`/`s64`/`u32`/`int dy` alone all stay at 52.
- **`func_020508f4` and `func_02051a34`.** A two-definition `fn` (`if ((u32)win & 3) fn = font->...;`) keeps its load and branch (the backend does not know the loaded value). A copy through a second local is folded away. In `1a34` the `0xffff0000` mask also gives the `-1` of `win->args[0] != -1` (`cmp r0, r6, asr #16`), so a mask variable would also need that compare rewritten.
## `const` source pointers, a `volatile` stack parameter and the ITCM padding (itcm, round itcm3)

`func_01ffc318`, `func_01ffc624` and `MIi_DmaSetParameters` (was `func_01ff8020`) matched this round. Drafts are in `scratchpad/itcm3/`.

- **`const` on a source pointer gives "load all, then store all" with descending registers.** `func_01ffc318` (point in a rotated box) copies the translation into the matrix: the target loads `trans->x/y/z` into `r4`/`r3`/`r2` and stores them after the `MTX_Inverse43` arguments are set up. Every order of locals, loads and stores (216 forms), struct copies, pointer locals, inlines and two-definition variables gave either an `ldm` or the stores in the wrong order. Declaring the parameter `const VecFx32 *trans` and writing the three plain `m._30 = trans->x;` assignments matches. A matched main-module struct copy with the same shape (`obj->pos = *pos` in `func_0206500c`, which also takes a `const` pointer) gave the hint: `scratchpad/itcm3/t/pat.py` searches all modules for `ldr rN; ldr rN-1; ldr rN-2` from one base followed by stores of the same registers. When the target has descending registers for three loads from one pointer, try `const` on that pointer first.
- **`const` on an inline's parameter adds a register copy.** In the same function the box test reads `v.x` into `r1`, compares it, and copies it to `r2` for the second compare (`mov r2, r1`). `HitInBox(const VecFx32 *p, ...)` does exactly this; without `const` there is no copy. The `MathItcm.h` helpers (`HitInBox`, `HitInCylinder`, `HitInCube`, `HitMagSq`, `HitMagSqXZ`) now take `const` pointers; the functions that already used them still match.
- **A `volatile` stack parameter copied into a local: `func_01ffc624` matched.** It is `func_01ffc318` with `HitInCylinder` and `HitMagSqXZ` at the end. The `const` changes took it from 29 to 5: the `x` copy was right, but the target loads the stack parameter `h` right after the first compare (`cmp r1, r4; ldr r3, [sp, #0x90]`), not at its use three blocks later. The fix has two parts. The parameter is `volatile fx32 h`, so the inline's parameter copy is a real read where the inline starts (as in round lo12, but here to load early, not late). And `HitInCylinder` names its bounds, `BOOL ret = TRUE; fx32 nr = -r; fx32 hh = h;`, in that order; without the locals the read is still propagated to its use, and with `hh` declared before `nr` their registers swap. `func_01ffc4ec` and `func_01ffc584` use the same inline and still match. A two-definition `hh` (`if ((u32)r & 3) hh = h;`) also moved the load, but the scheduler put it before the `cmp` (4 diffs). `register`, `const` or other integer types on `h`, the inline's parameter order, a wrapper inline, a struct parameter for `r`/`h`, nested range inlines, `&&` or early-return forms and 1,000 permuter iterations did not help.
- **The 32 zero bytes at the start of ITCM.** Nothing refers to `0x01ff8000`..`0x01ff8020`. While `func_01ff8020` was unmatched they were part of its gap object; as a gap of their own, the linker dead-strips them and everything after moves down by 0x20. `mi_dma_itcm.c` now starts with a `#pragma force_active on` asm block of eight `andeq r0, r0, r0` (the zero word), named `ITCMi_Pad` and listed as `kind:data(any)` in `symbols.txt`, because `dsd` refuses to analyse it as a function. Written as `dcd 0` it links the same, but the report shows it at 40%.
- **`MIi_DmaSetParameters` matched on the first try** (TwlSDK, `libs/nitro/mi/mi_dma_itcm.c`). Its mode bits are 1 = no interrupt disable, 2 = the dummy reads and DMA0 clear, 4 = skip the clear, 0x10/0x20 = 32/16-bit fill source. The names in `mi_dma.c` (`NOINT = 2`, `WAIT = 4`) do not follow this.
- **`func_01ffae08` (13), `func_01ff868c` (36), `func_01ff9f9c` / `func_01ff9060`: unchanged.** `const` pointer locals and `const` copies of the subtract/scale inlines, `s64` accumulators for the distance, struct copies of the scaled position, and `tdv.py` over every assignment did not move the two `ae08` spots.

## Main-module triage, a field cached in a local, and the TWL blocker (round mainmid1)

- **Triage.** The full table of unmatched main functions outside the TU1/TU2 sets is in `scratchpad/mainmid1/triage.md`. About 25 small main functions can't be matched yet because at least one `bl` goes into TWL-only code: its reloc in `relocs.txt` is `module:none`. Examples are `func_0200c0c4`, `func_020163b8`, `func_0200d85c` and `func_02049344`; the table has the full list. Most of the rest are library code (SDK, NNS, MSL) or register-allocation near-misses.
- **`func_02039844` matched (`GfxMgr.cpp`).** Two changes were needed:
  - **The `0x20` register.** It shared a register with the loop index. Building it in the reused index variable with the two-definition trick fixed that: `i = 0x20; if ((u32)pool & 3) i = 0x20; align = i << pool->alignShift;`.
  - **The load order.** The target loads `numBlocks` (`[r1, #8]`) before `alignShift` (`[r1]`). Ours got this order when `count = pool->numBlocks;` comes right before that line and `count` is used only in the loop condition. The later `i == pool->numBlocks` must still read the field: reusing `count` there too, or moving the read to the top of the function, gives a different register or 64 differences.
- **`func_0203b12c` (1 → 13): mul operand order.** The target's `mul r3, r2, r5` (`bpp * db`) comes out when the product is written in both of its uses: `dst = buf + (((u16)bpp * db) >> 3); db = ((u16)bpp * db) & 7;`. That moves the registers around (23). A climb over the declaration order (`declhc.py`) brings it back to 13, and now only `db` and `b` are swapped in the inner loop. These did not help: the types of `b` and `db`, `b` declared in the inner block, and a `7 - db` local.
- **`func_0206d43c` (28 → 14).** Write the align inline as `u32 m = total - 1; x += m; return x & ~m;`. Keep `dataSize` in a local `d` and use `s->dataSize * s->slotCount + d`, so the compiler doesn't factor `a*b + a` into `a*(b+1)`. The rest is registers. It still has to share a file with `func_0206d99c` (the `CODASAVE` pool).
- **Unchanged.**
  - `func_02041080` (7). A two-definition `z = 0` before `if (load)` gives the target's structure, but `z` lands in `r0` instead of `r2` (11).
  - `func_0203d298` (7). Moving `prev = pad->prev;` before the `0x30` fixup gives 8 → 7.
  - `WH_ChangeSysState` (`02046070`, `020459cc`), `func_0206e858`, `func_02049690` and `func_0206f6d4`: no new form helped.
- **Tools.** In `scratchpad/mainmid1/`:
  - `declhc.py src func N` hill-climbs the order of the top declaration block.
  - `var.py base func 'old' variants.txt` scores text replacements (variants separated by `====`).
  - `sd.py` and `sdr.py` give the aligned diff count, raw and register-normalised.

This round scored every draft of every unmatched overlay function below `0x500` bytes (four newest drafts each, 541 compiles) and ran `tdc.py` (literal as a two-definition variable, `TDNEAR=6`) and `tdv.py` (second definition after each assignment, `TDV_SPAN=1`) on the best draft of all 44 functions at 2 to 10 diffs, then `tdv2.py` (below) on the 37 that were left. Eight functions reached 0, and seven of them went into the build. Drafts are in `scratchpad/ovhi21/d/auto/<func>/` (`base.*` is the starting draft, `*.tdc`/`*.tdv`/`*.tdv2` the best variant).

  - `func_ov006_021cd914` (2 to 0): the `u32 idx = 0xffff` that a `switch` then overwrites. `noIdx = 0xffff; if ((u32)type & 3) { noIdx = 0xffff; } ... u32 idx = noIdx;` at the top of `case 7` puts `mov r7, #0xff` after the pool load, as in the target. The condition here is on an `int` parameter, so it can be true at run time. That is harmless because the second definition stores the same value.
  - `func_ov006_021e9f80` (2 to 0): the `0x8000` busy mask of the `SQRTCNT` poll loop, defined right before the `s64` sum. This moves `ldr r2, [r5]` below the first `smull`.
  - `func_ov014_02202a34` (4 to 0): the `0x100` in `(u8 *)self + 0x100`, passed as the pointer argument of `func_ov003_021d85c8`. With `(u8 *)self + off`, the `add r0` and the stack-argument `str` move to the target's places.

The field-by-field versions that its neighbours `021eba54`/`021ebae4` need give 8 diffs here. Both pairs are now in `ov003_021eba54.cpp` (`Ov003PartA_Assign` and `Ov003PartA_Copy`).
  - `func_ov015_022078bc` (9 to 0) matches with `self + kq` (`kq = 0xcb8`) for `func_ov000_02191b70`, but it is not in the build: it uses real literals from the ov015 pool `0x02212ccc..0x02212d2f`. That pool also holds the strings of the pointer tables at `0x02212cac..0x02212ccb` and two strings of `func_ov015_02207adc`, and contains `"mc/c1rob4"` and `"c1rob4cha"` twice. With `extern` arrays it gives 103 diffs.
- **Matched by `tdv.py`:** `func_ov015_0220ae90` (5 to 0) needs `if ((u32)self & 3) { dec = FLD(s32, p, 0xe0); }` after the declarations. `tdc.py` also found a form with the `0` of `st->unk_1c != 0`.
- **A second definition inside one arm keeps both arms predicated.** `func_ov003_021ddce4` (3 to 0, found by `tdv.py`): the target clears two bits with `biceq ... biceq` in one arm and sets them with `bicne; orrne ...` in the other. MWCC hoisted the common first `bic r0, r0, #1` out of both arms. `if ((u32)self & 3) { p = self->unk_44; }` as the first statement of the `then` arm stops that. The same works for `func_ov013_022001b8` (3 to 0), which needs `movne r3, #0; moveq r3, #1` for a `mode == 1` argument (round ovhi19). Every ternary and bool form gave `mov r3, #1; cmp; movne r3, #0`. This one matches:

  ```c
  BOOL m;
  if (FLD(u8, self, 0x15d) != 1) {
      m = FALSE;
      if ((u32)self & 3) {
          m = FALSE;
      }
  } else {
      m = TRUE;

  func_ov013_02202dc8(self, 0xa00, 0x1000, m, 0);
  ```

  A second definition of `m`, or of a `b = 0x1000` set in both arms, works in either arm when it comes after the arm's own assignment. A second definition of an `Ov013Actor *s = self` copy that is passed to the call works anywhere in either arm. All of these need the `!= 1` condition. With `== 1`, the best is 2. When the target has a pair of predicated instructions where ours has one unconditional instruction before the `cmp`, put a second definition into one arm.
- **`tdv2.py`** puts the second definition at every later statement of the function, at any block depth (`TDV_MAXD` lines, default 12), not only right after the assignment. Since the condition is never true for an aligned pointer, any position keeps the behaviour. `TDV_IN=<inline>` (also for `tdv.py`, and `TDC_IN` for `tdc.py`) runs the search inside an inline that the function uses. On its own, it found no match this round.
