## Overlay string-pool merges (all overlays, round ovpool1)

- **`func_ov015_022078bc` is in the build.** It is now the first function of `src/ov015/ov015_022078bc.cpp` (the old `ov015_02207adc.cpp`, renamed), which covers `.text 0x022078bc..0x02208070` and `.data 0x02212d08..0x02212d30` under `#pragma pool_strings on` / `dont_reuse_strings off`. `strrefs.py --claim 0x02212d08 0x02212d30` made the pool `@stringBase0`. `func_ov015_02207adc` now uses the literals `"ang00"`/`"ang05"`.
- **`strrefs.py` can join two pools.** It shows `0x02212ccc..0x02212d2f` as one pool, but `"mc/c2rob2"` ends exactly on the 4-byte boundary `0x02212d08`, so a new object can start there. The file's own strings start at `0x02212d08` (`"c1rob4"`, `"mc/c1rob4"`, `"c1rob4cha"`, `"ang00"`, `"ang05"`). The part before that (`0x02212ccc..0x02212d07`) holds the strings of the pointer tables at `0x02212cac..0x02212ccb`, and it repeats `"c1rob4cha"` and `"mc/c1rob4"`. With string reuse on, one file can't hold the same string twice, so the tables and their strings are a different file. When a pool from `--pools` has a string that ends on a 4-byte boundary, check whether the strings after it belong to different code. The tables are still unclaimed.
- **Literal arguments go into the pool last argument first.** The first build matched every function but failed the ROM check: the pool started `"mc/c1rob4"`, `"c1rob4"`. `match.py` hides this, because it ignores relocation targets. The inline was `Ov015_SetAnim(o, name, file)`, called as `(self, "c1rob4", "mc/c1rob4")`, and its body copies `file` first. Swapping the parameters to `(o, file, name)`, called as `(self, "mc/c1rob4", "c1rob4")`, gave the same code and the target's pool order. So MWCC pools a call's literal arguments right to left, whatever order the inlined body uses them in. The reversed `Ov003Big_Load(self, ext, name)` in `func_ov003_021e44dc` fits the same rule. If the ROM check fails after a pool claim, `cmp` the built overlay with the extracted one and look at the order of the pool's strings.
- **Still blocked:**
  - **ov003 pool `0x021f8564..0x021f85c1`.** It is used from `func_ov003_021e1034` (in `ov003_021e0e8c.c`) to `func_ov003_021e6fb4` (in `ov003_021e6cb8.cpp`). One file would have to cover `.text 0x021e0e8c..0x021e7274`: about 14 files, a mix of `.c` and `.cpp`, plus three unmatched functions. These are `021e1204` (2, the `ldrh` into `r1` instead of `r0`; `switch` forms gave 27, and `k` types and casts gave 2), `021e44dc` (3 with `scratchpad/ovhi18/d/44dc/v_rev.cpp`: the target loads `"g1plt01e"` into `r6` before the first `func_ov000_0218f074` call, and ours loads it after) and `021e6274` (14). For `021e44dc`, a pool with other strings before these two still gave 3. Locals, a two-definition `ext` or `name`, split inlines and an inline parameter for the `1` arguments gave 3 to 39.
  - **ov006 pool `0x021ebbb0..0x021ebc65`.** `func_ov006_021d3f04` matches with literals (`scratchpad/ovlow2/d3f04.cpp`). The pool is also used by `021cec68` (best draft 40, `scratchpad/ovlo5b/d/cec68b.cpp`), `021cf420` (59, `scratchpad/ovlow1/cf420.cpp`) and `021d4118` (33, `scratchpad/ovlo3/d/d4118_b.cpp`). Its first string `"--------------------"` is loaded from the `.data` word at `0x021ebbac`, so that word is part of the file too.
  - `scratchpad/ovpool1/unmatched_pool_users.txt` lists every overlay pool loaded by a function that is not in any `delinks.txt` (64 rows). The ones above are the only ones with a draft known to match once it has the pool.
## Points-to through one global array, and a reused parameter as the stack-pop variable (itcm, round itcm4)

`func_01ffae08` (ray against an unsorted triangle mesh) and `func_01ff868c` (the same ray test over a quadtree) matched this round, as `src/Main/Hit/HitTriItcm.cpp` and `src/Main/Hit/HitTriTreeItcm.cpp`. Their shared types, the attribute-filter and edge macros and the small inlines are in `include/Main/Hit/HitTriItcm.h`. Drafts are in `scratchpad/itcm4/`.

- **Both hit-record pointers must point into the same global array.** The two old `ae08` spots (the hit position stored as `y` then `z`, and `origin - info->pos` loading `pos.x`/`pos.y` before the first store to `e`) had one cause. The record pointer was `info = &data_02fe14b4` (overflow slot) or `&data_02fe0f50[n]`. `data_02fe14b4` is really `&data_02fe0f50[23]` (`0x564 = 23 * 0x3c`). Written that way, MWCC knows that `info` points into `data_02fe0f50` and can't alias the address-taken stack vector `e`. So the `info->pos` loads are no longer held behind the stores to `e`, which matches the target's schedule. With `info = &data_02fe0f50[23]` the function went from 13 to 2. A test that read `data_02fe14b4.pos` directly also gave the target's schedule, which showed that this was an alias problem and not register order. The last 2 (the `y`/`z` store order) then matched with plain `HitVecScale(&p, owner->scale, &info->pos)`. Before the alias fix, that form gave `stmib`. Look for this when the target hoists loads through a pointer above stores to an escaped local, and the pointer is chosen between two globals: one of them may be an element of the other.
- **`func_01ff868c`: the popped node is the `root` parameter.** With the `ae08` body, the quadtree walk was 23 (sequence) off: the target stores the decremented `top` before loading `stack[top]`, keeps the node in the index register (`ldr r1, [r0, r1, lsl #2]`) and reloads `top` for the first push's hoisted `top * 4`. Pop and push spellings (`top--;` first, `stack[top] = x; top++;`, `top -= 1`, casts, `volatile` or address-taken `top`, inlines taking `&top`, `while`/`for`/`else` loop forms, push loops, 155 declaration orders of `node` and `top`) gave 21–145. A focused permuter run (`PERM_RANDOMIZE` around the pop, bounds test and pushes) found it in 192 iterations: there is no `node` local. The loop reuses the parameter, `root = stack[--top];`. In the source the parameter is now named `node`. Before declaring a fresh local for a loop's "current" pointer, try reusing a parameter that is dead after its first use.
- **Focused permuter runs are fast.** With `PERM_RANDOMIZE( ... )` around just the statements that differ (balanced braces, inside the loop), the 0x9d4-byte function ran at about 4 iterations a second, against about 3 a second for a whole-function run that found nothing in 15 minutes. `scratchpad/itcm4/prun.sh` is `itcm3/prun.sh` pointed at this clone.
- **`const` sweep (part 1).** `scratchpad/itcm4/t/pat2.py` is `itcm3/t/pat.py` limited to the ARM functions that `report.json` lists as unmatched, with the overlay bases read from `arm9_overlays/overlays.yaml`. The old script read none of the overlays, because there is no `.yaml` beside each `.bin`. It finds 12 functions where the target loads three words from one base into descending registers and then stores them in order: main `0205e29c`; ov000 `02189b44`, `0219d9fc`, `021a0d4c`, `021aa978`, `021b4130`, `021bd8ac`; ov009 `02208b24`; ov011 `021fc0b8`, `02203ef0`; ov014 `0220a67c`, `022153e0`. In every best draft that was checked, these spots already compile to the same pattern (plain struct copies). The remaining diffs are elsewhere, so `const` had nothing to fix. `021b4130` has no draft. Variants with any offsets (`pat3.py`) or halfwords (`pat4.py`) found nothing new.
- **`func_01ff9f9c` (154 masked) and `func_01ff9060` (320 to 312 masked): not matched.** The new tricks barely move them. In `9060` (regenerated in `scratchpad/itcm4/9060/g3.cpp`), reusing `root`, `&data_02fe0f50[23]` and `HitVecScale` save 8 masked diffs. In `9f9c` the record-pointer change does nothing. The real blocker is the constants. The target sets a zero in `r3` at entry, uses it as the high word of every rounding add (`adc rX, rY, r3`, with `0x800` in a register too), and builds the edge threshold as `sub r0, r3, #5`, which it spills once for all three edges. `ae08` spills the threshold the same way but builds it with `mvn r0, #4`. A `zero` local in the threshold (`< zero - 5`, initialised at entry or at its declaration), `found = 0` at entry (frame 0x11c, closer to the target's 0x118 but `found` is spilled) and `x + 5 < 0` (worse) did not reproduce it. About 450 iterations of whole-function permuter on `9f9c` (base score 13295, best 7775) found only noise, such as moving one edge subtraction into a function-scope temporary.

## ov003 and ov006 pool blockers (round ovpool2)

Neither pool could be merged this round: `func_ov003_021e1204` and `func_ov003_021e6274` still differ, and the three ov006 blockers are far from matching. Drafts are in `scratchpad/ovpool2/best/`.

- **`func_ov003_021e44dc` matches with real literals (3 to 0, `best/44dc_match_literals.cpp`).** Drop the `Ov003Big_Load` inline. Load `name` into a local before the first call, and assign `ext` with a plain statement after that call:

  ```c
  const char *name = "gm/g1plt01";
  const char *ext;
  func_ov000_0218f074(&self->res, (char *)name, 1, 0, 0, 1);
  ext = "g1plt01e";
  self->res = 0;
  STD_CopyString(self->unk_290, name);
  STD_CopyString(self->unk_2b0, ext);
  ```

  An inline parameter, or an initialised local, is loaded at the top of the function. A plain assignment after the call is loaded after it, as in the target. The literals appear in pool order (`name` first). A two-definition `ext` gives 16 to 47 at every position. With `extern char[]` names instead of literals, this form has 7 diffs: the addresses are rebuilt at each use, not held in `r6`/`r7`. So this function can only go in with the pool merge.
- **`func_ov003_021e6274`: `n` must be `u8`, but then the decrement moves (14 to 8, `best/6274_u16mask_8.cpp`).** The target masks with `and #0xff`, so `n` is 8-bit. These remove every mask except one:
  - `u16 n` with `n = self->unk_18 & 0xff` and `n = (n - 1) & 0xff`;
  - `u32`/`s32` `n` with `(u8)` casts;
  - `s32 a` in the prototype of `func_ov000_02197dec`.

  The remaining diff is the `and r1, r5, #0xff` that MWCC emits before the 3-bit field store `self->unk_93_1 = n`. Any store expression other than a plain `u8` (`n & 7`, `(u16)n`, `n | 0`, an inline setter) keeps an instruction there. With `u8 n` the store has no extra instruction, but the new `and` of `n = n - 1` is scheduled above the store's `lsl`. That gives the new `n` its own register, which rotates `self` and the part pointer (46; 6 with registers ignored). These all kept that order:
  - `n--`, `n -= 1`, `--n` as the argument, and post-decrement in the store;
  - a separate `u8`/`s32` local for the old or the new value;
  - inlines for the store and for the animation call;
  - a re-read `self->unk_18` for the store;
  - storing through a `u8 *`.

  Two-definition locals around the store (`u8 m = n - 1; if ((u32)self & 3) m = n - 1; self->unk_93_1 = n; n = m;`, `best/6274_u8_twodef_struct2.cpp`) get the field insert into the target's order (2 with registers ignored), but the `and` still comes first. A barrier between the store and the decrement puts the whole store first (11). 40 minutes of the permuter found only invalid forms (stores moved into dead code after a `break`).
- **`func_ov003_021e1204` (2): unchanged.** The target loads `unk_16` into the entry pointer's register (`ldrh r1, [r1, #0x16]`), and every form we tried loads it into `r0`:
  - shift and mask expressions, divisions, and `s16`/`u32`/`s32` locals for the loaded value;
  - inlines taking the value, the entry, or the whole `if` block;
  - `const` entry pointers;
  - `u16`/`u32` bit-fields;
  - reading the entry again through `self->table`;
  - a live copy of `unk_06`;
  - a pointer local for `&self->unk_d0`;
  - every position and type of `k`;
  - compiling it as C++.

  The bit-field reads in matched code (`func_ov003_021cee68` and others) do load into the base register, but here a bit-field gave `r0` too. 25 minutes of the permuter found nothing.
- **ov006:**
  - `func_ov006_021d4118` (31 to 26, `best/d4118_26.cpp`): `tdc.py` made the `0xffff` in `self->unk4A != 0xffff` a two-definition variable, which fixes the load order of `data_ov006_021eb6fe[data_ov006_021ec884->unk5]`. What is left is the camera block. The target reads `rot.x`/`rot.y` before the two vector copies and `rot.z` after them. Declaration orders, store orders, by-value or `const` inlines and a non-`const` table did not change this.

## Function-scope temporaries decide the zero register, and stack order from declarations (itcm, round itcm5)

`func_01ff9f9c` (sphere against one triangle) and `func_01ff9060` (the same test over a quadtree) matched this round, as `src/Main/Hit/HitTriSphereItcm.cpp`. `HitTriSphere` and the `elen[3]` edge lengths of `HitTri` are now in `HitTriItcm.h`. Drafts and tools are in `scratchpad/itcm5/`.

- **The "zero in `r3`" blocker was a live-range effect, not a constant spelling.** The target keeps the high word of the `0x800` rounding constant in `r3` from the entry (and `sub r0, r3, #5` for the edge threshold); our draft had the same zero register, but in `r2`, swapped with `-dist`. Two-definition zeros, `s64` rounding variables, a zero in the threshold and dot-product inlines all moved it the wrong way. The permuter found a nonsense `cx = cx;` in one edge's fail branch that put the zero in `r3`; that pointed to the real form: the cross-product results `cx`, `cy`, `cz` are **function-scope** locals (`fx32 cx, cy, cz;` after `found`), assigned in each of the three edge blocks, while `ex`/`ey`/`ez` stay block-scoped. With that, plain operand order matched everything through the edge tests (masked 154 to 3). When a register swap involves a value that is live through several similar blocks, try declaring the per-block temporaries once at function scope.
- **Operand order of the `(s64)` products is a strong lever on a wrong base.** Before the scope fix, a hill climb over the operand order of every product (`(s64)a * b`, `b * (s64)a`, cast on the other side; `t/gen2.py` and `t/climb2.py`) took the raw sequence diff from 691 to 214, with an irregular mix of orders per edge. All of that was compensation: once the scope was right, the plain uniform order was best. Treat an irregular "winning" operand pattern as a sign that something structural is still wrong.
- **The third segment test ends in `goto found`.** In both functions the target jumps straight to the hit code when `found != 0 && s > dist` after the third edge segment (jump-threaded `bgt found`), instead of a predicated `ldrne/cmpne`. Writing `if (found == 0 || s <= dist) { dist = s; p = c; } goto found;` inside the `HitMagSq <= radiusSq` block gives it; `found = 3` or a `goto found` inside the inner `if` keep the predicated form.
- **`&data_02fe0f50[23]` and `q->owner` read twice finished `9f9c`.** The last 14 diffs were the owner pointer: ours folded `owner + 8` for `MI_Copy48B` into a post-indexed `ldr r2, [r0], #8`. The round itcm4 alias fix (`info = &data_02fe0f50[23]` instead of `&data_02fe14b4`) plus `info->distSq = FX_Mul(FX_Mul(dist, block->mtx._00), q->owner->scale); MI_Copy48B(&q->owner->mtx, &m);` (no `owner` local) matches; either change alone does not.
- **Stack layout follows declaration order.** With the sphere body fixed, `9060` differed only in stack offsets (`p`/`e`/`m` at `0xc4`/`0xd0`/`0xdc` in the target). Declaring `MtxFx43 m; VecFx32 e; VecFx32 p;` in that order (later declarations get lower addresses here) matched; the other five orders gave 41 to 67 raw diffs. When only `[sp, #N]` offsets differ, permute the declarations of the address-taken locals.
- **Tools.** `t/mktmpl.py`/`t/mktmpl2.py` turn a draft into a template with `{{name|A|B}}` product, `[[name%%a%%b%%c]]` permutation and `<<name%%alt0%%alt1>>` alternative markers; `t/climb2.py` (greedy sweep) and `t/anneal.py` (random plateau walk) search them with `sd.py` raw and masked scores. `t/pat800.py` lists functions whose rounding uses a register for `0x800` or for the zero high word (only `9f9c` has both). `t/mc.sh` compiles a small reproduction and disassembles it with capstone (`t/odis.py`).

## Block-local temporaries and statement placement (overlays 0x500 bytes and up, round bigsweep1)

- **Match.** `func_ov003_021ed6b8` (0xbf0 bytes) went from 6 diffs to 0. A store that sits next to a block-local temporary has to go inside that temporary's `{}` block. In case 0 the target wants `q.unk_18 = 0;` inside the block that declares `s32 r = self->unk_64 + 0x400;`, not just before it. Moving a statement into or out of a bare block changes how MWCC schedules it, even when the statement does not use the block's variables.

## TU1 blockers, round 6: copies across joins, and a declaration climb on `0204e5d4` (main, round mainpool12)

Nothing matched this round, so TU1 is still not merged. Drafts and tools are in `scratchpad/mainpool12/` (`d/` drafts, `v/` sweeps; `v/t524.sh` is the round mainpool10 tester pointed at this clone).

A second 1500-round climb and the type scan (`ts.py`) from there found nothing. Left: `pitch` and `src` swap spill slots (`0xc`/`0x2c`), and `bp`/`w`/`sh` rotate in the pixel loop. Block-scoping any subset of `bp`, `w`, `sh` and `t`, the order and operand order of the three pixel statements, a separate variable for the end-of-glyph `bp`, and a 200-round climb over the order of the six per-glyph setup statements all gave exactly 30. So the pixel-loop registers follow the global numbering (declarations), not that block.
- **The zero copy crosses a join when its source is a copy.** In the `0204f524` tester, `u16 z; ... z = i; if ((u32)win & 3) { a = ...; c = ...; z = i; }` (with `long i`, after `i = 0; win->numBlocks = i;`) and `z` for every zero in the loop gives the target's instructions, including `mov r4, r5`. Only the registers rotate (16: `i` r4, `a` r5, `c` r6, `z` r7; the target has `z` r4, `i` r5, `a` r6, `c` r7). With a `u32 z` the backend also hoists `mov r4, r8`, a copy of `z` across the join. A two-definition constant (`z = 0; if (...) z = 0;`) gives `mov r4, #0` instead. So the backend's "register known to hold 0" survives a join for a two-definition copy of a multi-definition `long`, but not for a two-definition constant. A single `z = i` is propagated as 0 (back to 3 diffs). About 2300 type, declaration, statement and loop-form samples of this form (`v/zs.py`, `v/zt.py`, `v/zr.py`) never ranked `z` below `i`. The same holds for the 1440 declaration and copy orders of the round mainpool10 `n`/`z` form (`v/zc.sh`, best 6: `c` and `z` swapped). The best are still the old 3 (`0204f524`) and 1 (`0204f5bc`). In `0204f5bc`, putting the definitions and the `if` before `if (win->page >= win->numPages)` gives the copy, but the two `mov`s stay above the `cmp` (4).

That puts the `mov`/`rsb` in the target's place, but it turns the outer loop into a guarded form (102). `if ((u32)win & 3)` there is hoisted out of the loop and stays.

## Scope moves on overlay near-misses (overlays under 0x500 bytes, round ovhi22)

No new matches. This round tested the round itcm5 finding (function-scope temporaries decide registers, declaration order decides stack slots) on 24 overlay near-misses with 2 to 15 diffs. Drafts, logs and tools are in `scratchpad/ovhi22/` (`d/<mod>_<addr>/base.*`, `scope*.out`, `tdv2_a.out`).

- **`t/scope.py src func mod`** builds every scope move for one function (or for an inline with `SCOPE_IN=<name>`) and scores each move alone, then pairs of the best `SCOPE_PAIRS` (default 24). `SCOPE_DRY=<dir>` writes the variants without compiling them. The moves are:
  - `hoist`: every block-scoped declaration of a name goes to an enclosing block, up to function scope. Initialisers become assignments in place. In `.c` files the assignment goes after the block's declarations.
  - `hoistgrp`: all block-scoped names of one type in the same blocks move together, plus every 3-name subset when a group has 4 to 6 names. This is the round itcm5 `cx, cy, cz` move.
  - `sink`: a declaration moves into the innermost block that holds all of its uses, or into any block in between.
  - `wrap`: a declaration's use spans (for example two loops that share an index) each get a new block with their own declaration. The tool tries each span alone and all spans together.
  - `merge`: two block-scoped names of one type whose line ranges do not overlap become one function-scope variable.
  - `uninit`: `T a = e;` becomes `T a;` plus `a = e;` after the declaration list.
  - `order`: each function-scope declaration moves to every other slot of the declaration list.
- **Sanity check:** on the pre-fix itcm5 draft (`itcm5/9f9c/g4.cpp`), `hoistgrp cx+cy+cz` takes the masked score from 197 to 153. That is the known lever, so the tool does find this kind of move.
- **Results on the overlay batch:** about 7,400 compiles across all runs. No move improved any of the 24 functions. Many moves changed nothing at all, which means MWCC gave the same code whatever the scope. In the drafts that use an inline (`021708ec` `Lo_FindMsg`, `021be5dc` `CalcDepth`, `02199180` `DistSq9180`), declaration order inside the inline does matter. Writing the same body by hand in the caller does not: `02199180` scores 10 for all 18 orders and scopes of `dz, dx, dy`.
- **Other tools on the same drafts:** `tdv2.py` (`TDV_MAXD=8`) on the ten ovmid2 drafts found `021d8d00` 13 to 12 (a second `chr = last->chr` right after its declaration, `best/d8d00_12.cpp`; still 7 with registers masked). It also found the known `021c4460` 10 to 9, which needs an extra `self->unk_a4 = n` store and so is not real.
- **Hand forms that did not move (all scored):**
  - `021e2690`: function-scope `8`/`3` variables in any declaration or assignment order, a scoped `t = 8` at every level with the swapped store order. Copy propagation removes them; the store order still sets the registers.
  - `02211b2c`: a `self + 0x14c` pointer local for any subset of the four calls, the name argument in a local, `char *` and index spellings.

Nothing matched this round, so TU2 is still not merged. Drafts and tools are in `scratchpad/mainpool13/` (`d/`, `t/`).

- **The bare-block tools find nothing on TU2.** `blk.py`, `near.py` (`NEAR` up to 8) and `fscope.py` (with `FS_PAIRS`) left all five blockers unchanged: `0205e5c4` 2, `0205c234` 2, `0205e29c` 9, `02060a08` 13 and `02060b18` 16. `blk.py` finds no bare block next to a simple statement in the last three.
  - In `c234`, `t/c2gen.py` wrapped every contiguous run of the second set of stores in a bare block (760 variants, also with `start` in a nested block). The block never changes the code. Only the position of `start = data_02149efc.slotStart;` matters.
  - In `e5c4`, `t/e5gen.py` combined orders with `unk_14` before `unk_04`, the start of the `{ id ... }` block and an inner bare block (8616 variants). The best is 4, the round mainpool9 form (`res`, both stores, then `id`). `e5_g4.cpp` has the target's registers and store order but loads `id` after the stores.
- **A zero store to a global sinks or stays depending on its offset and the global's declared size.** Take `e5c4` with one store in place of the pair, written as `*(u32 *)((u8 *)&G + off) = 0`:
  - With `data_02149efc` (`ObjPoolGlobals`, 0x1c bytes), a store at `+0x10` or above (including offsets past the end, up to `+0x100`) is scheduled just after the two `slot` loads, with its address and zero.
  - A store below `+0x10` sinks, together with its address `ldr` and `mov #0`, to just before the `LightParam_Init` key store at `[sp, #0x10]`. That moves the registers (`id` goes to `sb`, and there is an extra push).
  - The threshold follows the size of the declared type, not the field types: a 4-byte type or a 0x1c-byte `u32[7]` struct keeps `+0x14` up, a 0x18-byte one sinks below `+0xc`, a 0x20-byte one below `+0x10`, and a `u32[16]` sinks up to `+0x2c`. `data_02fe1534` and `data_02149f18` sink at every offset tried.
  - The `slot` loads, the parameter struct's size, the field types, the base spelling (index, cast, member of `pool`) and the store's type (`u32`, `s32`, `StageRes **`) make no difference.

  So with the source order `unk_14`, `unk_04`, the `unk_04` store sinks (17). With `unk_04`, `unk_14`, the store order drags `unk_04` up with `unk_14` (2). Padding `ObjPoolGlobals` to sizes up to 0x504 bytes, or declaring it as `[1]` or `[]`, does not give the target's order (17 to 18). `__restrict` on `slot` lets the loads move above the stores, but it changes the whole schedule (20 to 33). An `unk_04 = unk_14` copy, `NULL`-returning inlines, setter inlines and local `o`/`l` copies all stay at 17.
- **`func_0205e29c` (9): the late `unk_14` store follows from the register swap.** In the target, the `Stage_FindObj3D` result (merged with the `unk_80` zero) is in `r3`, so its `str [r7, #0x14]` can sink to just before the `bl`. In ours it is in `r2`, which `and r2, r8, #0xff` overwrites, so the store has to come first. These all stay at 9 or worse:
  - redeclaring `data_ov000_021ccd64` with other types;
  - loading it into a local before the `unk_14` store (15, because this drops the inline's second `id == 0` test);
  - `Stage_FindLight1` and `u8` forms of the inline;
  - 72 type and declaration orders of `id`/`b`;
  - five spellings of the `GetArea` multiply.
- **`func_0205c234` (2).** The `ldr` of a constant address always lands one store before its load. These did not move it:

## Pointer locals plus array indexing for operand order (round bigsweep2)

- **The trick.** MWCC chose the wrong evaluation order for `FX_Atan2(a.x - b.x, a.z - b.z)` on two globals: it loaded the z term first. Writing the operands as indexes through block-local pointers gives the target's x-first order and its registers:
  ```c
  {
      const s32 *b = (const s32 *)&data_02092a38;
      const s32 *a = (const s32 *)&data_02092a50;
      self->rot[1] = FX_Atan2(b[0] - a[0], b[2] - a[2]);
  }
  ```
- **Both parts are needed.** Pointer locals with `->x` still scored 6. Casts with indexes but no locals also scored 6. Our working theory is that an offset-0 field access counts as cheaper when MWCC orders the operands, and the index form hides that.
- **Matches from this trick:**
  - `ov011_022038ac`
  - `ov011_02204428` (a long-standing 6-diff)
  - `ov011_02203ef0` (0x40c bytes)
- **Where it did not help:**
  - `ov000_0219d9fc`: the `0x9ac < 0x9ae` u16 compare kept its load order. We tried index, swapped, casts, temporaries and `!(<=)`.
  - `ov000_021ffb90`: 7 against 8, with a different shape.
- **Partial gains, not yet matches:**
  - `ov013_021fc7e0`, 9 → 6: move the `+0x3c = 0xb33` store after the `v14(0x800,0x800,0x800)` call.
  - `ov000_02171478`: `u32 index = (u32)i < LEN ? i : i - LEN;` gives the target's `mov; subhs`. An end/index register swap remains.
  - `ov000_0219e998`: assigning `ok = GIdle...()` gives the target's structure. Only an r0/r1 swap remains.
  - `ov000_021a2670`: inlining `(u16 >> 12) != 5` and placing `anm` right after `lock` fixes the 0xb24 register.
- **Scratch tools:**
  - `vrf.py`: applies variants inside one function; an `@TOP@` prefix applies the edit to the whole file.
  - `fsn.py`: applies all neutral `fscope` moves together.
  - `pipe.sh`: runs fsn, then blk, then blk again.

## Declaration-position grids, a product temporary, and main near-misses (round mainmid4)

- **`func_0203b12c` (now `src/Main/Gfx/GfxMgrText_2.cpp`).** It needed two changes.
  - The pixel offset is `bpp * pos`. With `db = (u16)bpp * db`, the destination is an operand, so the `mul` puts `db` first. Writing the product in both of its uses (`dst = buf + (((u16)bpp * pos) >> 3); db = ((u16)bpp * pos) & 7;`) keeps `bpp` first.
  - The callee-saved registers then rotated. Single scope moves did not fix this, and neither did pairs from `scope.py`. A grid over the declaration positions of two locals (`pos` and `b`, each at every top-level slot) found the order: `int pos;` first, and `u32 b;` after `u32 cur;`. If a pair search finds nothing, try every position of two variables, not just moves between block and function scope.
  - The function could not be appended to `GfxMgrText.cpp`, because that file's local `GfxNnsFont` prototypes conflict with `nnsys/g2d/g2d_Font.h`. So it went into a new file.
- **`func_0203c2bc` (4 diffs after register normalisation).** `sys` lands in r4 if any one of these statements is removed: `REG16(0x4000050)=0`, `func_02043904(...)`, the palette init, or some of the `REG32` writes. So the cause is register pressure, not the scope of a local. Moving `REG16(0x4000050)=0` earlier helps, but it reorders `volatile` writes, so it is not a valid fix.
- **`func_0206e858`.** Address constants are CSE'd across calls no matter how the code is written. These all failed: labels, blocks, constant conditions, inlines, `volatile` casts on the global, `static const` pointers and table forms. Putting the calls inside switch arms does give two loads of the same pool word, but the tail-merge shape is wrong.
- **`func_02015510`.** A fake `case 5` or `case 6` in `default` brings the switch pivot to `0x80`, leaving one diff: `cmp #5` or `cmp #6` where the target has `cmp #4`. No case set found so far gives an upper bound of 4.
- **Unchanged:**
  - `0206d43c` and `0206d99c`: these two share a pool. Over 240 variants of inline, manual expansion and declaration order were tried.
  - `0203d298`, `02049690`, `0203a984`, `0206f6d4`, `02064b54` and `0206e3a0`.
  - Permuter runs of an hour on `a984` and `9690` did not improve them.
- **Tools.** In `scratchpad/mainmid4/t/`:
  - `bo.sh func files...` scores many drafts in parallel, giving the raw and the register-normalised score.
  - `scope.py` now builds its pair stage from the best moves of both kinds: non-order moves and order moves (`SCOPE_ORD`, `SCOPE_DELTA`). Before, every pair conflicted. `SCOPE_NOORDER=1` turns order moves off.

## Sweeping the pointer-local index trick over every near-miss (round opsweep1)

No new matches this round. Drafts and tools are in `scratchpad/opsweep1/`.

- **The rewriter.** `t/rw.py draft func module outdir` finds field reads in one function: `g.x`, `p->x`, `g.arr[2].x`, and the `LFLD`/`FLD`/`FIELD` macros. It routes them through block-local pointers indexed by the field offset, then scores every variant and greedily combines the ones that help. The variants are:
  - per statement: all reads, each base alone, and pairs of bases;
  - windows of 2–3 adjacent sibling statements that share a base, with reads only or with writes too;
  - one pointer per global or parameter at function scope;
  - each with and without `const`.

  The generated text is written so that it needs no type information:
  ```c
  const __typeof__(g.x) *_pp0 = (const __typeof__(g.x) *)&g;
  ... _pp0[((u32)&(*(__typeof__(g) *)0).x) / sizeof(__typeof__(g.x))] ...
  ```
  Fields of another type reuse the same pointer through a cast, `((const __typeof__(g.z) *)_pp0)[...]`. The cast is a no-op and does not lose the effect. On the old `ov011_022038ac` draft the rewriter rebuilds bigsweep2's fix by itself (6 → 0). The computed-offset form and the `__typeof__` form both score 0, the same as the hand-written `b[0] - a[0]`. A pointer to the first field read (`&g.x`, then `[0]` and `[2]`) also works. One pointer per field (`&g.z`, then `[0]`) does not.
- **Result.** The sweep covered 52 drafts with ≤ 15 differences: `ovhi22`, `ovmid2/best`, `bigsweep2`, `mainmid3`, and the TU1/TU2 drafts in `mainpool12`/`mainpool13`. It compiled about 11,000 variants, of which about 1,900 failed to compile, mostly on bit-fields. Nothing reached a match.
  - Almost every variant left the score unchanged.
  - The only reduction (`ov010_021ffd0c`, 13 → 12) is a scoring artefact: the pointer is hoisted to the top of the function.
  - The remaining near-misses are register choice or store/pool-load scheduling, not the evaluation order of two reads.
  - The trick is specific to the operands of one binary expression (`a.x - b.x`) on globals.
- **What was checked by hand:**
  - `ov003_021d883c` (2). The target copies the default vector as `ldr x; ldr y; str x; str y; ldr z; str z`. This is the only such sequence in the ROM (`t/pat_ll.py` scans every ARM function).
    - An 8-byte struct copy through a pointer, `*(Ov003XY *)&v = *(const Ov003XY *)&p[2];` with `const s32 *p = (const s32 *)&g`, gives the paired loads and stores with the right registers. With that copy, `z` read through `p` is hoisted above the stores (2). Read as `g.v.z` it stays below them, but then the base register is `r2` instead of `r0` (6).
    - An `s64` copy loads the high word first.
    - 25 minutes of permuter on the `g.v.z` form found nothing.

## Unused parameters as locals fix a whole-function register rotation (ov000, round bigfresh2)

One new match: `func_ov000_021782e0` (0x77c bytes, menu builder), now `src/ov000/Lo_021782e0.cpp`. Drafts and tools are in `scratchpad/bigfresh2/` (`best/`, `t/`, `m/` for the small experiments).

- **The fix.** Start from the clean redraft (`82e0_clean_146_sdr0.cpp`: 146 raw, 0 masked, no two-definition tricks). Declare `g` (`data_02149ef8`) and the loop's `m` as parameters instead of locals: `void func_ov000_021782e0(VObj *self, void *g, VObj *m)`. The function still assigns both before use. `g` alone gives the target's whole prologue (`g` r4, `self` r5, `1` r6, `0` r7, vtable r8) and 18 raw diffs. What is left is an `id`/`m` swap in the loop, and `m` as a parameter fixes it (0). Turning any other local into a parameter changes nothing or makes it worse. Adding an unused parameter without moving a local into it also changes nothing.
- **Why it works.** These conclusions come from small test functions in `m/`. When the callee-saved registers are tight, MWCC assigns registers in this order:
  1. parameters, the last parameter first (it gets the lowest register);
  2. the hoisted constants, in reverse order of first use;
  3. long-lived locals, in declaration order.

  With few live values the order is simply reverse creation order. A local therefore never gets a lower register than a hoisted constant, whatever its name, initialiser or declaration position. That is why bigfresh1 could not move `g` out of r8. When the target puts a local-looking value (a loaded global) in r4, below the hoisted `1`/`0`, try making it a parameter.
- **Declaration order still matters between locals.** A long-lived local declared later is assigned later. On the 48-raw draft, a vtable-pointer local declared after `g` (with `g` declared first) moved the vtable to r8 (48 to 37). The parameter form made this unnecessary.
- **`func_ov000_02176714` (43 to 29 raw, 2 masked).** Making the loop's `tbl` a parameter fixes the `tbl`/`a` swap in the loop (`best/6714_29_sdr2_tblparam.cpp`). What is left is one r4/r6 swap across the whole function. The hoisted `1` is assigned before `-0x1ccd` and the loop's `base`; the target assigns `-0x1ccd`, `0`, `1` (reverse first use). A two-definition `0x130` in the loop gives exactly the target prologue (`-0x1ccd` r4, `0` r5, `1` r6), but only because it takes `1` out of the loop, and the frame shrinks (56). So the weight of `1`'s uses in the loop is what moves it ahead. These made no difference:
  - parameter, local, single-definition and two-definition forms of `-0x1ccd` and `1` (at one use and at all uses);
  - every pair and triple of locals as parameters;
  - a separate parameter for the object in each switch case;
  - a declaration grid over the loop block;
  - 15 minutes of two-definition annealing (`t/tdan.py`).
- **`func_ov010_02201064` (190 to 176 raw, 6 masked).** Making the block-local `all` a parameter gives the 14. The fresh `mov r1, #0` for the `last` stores is still missing. A two-definition zero after `func_02040528(2)` (`s32`/`int`/`u16`/`u8`, used for the three stores and/or the `0x7a` store and the call) merges with the hoisted r5 zero. The other attempts (inline helpers with a zero parameter, a parameter zero) changed nothing or made it worse.
- **Tools** (in `scratchpad/bigfresh2/t/`):
  - `pparam2.py src func outdir K [force]` writes every subset of up to K locals turned into parameters. It also handles initialised declarations.
  - `bo.sh func mod files...` gives the raw score and our prologue for many files in parallel.
  - `fam.py log` groups a `tdc` log by the registers of `g`/`self`/`1`/`0`/vtable.
  - `tdc.py` now prints our prologue after `##` and has these options:
    - `TDRX=<regex>` for non-numeric operands such as `g` or a vtable symbol;
    - `TDPARAM=1` makes the two-definition variable a parameter;
    - `TDSINGLE=1` gives it a single definition.
  - `td2j.py` specs take `LIT:N:NEAR:TYPE:SKIP`.
  - `tdan.py` anneals over sets of two-definition replacements.
  - `near2.py` and `tmpify.py` move statements and wrap a statement's `self` field base in a pointer local, both printing our prologue.
  - `m/m.sh` prints our code for a small test file that defines the target function's name.

## Inline-local stack order and mid-block initialised declarations (main, round mainfresh3)

- **`0206bab8` matched (310 / 163 to 0, `Effect_16.cpp`).** The particle-emit function had a wrong stack layout and the wrong order of its zero stores. These changes fixed it:
  - **Locals of an inlined function are placed after all of the caller's locals, so they get lower addresses.** The target's rotation matrices sit below the caller's vectors. Moving the rotation code into inlines that each own their `EffectMtx43 tmp` (`Effect_MtxRotXZ` and `Effect_MtxRotYXZ`) gave the target's frame. Inside `Effect_MtxRotYXZ` the order of the declarations (`tmp, ry, rx, rz, rotated`) also matters.
  - **A C++ declaration with an aggregate initialiser between statements** (`EffectVec c = {0,0,0};` after `p->origin = em->pos;`) emits its zero stores at that point. At function scope the stores move to the function entry.
  - **An inline that takes `const s32 &base`** (`Effect_RandScale`) loads `base` after the `rand` call in its body, as the target does. Taking `base` by value loads it before the call.
  - Some forms had to match the target exactly:
    - Use the existing `EffectPtcl_SetCmds` inline, not open-coded stores (it gives load-load-store-store).
    - Write `v.x`, `v.y = 0`, `v.z` in that order, with no radius local.
    - Write `out.x = c.x + rand(...)` (forward the zero vector).
    - The angle comes from `func_02040498`, not `func_02040528`.
  - The remaining `bl`/`blx` differences on the Thumb `MTX_*` calls are interworking, as in the already-matched `0206b81c`.
- **`02069b3c` (66 / 21 to 44 / 4, scratch `d/9b3c_44.cpp`).** The target only partly tail-merges the arms. Writing `p->unk_50 = idx;` in each arm, with a block-local `s32 i` in the second arm, merges only the `0x50` store, as the target does. Writing the palette address as `((u16)p->tex->plttVramKey + pltt[0]) << 3` loads the key before `pltt[0]`. One register swap is left: the target keeps param + key in `r3`, the register `data[0]` was loaded into, and ours uses `r1`.
- **`02053254` (95 / 60 to 79 / 20, `d/3254_79.cpp`; the permuter's version `d/3254_p84.c` is at 84 / 18).** Changes that helped:
  - In the else arm, write the direction flag as nested ifs: `if (mode == 0x1000) { if (flip == 1) dir = -1; } else { if (flip == 0) dir = -1; }`.
  - Statement order in the else arm is `sy`, `sx = FxMul(...) & ~0xfff`, `sz`.
  - The permuter read `scene->unk_b8_0` into a local before `if (b == 0)`.
  
  The remaining problem: our build hoists the `~0xfff` mask to the function entry, and the target rebuilds it in each block.
- **No change on the register-only near-misses:** `02068e68`, `02056e74`, `0204205c`, `020417e0` and `02056230`. Tried with the declaration grid, the between-statements grid, `tdv2`, typed constants, index and pointer forms, and split loop indices.
## Sweeping locals-as-parameters over the register-only near misses (round bigfresh3)

Four new matches, all found by turning one or two locals into extra parameters that the function assigns before use (`scratchpad/bigfresh3/t/pp3.py`, then a plain raw-score sort):

| Function | Before (raw/masked) | Change |
|---|---|---|
| `func_ov011_021fb9b8` | 12/0 | `owner` (the list's actor) as a parameter. Appended to `src/ov011/ov011_021fb66c.cpp`. |
| `func_ov002_021dd9dc` | 28/0 | `w` and `obj` as parameters, together. Either one alone makes it worse (`w` 50, `obj` 66). New file `src/ov002/ov002_021dd9dc.cpp` (keeps the draft's file-wide `#pragma opt_loop_invariants off`). |
| `func_02051a34` | 35/0 | `fn` (the font's split-char function pointer) as a parameter. New file `src/Main/Gfx/SlideWin_2.cpp`. |
| `func_02056230` | 42/0 | The panel loop index `i` as a parameter. New file `src/Main/Sys/SlideDrawScene.cpp`, plus the symbol `data_020829c8` (a `u16[3]` colour table that the function copies), which was missing from `symbols.txt`. |

- **When the lever fires.** In all four, the swap was between a long-lived local and another value: a hoisted constant, an inline's local or a second long-lived local. In each case one of the two locals needed a lower register than its declaration order gave it. Making it a parameter moved it ahead. In `021fb9b8` this swaps `head`/`owner` (r8/sb). None of the four needed a second change.
- **It is not a rule that parameters get the lowest registers.** In `func_ov002_021d1f70`, making `x` a parameter moved it from r4 up to sb. In `func_ov000_021688c4`, the extra `a5` parameter went to r4 and shifted everything else up. So treat the lever as a search dimension: try every local and every pair, and also both parameter orders for a pair (`PERM=1`).
- **Landing.** When a header or the same file declares the function with the old signature, C++ `extern "C"` refuses the overload. For scoring, `pp3.py` (`HDR=1`) wraps the old declarations in `#define f f_hdr` / `#undef f`. For landing, put the function in its own translation unit, which is what all four did. Callers in other files keep their old prototype. The extra parameter is never read before it is written, so the call site does not change.
- **No effect** (every single local and every pair as parameters, 0 gain):
  - `ov000_021c3158` (4), `021688c4` (20), `0214dd3c` (49), `021dfcc0` (29, both orders), `021d1f70` (28);
  - `func_02056e74` (4; the diff is the scratch register of a 64-bit multiply, and seven multiply spellings change nothing);
  - `func_0204205c` (8; scratch registers again), `func_02068e68` (26), `func_020417e0` (24).
  
  These are not callee-saved rotations, or not ones a parameter reaches. In `021c3158`, sharing `res` between the two blocks, a `name`/`res` reuse, and inline-parameter forms of the model constructor also changed nothing.
- **Partial:** `func_ov002_021e7ea8` 34 to 28 with `gx` and `ret` as parameters (`bigfresh3/d/e7ea8/gxret.cpp`).
- **Tools** (`scratchpad/bigfresh3/t/`):
  - `pp3.py src func outdir K` works for any return type. It renames block-scoped duplicate locals (`a_0`, `a_1`) so that each can be chosen separately, and takes `HDR=1` and `PERM=1` (see above).
  - `ppd.sh` / `ppdx.sh` drive it and score with `sc.sh` (raw score, parallel).
  - `scan.sh func mod` scores the newest scratchpad drafts of a function to find the best one.

## One-element array sweep over every near-miss (all modules, round arrsweep1)

This round ran `pairarr.py`/`pa_iter.sh` on the best draft of every unmatched function whose register-masked score is 4 or less: 55 functions, from 1 to 146 raw diffs. It then ran `pairarr.py` with `PA_IN` inside each `static inline` the function uses (39 functions, about 140 inlines), and ran it again on a second draft for 8 functions. No function went into the build. Drafts are in the scratchpad under `arrsweep1/` (`w/`, `w3/` and `wi/<func>/<inline>/`, plus `x/` for hand work).

- **The lever helps on big rotations, not on 1 or 2 stray registers.** Every function at 2 to 6 raw diffs stayed where it was, inline arrays included. The hits were all in functions where a whole callee-saved rotation was wrong:
  - `func_ov006_021cec68` went from 38 to 12 with `void *res[1]` (the message resource), then to 1 with `u8 n[1]`. That draft still has the old uninitialised `kq` trick (`g + kq`, where `kq` is set only on the early-return path). It is not valid code, and it leaves `add r0, r4, r6` against `#0x8b0`. Without the trick the draft is at 7 / 0 (`arrsweep1/x/cec/plain.cpp`). Only a g/res swap between `r4` and `r5` is left. Pairs, mixed `u8 *gr[2]`, an inline and block moves did not fix it. The function is still blocked by the ov006 string pool.
  - `func_ov000_02176714` went from 43 to 29 / 2 with `tbl[1]` (`w/func_ov000_02176714/base.cpp.it1.cpp`). The clean draft went from 68 to 56 / 2 (`w3/.../base.cpp.it1.cpp`).
  - `func_0206e858` went from 5 / 0 to 0 / 0 with `LangState *st[1]` (`w3/func_0206e858/base.cpp.it1.cpp`).
- **A 0 from `sd.py`/`sc.py` is not a match.** These scripts mask `[pc, #...]`, so they hide an extra literal-pool word. Check every 0 with `tools/match.py`. `func_0206e858` at 0 still differs in one pool offset. The target loads one pool word (`data_0214b105`) for both `func_0206e900` calls. The draft names `data_0214b104.name` once and `data_0214b105` once, which gives two pool words. The object is 4 bytes too big, and every module then failed the ROM check. If both calls name the same address, in any spelling, MWCC keeps the address in `r5` (11 diffs). These forms also failed: a two-iteration loop, a helper inline, `#pragma opt_common_subs off`, and `u32` casts of the address.
- **No change from the lever (best draft, raw / masked):** `021e51f8` (2 / 0; the `mov #1` for `Ov006_Begin` is in `r0`, but the target has `r1`), `0206e3a0`, `0217a1f8`, `0218a5ec`, `021e2690`, `021ec010`, `02211b2c`, `021be5dc` (3 / 0; an FX temporary in `CalcDepth`), `0219d9fc`, `021d883c`, `021e8ef8`, `02189b44`, `021fb02c`, `0220640c`, `021fc688`, `0203d298`, `021c4460`, `02199180`, `021708ec`, `02171478`, `021fc0b8`, `0206f6d4`, `021e1204`, `02056e74`, `020508f4`, `0204205c`, `0203a984`, `0206d43c`, `02060a08`, `021d3e14`, `0219e998`, `021fb1b4`, `02051a34`, `0206d99c`, `02056230`, `021782e0`, `0204f5bc`, `02068e68`, `0204f524`, `0205c234`, `0205e5c4`, `021fff38`, `0205e29c`, `021d36fc`, `021afaf8`, `021e6274`, `021fce2c`, `021cf420`, `02064b54`, `021d4118` and `0203c2bc`. `021ffb90` went from 8 to 7 / 4 with the `q` parameter of `Ov015_Ang` copied into an array. `02060b18` went from 16 / 0 to 15 / 4, which is a worse result.
- **Tools** (scratchpad `arrsweep1/t/`):
  - `pairarr.py` now scores each variant with one compile (`sc.py`).
  - `pa_iter.sh` keeps a `.c` draft as `.c`.
  - `drive.sh list` runs `pa_iter.sh` over a list of `path func module` lines.

## Clean redrafts of small near-misses, and a dead store that orders hoisted constants (round nearfresh1)

- **New match: `func_ov002_021e2690`** (2 raw diffs before).
  - The redraft uses the sibling `Caption` struct layout (see `ov002_021e0c28.cpp`), with `tx`/`ty` block locals and the stores in the target's order (`mode`, then `timer`).
  - The last 2 diffs were the registers of two constants hoisted out of the loop (8 and 3).
  - MWCC gives loop-hoisted constants registers in the order of their first use in IR. A dead store that comes first, `c->timer = 8; c->mode = 3; c->timer = 8;`, gives 8 the earlier register. The target's store order stays the same, because the dead store is removed.
- **A new local can replace the comma hack.** `lx = x + 0x4c` stops the `(x+0x4c)-0x80 → x-0x34` fold just as `x = (0, x + 0x4c)` does (`ov000_0217e560`).

## Two-definition constants and a hand-rotated loop (main, round mainfresh4)

- **`020572f8` (605 / 203 to 6 / 6, scratch draft only).** The function sits in the `main_84` gap with `02056e74`, so it was not placed. The changes that helped, in order of size:
  - **Keep VRAM bases out of constant propagation.** The target selects between registers (`mov r10, r11; movne r10, r5`), not between immediates. Writing each base twice, `v4 = 0x6400000; if ((u32)win & 3) v4 = 0x6400000;`, keeps it in a register. Pass `v4` and `v6` into the helper inlines as parameters.
  - **Rotate the loop by hand.** `if ((c = fn(&win->str)) != 0) { setup; do { ... } while ((c = fn(&win->str)) != 0); }` puts the setup (here the two VRAM bases) in the preheader, after the first test, as the target does.
  - **Turn an unused parameter into the local that needs the low register.** The second parameter (`void *p` in the caller) became `SlideMsg *msg`. The body still assigns `msg = win->msgs;`. This fixed a whole-function register rotation.
  - **Merge the early returns into one `if (a || b || ...) return 0;`.** Separate `if`s give separate return blocks.
  - **Statement and declaration order inside blocks.** Stores through `msg` (a known offset from `win`) can be reordered by the scheduler. The order of the source statements inside each block still decides most of the schedule.
  - The last three diffs did not move:
    - two prologue stores to the same zero, swapped
    - one store scheduled across an address computation
    - two pool loads swapped
  - I tried every position of the `stop`/`nameChanged` initialisers, chained assignments and type swaps.
- **`02043100` (158 / 91 to 141 / 78, the `NONMATCHING` draft in `Gfx3D.cpp` is updated).** Changes that helped:
  - Declare `trans[3]` and `scale[3]` at function scope.
  - Assign `shape`, `name` and `ox` as statements, not as initialisers.
  - Flatten the nested inlines. The nesting depth of inline locals changes the stack slots.
  - Read the OAM attributes through a bitfield struct (`GfxOamBits`).
  - The permuter found nothing better (40 min).
- **`02053254` (79 / 20 to 76 / 16).** Writing the `y` mask with the same two-definition form helped (`kq = 0xfff; if ((u32)scene & 3) kq = 0xfff; y &= ~kq;`). Using it for `x` as well gives 74 / 20. Most of the `~0xfff` masks are still hoisted to the function entry.
- **`02069b3c`:** no change from 44 / 4.
## A string literal in a local, and merging a string-pool file (overlays, round ovmid3)

- **New matches: `func_ov006_021d5b98` and `func_ov006_021d5e68`** (a destructor and its deleting form, 0x2d0 and 0x2d8 bytes, both 2 raw diffs before). They are now in `src/ov006/ov006_021d5b98.cpp`, together with the already-matched `021d6140`, `021d630c` and `021d6724`, because all five load strings from one pool (`0x021ebfe0..0x021ec034`). The old three files are deleted, and `strrefs.py --claim` rewrote the pool.
  - The last 2 diffs were the order of the two loads before a `func_02036838(data_02097cdc, "ef/effect3darc", 7, 0)` call. The target loads the string address before `data_02097cdc`. Passing the literal through a block local gives the target's order: `{ const char *s = "ef/effect3darc"; func_02036838(data_02097cdc, s, 7, 0); }`. The next call (`"ef/effect3dtri"`) is written directly and loads in the opposite order, as the target does. With `extern` string arrays the same local trick still gives 2 diffs, so the literal is needed, and with it the pool merge.
  - When a pool merge turns a matched `extern` string into a literal, check for null tests that only existed for the `extern`. `021d6724` had `const char *name = data_...; if (name) { ... }`. MWCC folds the test for an array address but not for a literal, so the merged file emits a `cmp`. Keep the local and drop the `if`: `const char *name = "cefly1pic00";` followed by the three calls.
  - When the merged files declare the same global with different types (`data_ov000_021ccd54` as `u8 *` and as a struct pointer), declare it once and cast at the uses. The cast does not change the code.
- **Finding these:** `strrefs.py <mod> <func>` on every near-miss shows which ones load strings. A draft that is 2 or 3 diffs off only around string loads is a candidate for literals. Check that every function sharing the pool is matched (or in your file) before merging.
- **`func_ov000_0218e12c` (16 / 3 to 28 / 0, structure only).** The draft hand-inlined the manager teardown. The matched sibling file `ActorMgr_0218e0f0.cpp` already has `ActorMgr_Delete`, `ActorMgr_RemoveGroup` and `ActorGroup_Delete`. Using them, `if (data_ov000_021ccd68 != NULL) { ActorMgr *mgr = data_ov000_021ccd68; if (mgr != NULL) ActorMgr_Delete(mgr); data_ov000_021ccd68 = NULL; }`, gives the target's instructions (the separate `ldr`s instead of an `ldm`, and the branch layout). Turning `saved` into a parameter fixes `mgr`. What is left is a reversed allocation: the target gives the innermost inline's locals (`ActorGroup_Remove`'s `prev`/`next`) `r4`/`r5`, and `saved` gets `r8`. Ours runs outer to inner. Neither local inline copies with other declaration orders nor `pairarr` inside each inline nor `inline_bottom_up`/`inline_depth` changed it. The draft is `scratchpad/ovmid3/best/e12c_28_0_clean.cpp`. It belongs at the end of `ActorMgr_0218e0f0.cpp` (it fills the gap up to `0218e234`).
- **No change** from locals-as-parameters (`pp3.py`, K=2, both orders), the one-element array sweep (`pairarr.py`), the dead-store sweep (`dup.py`) or the two-definition sweep (`td1.py`) on these:
  - Leftovers: `0217a1f8` (2), `0218a5ec` (2), `021ec010` (2), `0217e560` (6/6), `021e0b80` (8/7; 420 more statement orders with separate `w`/`h` locals) and `021d36fc` (20/2).

## Spill order by type, a scale local before calls, and cached OAM words (main, round mainfresh5)

- **`020572f8` (still 6 / 6, scratch draft only).** Spill stores in the prologue follow the type of the local: a narrower local is stored first. Within one type class, `nameChanged` is always stored first. Changing types fixes the order of the two zero stores, but MWCC then stops if-converting `case 36`. Net result: no gain.
- **`02053254` (76 / 16 to 36 raw).** Two changes helped:
  - Assign a function-scope `scale = dir << 12;` before the `SetPos`/`func_ov000_02190758` calls. This stops MWCC from sinking the shift past the `bl`.
  - Use one two-definition mask `kq = ~0xfff; if ((u32)scene & 3) kq = ~0xfff;` for both `x &= kq` and `y &= kq`. The mask is then materialised in the tail block, not at function entry.
  - After those two changes, a hill-climb over locals-as-parameters, one-element arrays and the declaration grid did the rest.
  - The diffs left are register colouring in the middle block and the order of the `0x78`/`0x7c` store tail.
- **`02024730` (`NNS_G2dMakeCellToOams`, new draft, 85 raw).** Changes that helped:
  - **Give the shape mask a signed type.** The target uses `asr` for the `(shape & 0xc000) >> 14` index and `lsr` for the `0xc0000000` part. Declare the shape as `s32`, as an `int` enum would be.
  - **Read `attr01` once.** Load it into a local and pass the value to the `G2_GetOBJEffect` inline. The target reuses that load for the shape mask. Reading through the pointer twice reloads it.
  - **Write `G2_SetOBJEffect` as `if (effect != 0x100 && effect != 0x300) plain; else with rsParam;`.** This matches the branch layout.
  - **Open issue: the frame is `0x18`, not `0x20`.** In the target, `_01` and `_11` are spilled and the centre correction is written as `-hw*4096 + _00*hw + _10*hh`. That expression form gives the right `rsb`/`mla` chain. It also makes MWCC spill `isDouble` instead of the loop counter, which costs 143 against 85 for the other form.
## Widening the locals-as-parameters sweep, plus inline arguments and statement units (round parsweep2)

For each argument of a `static inline` call that is not a plain name or constant, a variant assigns that argument to a new parameter (or local) on the line before the call, then passes the variable. A unit is one statement, or one compound statement such as an `if`/`else` chain, a loop or a block. The tool writes every permutation of every window of 2 and 3 sibling units. It is not semantics-preserving, so check each hit by hand. It found the `afaf8` fix. ## An unused register parameter as a spilled local, a pragma swap, and a two-definition scale constant (overlays, round ovmid5)

Three new matches:

| Function | Before (raw/masked) | Change |
|---|---|---|
| `func_ov000_02160534` (0x4b8) | 17/17 | New file `src/ov000/ov000_02160534.cpp`. |
| `func_ov002_021d98ac` (0x358) | 43/36 | New file `src/ov002/ov002_021d98ac.cpp`. |
| `func_ov000_02191c24` (0x2a0) | 4/4 | Appended to `src/ov000/Shadow_0219196c.cpp`. |

- **Use an unused register parameter for a local that spills (`02160534`).** The only diffs were the stack slots of two spills: `pid` and the 64-bit copy of `d`. The target has `pid` at the lower slot. Declaration order, statement order, types, one-element arrays and trailing stack parameters did not change the slots. A trailing parameter is spilled to its own home slot, which gives a different frame. The second argument `a` (in `r1`) is never read, so the fix was to rename it `pid` and assign it in the body. A parameter's virtual register is created before every local, which gives it the target's slot order. When a function has an unused `r0` to `r3` parameter, try each local in it before adding trailing parameters.
- **`match.py` does not compare `bl` targets.** With 0 diffs in `match.py`, the ROM check still failed for `02160534`. The draft called `_ffltu` (from `(float)(u32)`), and the target calls `_fflt`. Casting the operand to `s32` fixed it. When the check fails after a 0, compare the bytes (`cmp -l extract/usa/arm9_overlays/ovNNN.bin build/usa/build/arm9_ovNNN.bin`) and read the target's call names with `t/asm.sh`.
- **`#pragma opt_loop_invariants off`, not `optimization_level 2` (`021d98ac`).** Level 2 stops the sin/cos table loads from being hoisted, but it also turns off the tail merge of the three `MTX_RotY33_` calls in the `SetRot` switch. `opt_loop_invariants off` keeps the merge (43 to 22).
- **Read two bitfields of one halfword into locals before both stores (`021d98ac`).** `s32 x = m->bits.x; s32 z = m->bits.z; n->a = x; n->b = z;` loads the halfword once and extracts both fields before the stores, as the target does. Writing the fields straight into the stores loads the halfword twice. A struct copy (`Size98ac sz = ...`) goes through the stack. Hand-written shifts on a loaded `u16` get the order wrong. With `u8` locals the code is worse. `s32`, `u32` and `u16` all match. The only diff left in `match.py` is the `bl`/`blx` to the Thumb `MTX_RotY33_`, which the linker fixes.
- **A two-definition constant for one store of a vector (`02191c24`).** The target loads `unk_14` into `r1` and the constant `0x1000` into `r2`. Every store order, a dead first store, the `SetScaleXZ`/`VEC_Set` inlines, a block local, `u32` and one-element arrays all gave the reverse (5/0) or worse. `s32 one = 0x1000; if ((u32)self & 3) one = 0x1000;`, used only for `scale.y`, matches.
- **No change:**
  - `0218e12c` (17/0): every subset and order of up to three of its locals as parameters (139 variants), and block-scoped `group`, `gprev`/`gnext` and `aprev`/`anext`.
  - `0218867c` (22/6): all 24 orders of `kind`/`arg`/`one`/`done`, and `arg`, `done` or `one` as a parameter in each position.
  - `0219badc` (5/4): an `|= 0x40` store, and an inline or split `if` for the event-table tail (`strne` before `popeq` in the target).
  - `0218a670` (12/6): every order of the case 20 to 22 statements, `code++`, `pairarr` and `dup`.
  - `021512b4` (35/3): a widget-draw inline for the six `+0x70` store / `vfunc_20` / `vfunc_90` triples, the unused `a` as `x`/`y`/`h`, and a constant local. The first `x` is still folded into the add, and the target keeps it in `r5`.

## Bitfield stores as a register lever, and string-pool blockers redrafted (round poolfresh1)

Drafts are in `scratchpad/poolfresh1/` (`best/`, `d/<func>/`). Scores are raw / register-masked seqdiff.

- **New match: `func_ov006_021cec68`** (0x6e8 bytes, the network menu task's init), now `src/ov006/ov006_021cec68.cpp` with its own `.text` range `0x021cec68..0x021cf350`. Its two strings are `extern` arrays, so it lands without the ov006 pool (which still needs `021cf420` and `021d4118`). The fix is one statement. The draft had `g[0x8b0] |= 0x30;` on the byte at `data_02097d48 + 0x8b0`; writing it as two one-bit bitfield stores matched it (7 to 0):

  ```c
  ((ov006_Bits8b0 *)(g + 0x8b0))->b4 = 1;
  ((ov006_Bits8b0 *)(g + 0x8b0))->b5 = 1;
  ```

  MWCC merges the two read-modify-writes into the same `ldrb; orr #0x30; strb`, so the instructions do not change. The register allocation does: `g` moves to `r4` and the hoisted `&data_ov006_021ec884` to `r5`, as in the target. Matched code in ov002 (`021ccda0`, `021e779c`) already writes this byte as bitfields. `n` and `res` stay parameters (the parsweep lever).
- **Try it on other register-only near misses.** If a draft ORs or clears several bits of one field at once and only registers differ, write the bits as separate bitfield stores, and the reverse. It did nothing on `ov006_021cf420` (`flags |= 6` as `f.b1`/`f.b2`) or `02060a08` (the packed slot word as a bitfield or `u8` struct is 42).
- **`func_ov003_021e6274`: 45 to 9 without hacks** (`best/e6274_9_u16c.cpp`, no `(u32)self & 3`). In case 2, read the slot into a separate `u16 c` and keep `n` for the decremented value:

  ```c
  c = self->unk_18;
  if (c == self->unk_93_1 || c == 0) return;
  func_ov000_02197dec(self, c, -1);
  self->unk_93_1 = c;
  n = c - 1;
  ```

  The `self`/`t` swap through the whole function is gone, and `n` takes `r5` with the bitfield value in `ip`, as in the target. What is left is one extra `and r1, r5, #0xff`, because a `u16` (or `s32`/`u32`) `c` is converted to the `u8` bit-field type. With `u8 c` the `and` goes, but the store's value computation is sunk past `n = c - 1`, `n` gets a new register and `self`/`t` rotate again (46). Every `u8 c` form tried stays at 46: 30 declaration orders, block scope, manual read-modify-write of the byte, a separate index variable, a `PlayAnim(self, idx)` inline (40 variants), other container types for the bit-field.
- **No change:**
  - `ov003_021e1204` (2). About 700 variants: `k` types and declaration orders, `switch`, `Kind` inlines on the entry or the value, a dispatch inline, a variable reused for `unk_06` and the kind, a `lo:12, kind:4` bitfield view (3), `goto`. The load of `unk_16` always takes `r0`; the target puts it in `r1` (the dead entry pointer).
  - `ov006_021cf420`. Without the two-definition `kq`, case 5's tail merges into case 4's (60). An inline with a state parameter, a local `st`, and the case-4 locals as parameters (80 sets) change nothing; `state + 2` breaks the merge but costs 32.
  - `0204f524` / `0204f5bc`. The natural form (`win->numBlocks = 0;` and a constant ternary, no two-definition `a`/`c`) gives the target's instructions with a rotation (12: `i` `r7`, `0x6600000` `r5`). Parameters for `i`, `a` or `c` do not move it.
  - `02060a08` (10 / 0): all 54 orders and groupings of the four OR terms.

  1. `pp3.py` with `K=2`, `PERM=1` and `HDR=1`: every one or two locals as trailing parameters, in every order.
  2. `pperm.py src func nkeep out` on the best result: every order of the added parameters, and every order with one more top-level local added. In `021ddf18` and `021cfa38` this step went from 32 or 20 to 0. In `ov002_021dedf0` it went from 9 to 5.
  3. `sib.py` (statement-unit permutations, W=3) on that best result, then check each hit by hand.

  Earlier rounds ran step 1 without `PERM` (new parameters only in one order) and never ran step 2. They also picked candidates by masked score ≤ 10, so drafts like `021e5974` (12 / 0) and `021cfa38` (89 / 0) were never swept in their current form. Run the chain on every draft whose masked score is 0, whatever the raw score.

With the mask written before the loop, its longer dependence chain is scheduled first in the block. What matches is a plain `s32 y = m->0x100;` (placed with the `x` load, above the clamp) and `oam[n].y = (u16)y & 0x1ff;` in the loop: LICM hoists the mask to the end of the preheader.

Writing `o = new ...; self->0x3c = o; o->vfunc_10(b);` at the end of each arm, not once after the `if`, gives the target's whole branch layout (70 / 0 to 58 / 0). Putting all the setup code that follows into each arm is too much (108).

Passing `g` as a parameter, and reordering the `func_0205976c`/`func_0205975c` locals, gets to 121. The target colours 1→r4, 0→r5, o→r6, g→r7. We put `g` in sb (as a parameter) or r4 (as a local). Declaration permutations and greedy found nothing better. |
| `func_ov000_02191f18` | 220 / 130 | 393 / 78 (`d/1f18/best_393_78m.cpp`) | Each of cases 8–13 writes the scale out in full: `h = m->unk_cc; sc = (s16)m->unk_ce; k = FALSE; if (h < 0) h = 0x64; if (sc != 0 && sc != 0x1000) k = TRUE; c = p[N]; if (k) c = ...;`. This gives the target's materialised flag. Raw is worse because we hoist 0, 0x1000 and 1, and the target hoists only 1. Keep `a0.cpp` (220 raw) as the raw base. |
| `func_ov008_021ce518` | 1 / 1 | 1 / 1 | The only diff is the switch root, `cmp #0x15` against `#0x14`. Dummy cases 18 or 19 mapped to default move the root to 0x14 but leave a dead `cmp #0x13`. Not solved. |

- **Constant hoisting threshold, micro-tested (`bigfresh7/x/`).** MWCC hoists a constant into a callee-saved register at function entry when it has **5 or more register uses**; 4 uses are not hoisted. Compare-immediate uses do not count. The threshold does not change with:
  - the literal's form: `0`, `0L`, `0u`, `(u16)0`, `static const`, `enum`, or `FX32_CONST`;
  - the parameter type (s16, u16 or u32);
  - wrapping the use in an inline.

  Zero stores inside a loop, together with other zero stores, also push the zero to entry. Under high register pressure only some constants are hoisted. When the target keeps a constant local and we hoist it (1f18, 8fc0), the fix is to have fewer uses, not to write the literal differently.
- **Materialised bool (`mov rX,#0 ... movne rX,#1; cmp rX,#0`).** Two forms produce it:
  - `BOOL k = 0;` and `if (cond) k = 1;` with other statements between them, and the `k` test after a load;
  - `r = 0; if (a) { r = b != NULL; }` inside an inline.

  A plain `k = FALSE; if (a && b) k = TRUE;` is jump-threaded away, or comes out as `movne`/`moveq`.
- **A `const T *self` inline parameter keeps a bitfield byte reload.** With it, `if (!self->active) return; if (!IsValid(self)) return;` stay as two loads. With a non-const pointer, the second load is CSE'd.
- Passing a struct by value to an inline, or returning one, makes a stack temporary. Use `const &` to avoid the copy.

The target loads `t` before the first call. What is left is `g` in `sb` (target `r7`), plus the order of `mov r0, rT` / `mov r1, #0x1a` before `func_ov000_02154b58`. Writing it with a `u16` id variable, a `?:`, an inline or a cast on the literal does not change that order. |

The rest came from cxxperm, mostly locals turned into trailing parameters. That result is too noisy to land as it is. |
| `func_ov000_021652e4` | 333 | 258 (`d/52e4/perm/out-258-*.cpp`) | cxxperm only. Spill slots are the main difference: the target's order from `sp` up is `i`, `tbl`, `y0`, `x0`, `row`, then the template copy. Reordering the declarations changes almost nothing (328). |
| `func_ov003_021d8fc0` | 610 | 488 (`d/8fc0/perm/out-488-*.cpp`) | cxxperm on bigfresh7's `b3.cpp`, 13,000 compiles. The struct-copy count is unchanged. |

How MWCC lowers a sparse `switch` (worked out with one-line test files; superseded by round swtree, which reads the rules from the compiler and explains the `{16,20}` cluster below as the x87-precision case):

- **3 or fewer cases** become a linear `cmp`/`beq` chain. **4 or more** become a binary tree. A node is the sorted case at index `(n-1)/2` and is emitted as `cmp k; bgt right; bge k_body; left...`.
- **Cases close together form a cluster** when `hi - lo + 1 <= 2 * count`, for example `{30,31}`, `{30,33}` or `{16,18,20}`, but not `{30,34}` or `{16,20}`. A cluster is one node: `cmp hi; bgt right; cmp lo; blt left; beq lo_body; cmp v; beq ...` for each other member, in ascending order.
- **Cases that go to `default`** stay in the tree and keep their compares. The only exception is the last compare of a chain (`beq D; b D` becomes `b D`). That is how `case 21: default:` in `ce518` gives the cluster `{16,20,21}` with root `cmp #0x15` and no compare for 21.
- The target's `cmp #0x14; bgt; cmp #0x10; blt; beq; cmp #0x14; beq` is a cluster `{16,20}` with nothing between them. Under these rules that cannot happen without a dead compare inside the chain. These all fail: dummy cases 0–45 (alone, sharing each real body, or as an empty `case X: break;`), pairs of dummies from -100 to 1000, every source order of the case blocks, case ranges (MWCC has no `case a ... b`), and the pragmas `optimize_for_size`, `optimization_level 1-4`, `switch_tables`, `opt_*` and `peephole`. Dense sets such as 16–20 become a jump table.

- **The combined lever (`scratchpad/ovmid8/t/ppa.sh src func mod tag`).** `pp3.py` with K=1 makes each local a trailing parameter in turn. Then `pairarr.py` with `PA_ONE=1` runs on the base and on each result: every local becomes `T x[1]`, and every parameter is copied into a one-element array. Each result is scored. On the ovmid7 base of `021e0280` (20 / 0) it finds the match in about 25 seconds. Neither lever alone matched: ovmid7's K=2 parameter sweep stopped at 7, and the ovfresh2 array sweep had never been run after the parameter step. `K=2` sweeps pairs of parameters first, which is much slower.

When the file you merge into already declares the symbol with another type, put the `const` declaration in a namespace, `namespace Ov010T6974 { extern "C" void *const data_ov010_0220f024[]; }`, and use `(const char *)Ov010T6974::data_ov010_0220f024[i]`. `extern "C"` makes it the same symbol.

## A size-guarded fill splits the slot address across a call (overlays, round ovmid9)

One new match. Scores are raw / register-masked seqdiff.

| Function | Before | Change |
|---|---|---|
| `func_ov006_021dacb0` (0x184, `SlotManager` create) | 24 / 7 | The inlined slot clear writes the name fill as `{ u32 n = sizeof(self->name); if (n != 0) { MI_CpuFill8(self->name, 0, n); } }`. The one-element `i_1[1]` counter from ovmid8 is no longer needed. New file `src/ov006/ov006_021dacb0.cpp`, with a local copy of the inline (`ov006_Slot_ClearGuarded`). |

- **What the guard changes.** In the target, the slot loop keeps only the offset `i * 0x4c` in a callee-saved register. It computes `p + off` once for the stores before the `MI_CpuFill8` call and again for the stores after it. With a plain call, MWCC CSEs `p + off` across the call and keeps the slot pointer in the callee-saved register instead. The `if` puts a block boundary around the call, so the two address computations stay separate. Every other form changed nothing: `p->slots[i].field` written out, a re-taken `&p->slots[i]` after the call, the sub-struct clears as separate inlines, a `goto` label after the call. `if (sizeof(...) != 0)` (a constant condition) and `if (self->name)` do not work either; only the `u32 n` local with `if (n != 0)` does.
- **The header inline cannot take the guard.** `func_ov006_021daea0` (already matched, same `ov006_SlotManager_Reset`) goes from 0 to 23 with the guarded fill, while `func_ov006_021dafb4` stays at 0. The game had two versions of the slot clear, so the guarded one is a local inline in the new file.
- **Try this when** the target recomputes `base + offset` after a call and keeps only the offset in a callee-saved register, while our build keeps the summed pointer.

## Split-then-modify locals fix register coalescing, and three codegen blockers that stay open (overlays, round shared1)

Five new matches. Each puzzle was first reproduced in a small standalone test file compiled with the project flags, and the source forms were then searched in that file or straight in the draft. Scores are raw / register-masked seqdiff. Drafts and test files are in `scratchpad/shared1/d/` and `scratchpad/shared1/p1`–`p5/`. `t/cc.py file [func]` compiles a test file and prints its disassembly, `t/ccq.py` is the same as a library, and `t/rsw.py file func mod spec.py` scores the text variants listed in a spec file.

| Function | Before | Change |
|---|---|---|
| `func_ov000_02196258` (new `Robo_02196258.cpp`) | 34 / 0 | `SetNibble` computes the shift in two steps: `s32 sh = idx % 8; u32 *p; sh *= 4; p = &...flags[row][idx / 8];`. `GetNibble` stays `(v >> ((idx % 8) * 4)) & 0xf`. |
| `func_ov000_021971c4` (new `Robo_021971c4.cpp`) | 85 / 4 | The same `SetNibble` (85 to 2; the four-way `self`/`zero`/`none`/`tgt` rotation went too). The last 2 came from a `FindActor(u16 id)` inline (`mgr = data_ov000_021ccd68; if (mgr == NULL) return NULL; return func_ov000_0218e640(mgr, id);`) in place of the `?:`. The inline's argument `self->0x90` is then loaded before the `mgr` NULL test, as in the target. |
| `func_ov003_021d6a3c` (new `ov003_021d6a3c.cpp`) | 16 / 3 | The same `SetNibble` and `GetNibble` pair as 6258. |
| `func_ov000_02199554` (appended to `Body_021992b4.c`) | 13 / 0 | The distance inline as `s32 x = a->x; s32 y = a->y; s32 z = a->z; x -= b->x; y -= b->y; z -= b->z;` instead of `s32 dx = a->x - b->x;`. That fixes the loop's scratch registers but rotates `n`/`q`/`out` (26 / 0). Declaring `s32 i;` before `s32 n;` fixes the rotation (0 / 0 in every order where `i` comes before `n`). |
| `func_ov000_02199180` (appended to `Body_02198c8c.c`) | 14 / 0 | The same two changes as 9554. |

- **Split-then-modify locals (the shared fix for puzzles 1 and 2).** When the target puts the result of `a op b` in the register of the other operand, or keeps a value in a register of its own where ours coalesces it, initialise a local from one operand and apply the operation as a separate statement (`s32 sh = idx % 8; sh *= 4;`, or `s32 x = a->x; x -= b->x;`). MWCC then gives the result a different live range, and the coalescing changes. In the standalone test the nibble register moved only with this form or with a whole-expression call (`Set(row, idx, 0xf | (Get(row, idx) & 8))`), and the second form changes the instruction count in the real function. In 6a3c the working pairs are a split `SetNibble` with a plain `GetNibble`, or a plain `SetNibble` with a split `GetNibble` (`s32 sh = idx; u32 w; sh %= 8; sh *= 4;`). Try both inlines.
- **Puzzle 3: `add rX, sp, #0` scheduled too early in `Ov012_Fx2` (still 2 / 2 in `fc688` and `fdfa0`; `ab7c` not retried).**
  - A standalone `Fx2` gives the target order when it is the first thing in its block. Put a call and a store in front of it in the same block (`p3/gen2.py`, context `c2`), and the `add` follows `mov r0, #0x68` before the copy stores, as in our build.
  - In every variant the `add` was scheduled right after `mov r0, #id`. The target's `add` fills the load slot after `ldrh z` instead, so the `&r` address is created later in the target's source.
  - None of these moved it in the test file or in fc688: `Rot3 r; r = *base;`, member-wise copies, a `u16 *` copy, `base[0]`, `const` temporary copy, `volatile` source, a copy inline, a one-element array, `r` as a caller local passed by pointer, `r` by value, a pointer local before or after the calls, the order of the `o`/`r` declarations, `id` typed `u16`/`s32`, and a returned versus discarded result (432 test variants and 16 in fc688). The member-wise, array and assignment forms stop keeping `&r` in a callee-saved register (47 / 34 and worse).
- **Puzzle 4: the `ov008_021ce518` switch root (still 1 / 1).** Once clusters are formed the target tree is ordinary: the elements are `{11}`, `{16,20}`, `{30}`, `{40}`, and the root is element `(4-1)/2`. So the open question is only how `{16,20}` became a cluster. `p4/sw.py` and `p4/sw2.py` add one or two extra labels with values 8–44 (pairs from 12–25). Each label goes to default, to its own empty `break`, or to one of the four real bodies (2,568 switches). No combination gives the target compares. An extra label that shares the 16/30 body (`case 18:`) removes its own `beq`, but the compare becomes `cmpne r0, #0x12`. The target has no conditional compare, so this is not the source either.
- **Puzzle 5: the 7-call block in `ov014_022153e0` (still 6 / 6).** The limit is not a fixed number of calls before a region. In a test file (`p5/reg.py`) with effects of three calls each, the region after the 7th call is left in source order. With N plain calls followed by one effect, the effect's first region is scheduled up to N = 4 and left in source order from N = 5. In the `53e0` shape (`p5/a7.cpp`), the region after the 4th call is already left in source order, and the region after the 6th call is scheduled again. Any real branch inside the block (for example a two-definition `id2`) splits it and restores the scheduling. That adds instructions the target does not have. Eleven other forms change nothing: block-scoped or array effects, effect, sound and flag inlines, a cached `pos` pointer, a chained call, and a cached sound global.
- `ppa`-style or permuter searches were not needed for the five matches. Every one came from the two source idioms above, plus the inline for `FindActor`.

- **Candidates.** I took every unmatched function (not in ov004) whose best draft scored 10 or less masked in `permsweep2/best.txt` and `bigfresh7/best_scan*.txt`, and skipped the functions ovmid8 had already run. That left 92 functions with a raw score above 0. The list is in `scratchpad/ppasweep1/cand.txt`.

K=2 (pairs of parameters) gave nothing that K=1 had missed, and it costs too much once a function has more than about 12 locals: `0204205c` ran 40 minutes without finishing. Run `ppaiter.sh` only on drafts that the first pass improved; on the others its first round just repeats the K=1 pass.
- **Comma order in a `for` initialiser is a scheduling lever.** `for (a = 0, b = 0; ...)` and `for (b = 0, a = 0; ...)` emit the same instructions in a different order. Try it whenever the only diff left is one swapped pair just before a loop.
