## The no-draft leftovers: conditional cross-object branches, crt0's parameter blocks and the last Mobiclip audio asm (main, round sinit5)

Code went from 92.756% to 92.851% (about +2,050 bytes). Scratch files are under `sinit5/`.

- **The list.** Of the unmatched functions in `report.json` with no draft (ov004 left out), the only `__sinit_*` left is `__sinit_ov002_021ef1f0`, which is off-limits because it needs the TU's asset-name table (round block7). The 18 "BIOS thumb stubs" (`CpuFastSet` .. `LZ77UnCompReadByCallbackWrite16bit`, `0x0200406a`..`0x02004798`) are `swi n; bx lr` pairs scattered through the secure area `0x02004000..0x02004800`, which is otherwise random filler (it starts with `ff de ff e7`). This is the `libsyscall` blob. Landing them would mean writing 2 KB of random bytes as `dcd`s, so they are skipped. The hand asm and data were `02004f94`, `BuildInfo`, `02004ffc`, `02075810`, `02075d4c` and `0207670c`, and all of them now match. Nine asm functions in matched files were below 100% because of `dcd` words. `Entry` and `_fdiv` now match; the seven FP runtime ones can't yet (see below).
- **dsd now keeps the condition field of a relocated ARM `b`/`bl`.** When delinking, dsd overwrote every `arm_call`/`arm_branch` word with an unconditional `bl #0`/`b #0`. A conditional call to another object, like `blne func_02075a78`, therefore had to stay a raw `dcd` (asm2mw's rule), and objdiff scored the function below 100%. `tools/dsd-patches/ds-decomp.patch` (`cli/src/config/section.rs`) now keeps bits 28–31 of the original word (`0xf` becomes `AL`). With a `kind:arm_call` line in `relocs.txt`, the asm can say `blne func_02075a78`. MWCC emits `R_ARM_PC24` for it, and mwld links it correctly. No existing `relocs.txt` entry was on a conditional instruction, so nothing else changed. ninja rebuilds dsd through `tools/build_dsd.py` (cargo plus network). The patch is `git diff -- . ':!Cargo.lock'` in `build/dsd-src/ds-decomp`. The MWCC assembler can't write a branch to `sym+offset` (`b _ll_sdiv+0x10` is "end of line expected", and the parenthesised form is "illegal operand"). So the FP runtime's branches into the middle of a neighbouring routine stay `dcd`, and `_dadd`/`_dsub`/`_fadd`/`_fsub`/`_ll_mod`/`_ll_udiv`/`_ull_mod` stay at 80–99.7%.
- **`libs/mobiclip/mobiclip_asm_02075810.c`** (`0x02075810..0x02075940`) holds the deblocking driver and its two byte tables (`data_020758f4`, written with `B4`). The code reads the tables through `add rX, pc` from a base inside its own last instructions, indexed by the quantiser. So asmblob's flow analysis reports `0x020758e8` as both code and data; use asm2mw for the function and a separate data block. Its three `blne` calls (`0x02075878`, `0x020758b8`, `0x020758e8`) got `relocs.txt` entries.
- **`libs/mobiclip/mobiclip_asm_02075d4c.c`** (`0x02075d4c..0x02076990`) is the audio frame decoder. Its first word is `b` to the real entry at `0x0207655c`, and the routines in front of that are reached only by local `bl`s, so dsd had sized it at `0x38`. It is now one asmblob block of `0x9c0` with 21 `.D_`/`.L_` labels. The file also holds `func_0207670c` (`b func_02077118`) and `data_02076710`, the 160-word quantiser table that `func_02076990` reads pc-relatively. Round mainbig5's worry about gaps with only data no longer applies: `delink -M` gives them mapping symbols, and the table now sits in a file anyway.
- **crt0.** `crt0.c` now runs to `0x02004fd4`. ## Every function in a non-gap unit at 100%: the FP runtime as `.s` files, and target-side fixes (round rtfix)

Code went from 92.851% to 93.093% (`matched_code` +5,736 bytes, 27 more functions at 100%). `total_code` grew by 600 bytes because two symbol sizes were wrong. No function in a non-gap unit is below 100% now (ov004 included). Scratch files are under `rtfix/`.

| Function(s) | Was | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| `_dadd`/`_dsub`, `_fadd`/`_fsub`, `_ll_mod`/`_ll_udiv`/`_ull_mod` | 80–99.7% | branches into the middle of a neighbour (`bmi _dsub+0x10`), written as `dcd` | `FP_fastI_dadd.s`, `FP_fastI_div.s`, `FP_fastI_fadd.s` (see below) |
| `__call_static_initializers` | 99.6% | the `.ctor` start was a number, the target has a `link_time_const(ARM9_CTOR_START)` relocation | `extern VoidFunc ARM9_CTOR_START[];` (the linker script defines it) |
| `svc_twl` `func_0200c118` | 96.5% | `blx` to TWL-only code (`module:none`) has no relocation in the target, but the compiled object has `bl` with one | dsd patch, below |
| `MATHi_SHA1K` | 0% | `kind:data(any)` came out 4 bytes long because of the `.L_` labels inside it | `kind:data(byte[0x10])` |
| `func_02017100` (`mi_memory`) | 0% | `symbols.txt` size `0xa4`; the asm routine runs to `0x020173f0` | `size=0x2f0` |
| `OSi_DisplayExContext` | 99.97% | `relocs.txt` was missing the `bl OS_DisableProtectionUnit` at `0x02019da0` and the `ldr lr, =@1` pool word at `0x02019dc8` | two `relocs.txt` lines (the second is `to:0x02019d50 add:0x50`) |
| ov004 DSProtect stubs (15 functions in `ov004_021cd4c0`, `021ce2ec`, `021ce7d8`, `021cf5cc`) | 7.5–89% | pool words written as `func_A+0x3214` where the target says `func_B+0x3200`, no `$d` on the target's pool words, and `dcd 0x1a...` for `bne func_ov004_021ce574` | the target's symbols, `.D_<addr> kind:label(arm,data)` lines, and `kind:arm_branch` relocations so the `bne` can be an instruction |

- **`.s` files through `mwasmarm`.** `tools/configure.py` now builds any `src/`/`libs/` `.s` file with `tools/mwccarm/dsi/1.3/mwasmarm.exe -proc arm5TE` (rule `mwasm`; it has no `arm946e`). `delinks.txt` names the `.s` file. The assembler takes GNU directives (`.global`, `.type x, @function`, `.size x, .-x`, `.word`, `.ltorg`, `;` comments), local `.L_` labels that don't reach the symbol table, any number of global labels in one section, and `b sym+0x10`. A branch inside the one `.text` section is resolved at assembly time with no relocation, the same as the target's object. `f1`/`f2` are register names there, so don't use them as labels. `.word` gets `$d`.
- **`.ltorg` reuses an earlier pool.** In `_dsub`, `ldr r1, =0x7ff00000` used `_dadd`'s pool entry (still in range) and the second pool was dropped, so the file loads that constant with `ldr r1, .L_dsub_pool` from a `.word` placed by hand.
- **Calls inside one `.s` file have no relocation.** The target had relocations for `_ll_sdiv`'s `bl _s32_div_f` and `_ull_mod`'s `bl _u32_div_not_0_f`, and mwasmarm can't emit them for a symbol in the same section. Repeated `.section .text` just merges. The two `relocs.txt` lines are removed. The code is the same either way.
- **`rtfix/c2s.py`** (scratch) converts a file of MWCC `asm void f(void) { ... }` blocks into a `.s` file. It turns `dcd 0x.. // bXX sym+off` into a real branch, `@L` into `.L_`, and adds `.ltorg` to functions that use `ldr =`. It was used once; the `.s` files are now the source.
- **dsd patch (`cli/src/config/section.rs`).** For a `module:none` `thumb_call_arm` relocation, dsd now writes the raw `blx` as the `bl` with the same offset (sets bit 12 of the second halfword) and still emits no relocation. objdiff already scores a raw `bl` against a relocated `bl` as equal (that's how the other three TWL wrappers were at 100%). There is only one such relocation, at `0x0200c13a`. The patch was made the sinit5 way (`git diff -- . ':!Cargo.lock'` in `build/dsd-src/ds-decomp`), and ninja rebuilds dsd.
- **ov004.** `func_ov004_021cd050`/`16c`/`288`/`3a4`, `021cdc6c`/`cdfac`/`cde0c`/`ce14c` and `021ce874`/`ce934`/`ceff8` are now `extern char[]` in the asm files. In `func_ov004_021ce50c` the `bne` sits at `0x021ce53c`, not at the start of the data, so its `.D_` is at `0x021ce540`.

With `ok` declared first, the zero comes in as a copy that MWCC doesn't fold into the store. This alone gives 4 / 4, and only the entry block's schedule is left.

## A matched sibling's inline, a split loop counter and a function-scope pointer: `ov011_021fb02c` matches (round ovra)

Drafts and tools are in the scratchpad under `ovra/` (one folder per function; `t/` holds ovreg's tools pointed at this clone, plus `v.py`, `par.sh`, `reuse.py` and `split.py`). Scores are raw / register-masked (`t/sc2.py`).

- **`func_ov011_021fb02c` (6 / 0 to 0), appended to `src/ov011/ov011_021fa6a0.cpp`** (the TU's `.text` end moves from `0x021fb02c` to `0x021fb38c`). The last diffs were `j` (the third loop's counter) and `dz` swapping `r5`/`r8`, and the draft needed `actor = (0, self->list->actor);`. Three changes, none of which helps alone:
  1. **The node is built with the matched sibling's inline.** `func_ov011_021fe3b4` (same overlay) builds its path node with `Ov011_NewPNode(const Ov011Vec *v)` (alloc, copy `x`/`y`/`z`, `next = NULL`) and then `e->unk_04 = Ov011_PushNode(e->unk_04, q); pn = q;`. Writing the delta as an `Ov011Vec delta` and building the node the same way gives 27 / 0 alone, but it is the base the other two need.
  2. **The second loop (`func_ov003_021d7c08` over `arr8`) gets its own counter**, `for (s32 k = 0; ...)`, instead of sharing `j` with the third loop. With 1, this gives 0 with the comma, or 21 without it.
  3. **`Ov011Ent *e` declared at function scope** instead of inside the third loop's `if`. This replaces the comma: the plain `actor = self->list->actor;` then matches.
- **Declaration order vs. definition order (toy functions, `ovra/exp/`).** Values defined once and never reassigned (call results, loads) are coloured in reverse order of definition, whatever the declaration order: of four call results, the last one gets `r4`. Locals with several definitions (accumulators, loop pointers) are coloured in declaration order: the first one declared gets the lowest register, and the order of the assignments doesn't matter. Hoisted constants come before both. So `dperm`-style declaration sweeps can only move multi-definition locals. To move the others, change where they are defined, or whether they are a separate local at all. Block scope against function scope also counts. In `021fb02c` and `02165a20` moving a pointer to function scope changed the result, but moving its declaration around within function scope did not.
- **`func_ov000_02165a20` (68 / 0 clean to 38 / 0 clean, `ovra/5a20/best_38_0_clean.cpp`).** The earlier best was 45 / 0, with fake parameters. Four changes to ovmid10's clean `e1.cpp`:
  - The area search is an inline, `FindArea02165a20(w, key[1], key[2])`, with `for (i = 0, s = w->areas; i < w->count; i++, s++) ... return s;` (no `goto`). This fixes the head's `a`/`b`/`i` registers.
  - `best = 0xffff;` is a separate statement after the declarations of the path block.

## Register allocator, more findings (round ovrb)

Toy tests (not in tree) refined the "round ovra" rules:
1. Straight-line call results are coloured in reverse order of definition, lowest free register first, whatever the declaration order.
2. A local's second and later lifetimes (reassigned after its first use is dead) are coloured after the first lifetimes of every other multi-def local, even ones declared later. This is why passing a model pointer to exactly one inline call changes which calls get swapped registers.
3. Values that live across a loop follow declaration order, even when assigned once.
4. Hoisted constants are coloured in reverse order of first use. They are not always first: a multi-def pointer used in a loop can beat a hoisted zero.

Drafts and tools are in the scratchpad under `big4/` (`53e0/`, `1478/`, `558c/`, `43bc/`, `6180/`, `toy/`, `lev/`; `t/` is ovra's tools pointed at this clone). Scores are raw / register-masked (`t/sc2.py`).

The fix is in the shake flags *after* those calls: `FLD(u8, g, 0x190) |= 0x1c;` becomes `FLD(Ov014Flags8, g, 0x190).b2 = 1; .b3 = 1; .b4 = 1;` (as `Ov014_Flash` in `ov014_0220eca0.cpp` writes the same byte). In the `53e0` shape, deleting the final `func_02049f44` call, or replacing it with a call of one or two arguments, schedules the region; a later call that passes something in `r2` (three or four arguments) leaves it in source order. Plain constant stores before the region do not change it, and neither do the forms of the `&self->pos` argument, the effect variable (one or two), the virtual-call spelling or a variadic prototype. So when a scheduling diff sits in a long block full of calls, try equivalent spellings of the statements later in that block (bit-field sets against masks, chained stores), not only of the region itself.

## A second access path instead of `volatile`: const views of a field, and the near-misses it did not reach (round view1)

The lever from `ov010_02201bf4` (`src/ov010/ov010_022019f4.cpp`): MWCC merges two reads of a field only when they go through the same access path and type. A read through a different path (a `const` view, a cast to the field's own struct type, or a different scalar type) is a separate expression. It is loaded again where it is written, and it does not reuse a register that holds the first read. Writing both reads the same way merges them. Most `volatile` casts in matched code exist only to force such a re-read, and a const view does the same job.

- **Replaced `volatile` in 35 matched files, every file still at 0** (checked per file with `scratchpad/view1/t/fm.py src module`, which compiles once and diffs every function in the object; then the full build):
  - **State machines (ov009, ov012, ov014).** `*(volatile u16 *)&s->state` and `&s->timer` became small accessors in the overlay headers: `Ov014Sub40_State` / `Ov014Sub40_Timer`, `Ov012Sub40_State` and `Ov009Sub40_State`, each `static inline u16 X(const T *s) { return s->field; }`. The inline with a `const` parameter is enough. With a plain `s->timer` read in the same place, most reads get merged (6–377 diffs). Only 7 of the 31 reads also match when written plain.
  - **`volatile` read-modify-writes** (`(*(volatile u16 *)&s->state)++`, `((volatile T *)p)->timer++`, in ov000, ov003, ov009, ov010 and ov013). There are two forms, and both match where they were tried: `x = <const view of x> + 1;`, or a plain `x++` with the earlier read that it must not reuse (usually the `switch`) taken through the const view. The second is the original's likely shape (`ov014_0220b74c`, `ov009_021fc51c`, `Robo_021a1c2c`).
  - **Single re-reads.** `((const ov006_Actor58 *)a)->pos.x` (`ov006_021d2c84`), `((const ov006_MenuNode *)n)->timer`, `((const Ov003FxNode *)p)->next`, `((const VecFx32 *)&data_ov013_0220af28)->x` (a cast to the object's own type is a second path), `FLD(const s16, ...)`, `FLD(const Ov011Flags8, ...)`, `FLD(const u16 *, self, 0x40)[0]`, and `*(CmdQueue *const *)&...` in `Widget_02182590`. In `ov002_021d2fdc` the `void *` field that was tested just before is read again as `(void *)FIELD(t, 0x118, u32)`: a different scalar type also counts as a separate path.
  - Not every case could be replaced. `VIDX` in `ov003_021d8fc0.cpp` (`Seq_Next` increments through it: 161–356), `ov010_0220b7b0` (the `b0` re-read: const view, own type or a new one-bit struct all leave 2), `Ov013Prm *volatile` in `ov013_02204a3c` (197), `Lo_0214e9e4` (31), and the reads where `volatile` fixes the order of two loads rather than a reuse all stay `volatile`. The order cases are `GfxSys_2` `state`/`nextState`, `SlidePanel_2`, `NamePool` `progress`, `ov009_0220b70c` and the ov007 queue pointer. The `volatile` parameters and locals that force a reload from the stack are a different mechanism, and this lever does not apply to them.
- **`func_0206e858` stays at 1.** Address constants are not keyed by access path. Every spelling of the `data_0214b105` destination (member, symbol, `&x[0]`, `+ 0`, const casts, const accessors, an own-type cast, inline wrappers, 9 × 9 and 10 × 10 pairs in `scratchpad/view1/e858d`–`e858h`) is either CSE'd into `r5` (11) or gets `add r0, r5, #1` from `st`. The only form with the target's code, `data_0214b105` and then `data_0214b104.name`, has one pool word too many. ## How MWCC lowers a `switch`, read from the compiler, and the x87 precision of the build (round swtree)

Three new matches: `func_02006e48` (MSL `__pformatter`, appended to `libs/msl/printf.c`), `func_ov008_021ce518` (new file `src/ov008/ov008_021ce518.cpp`) and `func_02015510` (`GX_SetBankForSubBG`, added to `libs/nitro/gx/gx_vramcnt_2.c`). All three were already right in earlier drafts. What kept them from matching was the build: MWCC decides switch clusters with the x87 FPU, and under wibo the FPU ran at a different precision from the original Windows build.

### The fix: `tools/fpucw.py`

`mwccarm.exe` never sets the x87 control word. It uses whatever the OS gives a new thread, which on Windows is `0x27F` (53-bit, double precision). Linux starts every process at `0x37F` (64-bit precision), and wibo 0.6.16 keeps it. The cluster test below divides `count / range` in the FPU and compares the result with the double constant `0.4`. At 64-bit precision an exact 2/5 (`{16,20}`, 4/10, 6/15, ...) comes out just below the rounded-up double `0.4`, so the merge is refused. At 53-bit precision the two are equal and the merge happens. The ROM was built the second way.

`tools/fpucw.py program args...` starts the program under `ptrace`, sets the control word to `0x27F` right after the `execve`, and detaches. The `mwcc` rule in `tools/configure.py` (non-Windows only), `tools/match.py`, `tools/permuter/cxxperm.py`, `tools/permuter/cc.sh` and `tools/asm2mw/asm2mw.py` now run the compiler through it. A full rebuild with the wrapper gave the same bytes for all 2,384 objects, so nothing that already matched depended on the old precision. **Scratch scripts that call `./wibo ... mwccarm.exe` directly still compile the old way.** Put `python3 tools/fpucw.py` in front of `./wibo`, or score with `tools/match.py`. The wrapper costs about 20 ms per compile.

### The algorithm

This was read from `mwccarm.exe` (dsi/1.3; every compiler under `tools/mwccarm` behaves the same). The cluster pass is at `0x5a21f0`, the tree builder at `0x5a2090`, and the per-cluster emitters at `0x52b1d0` (`CodeGenSwitch.c`). `scratchpad/swtree/t/swsim.py` implements it. It predicted the clusters of 1,500 random switches exactly in each precision mode (`--strict` gives the old wibo behaviour).

1. **Case list.** Every `case` label is one entry, including labels that share the `default` body (`case 'p': default:`) and empty `case N: break;` labels. Arm grouping, the order of the labels in the source, and where `default` sits make no difference. The list is sorted by value: unsigned for `u32`/`unsigned` operands, signed otherwise (`u8`/`s8`/`u16` promote to `int`). Unsigned operands also get `bhi`/`bhs` instead of `bgt`/`bge`. Each `switch` statement, nested or not, is lowered on its own.
2. **Three or fewer cases**: a linear `cmp`/`beq` chain in ascending order, then `b default`.
3. **Cluster pass.** For four or more cases, with `c[]` the sorted values and `S[k]` the first case of cluster `k`:

   ```
   k = 0
   for i in 0 .. n-1:
       S[k] = i
       while k > 0:
           range = c[i] - c[k-1] + 1      # c[k-1]: indexed by CLUSTER number, not c[S[k-1]]
           count = i - k + 2              # likewise: i - (k-1) + 1
           if count / range < 0.4: break  # x87; at 53-bit precision exactly 0.4 merges
           k -= 1                         # cluster k joins cluster k-1
       k += 1
   ```

   The intended test was "cases `S[k-1]..i` fill at least 40% of their range". The shipped code indexes the case array by the cluster number instead. While every cluster so far is a single case, `k-1 == S[k-1]` and the test is the intended one. After a cluster of `s` cases forms, the reference value `c[k-1]` lags `s-1` cases behind the cluster's real start. Three consequences:
   - **The first cluster is the honest one.** For example, `{100..103}` followed by `{120..125}`: the later group is measured from a stale low value, so `120`, `121` and `122` stay single compares and only `123..125` merge, giving `T[100..103] 120 121 122 C[123..125]`. With a two-case first cluster, only `120` is left out.
   - **One case can merge several clusters at once** (the `while` loop walks back). `{100..103}` + `{112..116}` becomes one table `T[100..116]` (when `116` arrives it merges the singles `112..115` and the first table in one go), while `{100..103}` + `{112..115}` stays `T[100..103]` and four singles. The deciding test is `count/range` from the stale reference, not the density of the whole run.
   - **Adding or removing a label anywhere before a cluster** (even one that goes to `default`) shifts every later stale index. That is why extra default labels move tables around unpredictably.
4. **Cluster kinds.** A cluster of 4 or more cases is a jump table, 2–3 cases are a range compare, and 1 case is a single compare.
5. **Tree.** A binary search over the clusters: `build(lo, hi)` takes `mid = (lo + hi) / 2` and emits cluster `mid`, then `build(lo, mid-1)`, then `build(mid+1, hi)`. With `m` clusters the root is cluster `(m-1)/2`.
   - A single case: `cmp v; bgt right; bge body` (`beq body; b default` when there is no left subtree), then the left subtree.
   - A range compare: `cmp hi; bgt right; cmp lo; blt left; beq body_lo; cmp v; beq body_v` for each other member; then `b default`.
   - A table: `cmp hi; bgt right; subs rX, v, #lo; addpl pc, pc, rX, lsl #2; b left`, then one `b` per value (gaps go to `default`). With no tree around it: `sub`, `cmp #(hi-lo)`, `addls pc`.
   - A table whose lowest case is 1..7 starts at 0 instead (no `sub`). The limit is 3 for Thumb.
   - A compare whose only outcome is `default` disappears (`beq D; b D` becomes `b D`).
6. **Bit tests.** A switch whose cases all go to one body (`case 1: case 5: case 9: ... return 1; default: return 0;`) can become `sub; cmp; tst mask, 1 << x` (`IsLogicalSelectionBitTestBeneficial`) and no tree at all.

How to use it: write down the target's clusters from the disassembly (`addls`/`addpl` tables, `cmp hi; bgt; cmp lo; blt` ranges, single compares), list the draft's labels, and run `swsim.py` on them. If no label set gives the target's clusters, the structure is wrong somewhere else. Brute force over extra labels in the simulator takes seconds; with the compiler it took thousands of builds.

### The three matches

- **`__pformatter`.** The original MSL label set (`% A E F G X a c d e f g i n o s u x`, no `'p'`) gives `'%' T[A..G] 'X' 'a' 'c' T[d..u] 'x'` at 53-bit precision, which is the target. At 64-bit it gives `T[d..o] C[s..x]`. A `case 'p':` (from the mainnm draft, 7 diffs) gives `T[d..x]` in both modes. Under the stale rule, `T[d..u]` followed by a single `'x'` cannot happen at 64-bit precision with any set of extra labels: `u` merges against `c[5]` with `count/range = 12/30`, and that is exactly 0.4. The function goes at the end of `printf.c`, whose `.text` now ends at `0x020076f4`. Its `""` and `L""` literals are the compiler's `@1185`/`@1186` (`symbols.txt`, `local`), so `printf.c`'s `.data` now ends at `0x0208adb8`.
- **`ov008_021ce518`.** `big11/d/ce518_none.cpp` (the draft without the dummy `case 21:`) is 0. Round bigfresh8's "`{16,20}` cannot be a cluster" was the 2/5 case. The window allocation of case 11 is written out inline: the `Ov008_NewWin()` inline from the draft costs 13 diffs.
- **`func_02015510`** is NitroSDK `GX_SetBankForSubBG`, placed right after `GxSetBankForSubBG` in `gx_vramcnt_2.c` (start moved to `0x02015510`). The mainbig6 and mainlow12 drafts were already exact.

## Inside the register allocator: how MWCC numbers vregs, and what that fixes (round rgraph)

Round giantsD built a window into mwccarm's colouring: `ra.sh`/`ra.py` run the compiler under gdb, break on the graph colourer and dump, per round, the interference graph (one line per vreg: colour, flags, spill cost, neighbours and the debug name of the object behind it), the simplify order and the whole pcode with vreg operands. `sim.py` replays simplify and colouring in Python. This round used them on the register-only near-misses to find out *which vreg numbering* each target needs, and then which source constructs produce which numbering. The numbering rules below are the useful part; no function landed from them yet.

### The allocator, confirmed

- The integer register class is **14 wide**. `sim.py` reproduces the compiler's simplify order and every colour exactly at `K=14` on real functions (`ov006_021de6bc`, 381 nodes, and `ov000_02165a20`, 254 nodes: order identical, zero colour mismatches). `K=13` and `K=15` reproduce neither. On `ov002_021d3e14` the order comes out slightly different but every colour still matches, so treat the order as a bonus and the colours as the check. Nodes are pushed while their degree is `< K`; when every remaining node is saturated, the one with the smallest `cost/degree` is pushed (flag `0x80` and `0x400` nodes last).
- Colouring walks the stack back and takes the **lowest free register**, from `r0-r3, r12, r14` first and then `r4 … r11` opened one at a time as the volatile ones run out. Because the simplify order mostly mirrors the vreg numbers, the practical rule is: **among values that interfere, the higher-numbered vreg is coloured first and gets the lower register.**
- The dump is only usable when the graph colours without spilling. `ov002_021d1f70` spills (`c=-1` nodes, the `str [sp]`s in the target), the compiler then rebuilds and re-colours, and `sim.py` does not follow that yet.

### Where vreg numbers come from

Read off the pcode dumps of `ov006_021de6bc` (381 vregs) and `ov002_021d1f70` (210):

1. `v0 … v15` are the physical registers; the parameters follow at `v16`.
2. The function-scope named locals occupy **one contiguous block, numbered in reverse declaration order** — the first declared local has the highest number, and inner-scope declarations continue the same descending run. `ov006_021de6bc` declares `m0, pair, item, m1` and then `py, px, pz`, `x, y`, `m`, and gets `m0=123, pair=122, item=121, m1=120, py=119, pz=118, x=117, y=116, m=115`. `ov002_021d1f70` declares `v44, d, n, x, o, y, z` and gets `v44=71, d=70, o=68, x=69, z=66, y=67`. A local the compiler folds away (`px`, `n`) takes no number and the rest close up.
3. **Above** that block is the ordinary expression-temp pool, which *ascends* with first definition (`124 … 380` in `021de6bc`, `65 … 253` in `02165a20`).
4. **Below** it are the temps of inlined calls (`17 … 114`, `16 … 53`), and at the very bottom the extra lifetimes of multiply-assigned locals and some long-lived CSEs. In `021de6bc` the inline temps run *downward* with first definition (`112, 109, 106, … 77`) while those bottom values run upward (`50, 51, 54, 59`).

   This layout is not universal: in `ov000_02165a20` the locals and the low temps interleave in the same range (`w=64, p=62, e=60, k=58, k=54, best=55` with temps at `59, 61, 63`), because that function declares `e` and `k` twice in two inner scopes. Dump the graph rather than predicting the numbers; what the dump is for is telling you *which* number has to move, and the rules below say which source change moves it.

### The rule that decides register-only misses

**A local that is assigned more than once keeps its named-local number only for its first lifetime. Every later lifetime gets a vreg from the bottom pool, below every inline temp, so it is coloured last among the values it interferes with and gets the highest register.**

In `ov006_021de6bc` the four `self->unk34` blocks are the same inline called four times. Three of them pass a model pointer the compiler numbers high — `m1=120` (a local assigned once) and `87` (an ordinary temp, no local) — and both come out in `r5`, like the ROM. The two blocks that assign to `m0`, which was already used earlier, get vregs `50` and `51` for the same pointer: numbered *below* the inline's own `res` temp (`96`, `93`), coloured after it, and so put in `r7` where the ROM has `r5`. Those 16 instructions are the whole remaining diff. A toy with the same shape (four calls to one branching inline, a live `x`/`y` pair around them) shows it in isolation: one local reused across two call sites gives the second site's pointer vreg 25 and `r10`; two separate locals give it vreg 50 and `r7`, with nothing else in the function moving.

So the lever is lifetimes, not declaration order:

- to push a value into a **higher** register, fold it into a local that is already live earlier in the function (make it a second lifetime);
- to pull it into a **lower** register, split the local so that the value is a first lifetime.

### Two corollaries about declaration order

- **Order only matters between locals whose lifetimes interfere.** Twenty-four declaration orders of four pointer locals, each assigned once at a different call site of `ov006_021de6bc`, compile to identical code (all 132 diffs). A local that is assigned once and used nearby is coalesced with the temp that defines it and never reaches the graph at all (toys `h3.cpp`/`b3.txt`).
- **Adding or removing one *used* local is a blunt instrument.** It shifts the named block and both temp pools by one and can recolour everything: dropping one local from the `021de6bc` draft moved `self` from `r4` to `r5` and took the function from 16 diffs to 109. Six-local variants of the same draft (one local per call site, every declaration order) all score 114 or 132. Prefer changing a lifetime over adding a declaration.

### The what-if method, and what it says about the remaining misses

With a dump in hand, `wi2.py`-style renumbering proves what the target needs before touching the source: move a node's number, re-run `sim.py`, and check that the ROM's register swap appears *and* that no other node changes colour.

- `ov006_021de6bc` (16 diffs, registers only): swapping the model pointer with the inline's `res` temp in the two `m0` blocks (`50 ↔ 96`, `51 ↔ 93`) gives the target's registers with zero collateral changes. Every source shape tried keeps the model below `res` there.
- `ov000_02165a20` (38 diffs, all of them `r7 ↔ r8`): `FindArea`'s loop pointer (`27`) has to be renumbered anywhere between the second lifetime of `w` (`30`) and the top of the low pool (`53`); that flips exactly the eleven nodes the ROM wants and nothing else. A sweep of every single-node move in the graph finds no other way to it. Splitting `w` into two locals does the opposite — it raises the second value to a named number (`59`) — and hand-inlining `FindArea` to make its pointer a function-scope local changes the control flow (12 wrong instructions).
- `ov002_021d3e14` (18 diffs, all of them `r5 ↔ r6`): the hoisted `0` has to be numbered inside the named-local block, just below `g` — then `0` takes `r6` and both `g` and `base` take `r5`, which is the target, with nothing else moving. A local assigned `0` once does not do it: it is coalesced into the same hoisted constant and the graph is unchanged (`z2…z5` variants). Writing the field triples as `SetA`/`SetB` inlines with `0` as an argument does not either — same 18 diffs, same graph.

All three are now one known vreg swap away rather than an unexplained register miss.

## The vreg allocator traced, and two register-only misses matched (round rgraph2)

This round put breakpoints inside mwccarm (1.3, `dsi/1.3/mwccarm.exe` under wibo and gdb) on the code that hands out vreg numbers, so the numbering rules of round rgraph are now read off the compiler instead of guessed. Two of the three "one vreg swap away" functions matched with a source change found from that: `ov000_02165a20` and `ov006_021de6bc`.

### Who hands out the numbers

- `0x507830` gives one Object its vreg (`used_virtual_registers[class]++`, the counter at `0x65b860`). It is called once for the parameters and then from the loop at `0x507d60`, which walks the function's **local-object list** (head at `0x65e28c`). Every object is prepended to that list when it is created (`0x4aa440`), so the walk sees the newest object first: **vregs `17 …` go to local objects in reverse order of creation.** Everything numbered above the named locals is allocated later, during code generation, in ascending order. Compiler temps are named `@N` with `N` a running creation counter, so the dump's `obj=@N` already tells you the creation order.
- The objects are created in fixed phases, and logging the creating call site of each one (break on `0x4aa440`, read `[esp]` and the return addresses on the stack) gives this order, oldest (highest vreg) first:
  1. named locals, as the parser meets their declarations (`0x4ace06`);
  2. the inliner, call site by call site in source order: first a temp for every argument that is not a plain variable or constant (`0x4a8592`), then the inline's own locals (`0x4a8603`); nested inlines come in through `0x4a41e1`;
  3. a few post-inline temps (`0x4a819a`);
  4. the global optimizer (`0x4748fd` → `0x4f4a12`): loop passes (`0x561ebb`, `0x58fce4`, `0x59b50b`), then **CSE** (`0x5961cd`, one object per common subexpression, created when its second occurrence is found), then **lifetime splitting** (`0x59d3ff`, the extra lifetimes of locals assigned more than once);
  5. the back end's lowering of `?:` (`0x5077d0` → `0x59dc60`), which makes three objects per conditional expression. In `ov006_021de6bc` all 33 of vregs `17 … 49` are these — the `part` value of every inlined `GetPart` (`return idx >= n ? NULL : &parts[idx]`) — and they are numbered below everything else.

  So "inline temps sit below the named locals and extra lifetimes sit below the inline temps" (round rgraph) is the phase order. The practical lever is: **an equivalent spelling that makes a different phase create the object moves its number by a whole band.**
- Tools (scratchpad `rgraph2/re/`): `vo.sh FILE` logs every `0x507830` call (vreg, object name); `lw.sh FILE` (env `LWOUT`) also logs each object's creation call stack; `join.py LWOUT N` joins the two into "vreg, name, creation order, first N return addresses".

### Simplify, decoded

The simplify loop at `0x526b90` was disassembled and `sim3.py` now follows it exactly: sweep the nodes in index order, pushing every node whose current degree is below `K` (neighbours lose 1, or 2 if either node has flag `0x200`), and repeat the sweep while anything was pushed; the nodes left over form the spill list **in descending index order**, and the candidate is the first one with the strictly smallest `cost / current degree` (flag `0x80` counts as `3.4e38`, `0x400` as `1.7e38`). So ties go to the **highest**-numbered node; `sim.py` broke them the other way, which is why it got `ov002_021d3e14`'s order slightly wrong and `ov002_021d1f70`'s spill choice wrong. `sim3.py` reproduces the simplify order and every colour of all six dumped rounds (`021de6bc`, `02165a20`, both rounds of `021d3e14` and both rounds of `021d1f70`).

For functions that spill, `wi.py`'s `colour_rounds(dump, moves)` applies a renumbering to every dumped round and reports whether round 1 still spills the same nodes. While it does, the next round's graph is the dumped one (spill code only adds nodes above the old count), so the answer for the final round is exact; when the spill set changes, the what-if is out of reach and the function needs a recompile.

### `ov000_02165a20`: a `?:` returned through another inline (matched)

The loop pointer of `FindArea` (also `start` afterwards) was vreg `27` = `@201`, a `?:` temp from the back end. `FindArea` ended with `return GetArea(w, b);`, and `GetArea` is `return i >= w->count ? NULL : &w->areas[i];`, so the inline's merged return value came from the `?:` lowering — bottom of the pool. Writing that tail out as

```c
if (b >= w->count) {
    return NULL;
}
return &w->areas[b];
```

lets the inliner's own object for `s` carry the value (vreg `48`, inside the `(30, 53)` window round rgraph asked for) and the function matches (`src/ov000/Area_02165a20.cpp`). `GetArea` itself keeps the `?:` form for its other two call sites.

### `ov006_021de6bc`: test the field, then copy it (matched)

The model pointer had to be numbered above the inline's `res`. Logging creation showed why no ordering of locals could do it: `res` (`ov006_ModelRes *res = model->unk28; if (res == NULL) return;`) is an inline local, while the pointer in the two bad blocks was a split lifetime of `m0` (phase 4, below every inline local). What works is to move `res` down a band instead, into CSE, with a local copy of the inline:

```c
static inline void ov006_Model_PlayPartChk(ov006_Model *model, int idx) {
    ov006_ModelRes *res;
    ...
    if (model->unk28 == NULL) {
        return;
    }
    res = model->unk28;
    ...
}
```

`model->unk28` now occurs twice, so CSE creates the object that holds it, and `res` itself is copy-propagated away. Each expansion's `res` lands in the CSE band (`51 … 73`), in call order, under every pointer. The pointers were also made first lifetimes again: blocks 1, 2 and 4 pass `self->unk34` directly (an argument temp, phase 2) and block 3 keeps `m1`, so `m0` is assigned once. Neither change is enough alone. The checking form with the `m0` blocks kept gives 16 diffs, the direct arguments alone 114, and both together in only one of the two blocks 8. With both blocks fixed but the plain inline left at block 3's `m1` call, it is 114. The function matches when every `PlayPart` call in it uses the checking form (`src/ov006/ov006_021de6bc.cpp`). A grid of what-ifs had shown the condition first: `res` anywhere in `[37.5, 58.5]` with the pointer anywhere above it.

### Still open

- `ov002_021d3e14` (18 / 0): with `sim3.py` and the spill check, the only single moves that give the target are the hoisted `0` (`v84`) into `(60.5, 62.5)` — between `base` and `i`, so in the named block — or `base` above `84`. A sweep of every pair of positions for `g` and `base` below the named block finds nothing. `0` is a constant the code generator hoists. No object can be numbered above it, and a named local that holds `0` is constant-propagated away. Six variants that initialise a declared local to `0` (`count`, `p`, `i`, `id`, `base`, `tbl`) leave the code unchanged.
- `ov002_021d1f70` (35 / 0) spills `d`, `v44` and one temp in round 1. `sim3.py` reproduces both rounds, so it can now be analysed. The diff asks for nine nodes to change colour: `x`, `z`, the `o[0x51]` CSE, both inlined models and their `res`, one `part` and the `y << 12` CSE. No single renumbering does more than two of them (`z` into the CSE band, `[36.5, 61.5]`). A greedy search over pairs gets to six wrong and stops (`d1greedy.py`). The target is several moves away, and the moves have not been tied to source yet. The checking form of `PlayPart` from `021de6bc` changes nothing at the two call sites in the function body, and makes things worse (132) at the second call site inside `DrawCount`.

## Codegen temps versus objects: `ov002_021e7ea8` and `ov002_021d3e14` match (round vphase)

Round rgraph2 explained how *objects* (named locals, inline temps, CSEs, split lifetimes, `?:` results) are numbered. This round looked at the other kind of vreg: the **codegen temp**, a value with no object behind it (`obj=-` in the `ra.sh` dump). Two register-only misses matched once a value was moved from one kind to the other.

### Tools (scratchpad `vphase/re/`)

- `an.sh DRAFT FUNC MODULE DIR` runs `match.py`, dumps the graph and pcode (`dumpv.sh`), logs object creation (`lw.sh` + `join.py`), and runs `want.py`.
- `want.py DIR MATCHTXT` lines up the final round's pcode with our disassembly. It matches register tuples and `k2` immediates, using a longest-common-subsequence pass and then the nearest unpaired instruction. Each vreg then gets the target's register at the same position. The result goes to `DIR/tgt.json`, so nobody has to write the "want" dict by hand. It is reliable on short functions. In long functions with repeated call sequences the alignment can slip, so check `novote` and fill in a few nodes by hand.
- `sw1.py RA.out @tgt.json [procs] [moves]` lists every single move that gives the target with no other node changing, on top of optional fixed moves. `pair.py` sweeps a grid over two nodes, `gr.py` does a beam search, and `tryp.py` shows the wrong nodes after a given set of moves. All of them use `wi.colour_rounds`, so they handle spills. `ONLY=a,b,c` limits `sw1.py` to some nodes, which helps on big graphs.

### Which values are codegen temps

- A codegen temp is numbered when the code generator first produces it, in statement order, above every object. That includes the hoisted constants (`mov rX, #0` lifted to the top of the function), which get their number at their first use. "Above the hoisted `0`" therefore means "a codegen temp, not an object".
- **A local that is assigned once is folded into the codegen temp that defines it, unless a call lies between the definition and the first use.** In that case it stays an object in the named block. Toys (`vphase/toy/k1`–`k5`) show this. With `base = *(u8 **)(D + 0x4c)` and then a loop calling `F(base + 0x110, ...)`, `base` is a codegen temp. With `tbl = T(D, 8)` between the definition and the loop, `base` is an object. Calls inside the loop, after the first use, do not matter.
- **A local that copies a global (`g = data_x;`) is forward-substituted.** Every use becomes a load of the global, and those loads are merged into one CSE object. **A local defined as a load plus a constant (`p = data_x + 0x8b0`, `blk = data->unk_4c + 0x110`) is forward-substituted as a tree.** The load inside it is computed once and stays a codegen temp, even across calls. The add is done again at each use, or folded into the addressing mode (`ldrb r2, [r6, #0x8b0]`).

### `ov002_021e7ea8` (56 / 0, the dejunk draft)

`want.py` and `sw1.py` gave two moves. `gx` had to go below `ret` (anywhere `16.5 … 42.5`). The `data_02097d48` load (a CSE, `35`) had to go above the hoisted `0` (`63.5 … 83.5`), so it had to be a codegen temp. Declaring `ret` before `gx` handles the first move. For the second, `case 0` drops `g` and writes

```c
gx = data_02097d48 + 0x8b0;
...
FIELD(gx, 0, Bits8).b4 = 0;
FIELD(gx, 0, Bits8).b5 = 1;
```

The load is now one codegen temp shared by `gx` and the bit-field access (`ldrb r2, [r6, #0x8b0]`), and the function matches (`src/ov002/ov002_021e7ea8.cpp`). Neither change is enough alone (72 diffs with only the declaration order).

### `ov002_021d3e14` (18 / 0, the round rgraph2 "unreachable" one)

Round rgraph2's what-if said `base` had to be numbered above the hoisted `0` (`84`), which seemed impossible for a named local. It is possible for a codegen temp. `base` is loaded before the `func_0205976c`/`func_0205975c` calls and used only as `base + 0x110` in the loop. Pointing the local at the sub-block instead,

```c
blk = FIELD(data_02fe152c, 0x4c, u8 *) + 0x110;
... func_02059544(data_02fe152c, blk, tbl, 1, i) ...
```

makes the load a codegen temp (the `+ 0x110` is still done in the loop, as in the ROM), and the function matches (`src/ov002/ov002_021d3e14.cpp`).

### Same lever, not matched yet

- `ov000_02176714` (dejunk draft, 73 / 2): it has the same `Items` loop, `base + 0x130`. With `base = ... + 0x130` the draft goes to **15, all registers** (`vphase/6714/e1.cpp`). Two exact single moves remain. Either `tbl` goes below the `tbl[i].b` CSE (`id`, anywhere `16.5 … 65.5`, the split-lifetime or `?:` band), or the `id` CSE goes to `70.5`, between the inline's `i` and `tbl`. Every declaration order of the inline's locals, `id` declared at each position in the inline, and the `Ov002_Avail` shape from `021d3e14` stay at 15.
- `ov000_021743bc` (`big4/43bc/bfv/s12.cpp`, 113): `t + 0x70` in `Has021743bc` gives 105.

### Looked at, and why they are not register-numbering problems

- `ov000_0219b808` (4): the target's `ldrh r1, [r7, #0x7c]` interferes with the physical `r1` in our pcode, because the `Send` inline's struct copy is placed between the argument moves. That is pcode order, not numbering.
- `ov000_021be5dc` (3): the `z - 0x1000` temp has to be numbered below the `smull` result temps. The code generator gives the result registers numbers before it evaluates the operands. So the subtraction would have to be an object, and a single-use value never survives as one. `ToDepth2`, an `s64` temporary, a local for `g[0xa28]` and argument forms all stay at 3.
- `ov011_021fc0b8`, `ov000_0218cfc8` and `ov000_021b3e90` have instruction-order or condition differences, not only register ones.
- Many drafts listed in `bfsweep/best1.txt` are permuter output (parameters reused as locals, `(0, x)`, `__typeof__` temps, one-element arrays). These include `0214dd3c`, `021512b4`, `021688c4`, `0216c310`, `0217558c` and `021d1f70`. Their what-ifs point at objects that exist only because of the junk. The `021688c4` draft without the junk parameter is still 20, and it needs the `a5` local numbered inside the second `Model_PlayPart` expansion's inline band.
## A callee's real parameter type removes a CSE band: `func_0206f85c` matches (round vmain)

One new match in main, found with the rgraph2 vreg model (`vo.sh`/`lw.sh`/`join.py`, `sim3.py`, `wi.py`). Tools for this round are in the scratchpad under `vmain/re/` (the rgraph2 tools pointed at this clone; `dump.sh FILE` runs `ra.sh` and `vo.sh` and prints the last function's nodes with their names, `wi1.py ra.out ROUND "node:reg,..."` lists every single-node renumbering that gives the wanted registers with no collateral change, `wib.py` is the beam2 beam search on `sim3`, and `EXTRA=-lang=c` compiles C files). `vmain/var.py base func variants.txt` scores old/new text substitutions in parallel, and `vmain/audit.py files...` compares the parameter types of every prototype in the given files with the matched definition in `src/` or `libs/`.

### `func_0206f85c` (19 / 0 to 0, `src/Main/Lang/ItemGive_2.cpp`)

- The graph showed that the loop counter is not `i` at all. The node that carries it is `@668`, a **CSE** object (creation stack through `0x5961cd`), numbered 25, inside the CSE band. Round beam2 had already found that `i` needed to sit at about 31.5, which is the named-local block between `block` and `b`.
- The CSE object exists because the draft declared the callee as `func_02059544(..., int packed, u32 id)` and passed the `u16 i` to it twice. Each call converts `i` to `u32`, and CSE merges the two conversions into one object. The matched definition in `DataRes_5.cpp` is `(..., int packed, u16 sub)`. With that prototype nothing is converted, there is no CSE object, and `i` itself is the node, in the named block, numbered by its declaration.
- After that, the declaration order gives the number: `BOOL done; int a; int b; u16 i;` (then `block`, `entries`, `count`) puts `i` just above `block`, and the function matches. With `i` first it is 18. `ItemGive.cpp` and `ItemGive_3.cpp` still declare `u32 id` and match as they are; `ItemGive_2.cpp` now has the real prototype, and its other caller, `func_0206f788`, still matches with it.
- Lever: **when the live object for a local is a CSE temp, look for an implicit conversion of that local that appears twice** (a call argument whose declared type is wider than the variable, for example). Fixing the prototype to the real one moves the value out of the CSE band and into the named block. `audit.py` run over the newest drafts of every unmatched main function found no other integer-width mismatch on a call inside the target function, except `G3X_SetClearColor`'s `u8` in the `0206e3a0` draft (with the real `int` it still scores 2) and `NNS_G2dGetAnimSequenceByIdx`'s `int` in the `020417e0` draft (with the real `u16` it goes to 149).

### What the graphs say about the rest

- **`02056e74` (4 / 0).** The two wrong nodes are inside the inlined `(s64)s * -0x80000 + 0x800`: the target wants the sign word of `s` (`asr`, vreg 185) in `r4` and the low word of the `+ 0x800` (vreg 180) in `r1`. `wi1.py` says that 185 has to be numbered anywhere below 180 (15.5 to 179.5), and that nothing else works. The code generator allocates the 64-bit add's result pair (180/181) before it walks into the multiply, which then allocates the product (182/183) and the sign (185). So the sign must come from an earlier phase, or the add must be generated after the multiply. None of these moved it: an `s64` inline parameter (with the argument a plain variable, an expression, or `(s64)s`), an `s64` local for the product or for the operand, `t += 0x800`, operands swapped, `0x800 + ...`, `0x800LL`, and `Hud_FxMulR`.
- **`0203a984` (10 / 0).** The model agrees with beam2: `b` (the `blocks[i]` load, codegen temp 55) has to be numbered in 56.5 to 61.5, after the three temps of `name`. `name` would also work anywhere in 30.5 to 54.5, which is above every named local. All of these are code-generator temps. Codegen allocates a statement's result first and then its operands, top-down, so `b`'s load is always first. Folding the assignment into `name`'s expression (`((b = blocks[i])->addr >> 5) >> shift`) gives the same IR, so the same graph. Computing `name` after the `attr01` store moves the load below the store (49). Declaring `name` at function scope, in any position, does not make it a node: it is still coalesced into its temp.
- **`020459cc` (9) and `02046070` (6).** These are the same miss. At each inlined `WH_ChangeSysState`, the target puts the constant in a lower register than the reloaded `data_02097e40`. In every matched `WH_ChangeSysState` in `Wh.cpp`, `Wh_2.cpp` and `WhScan.cpp`, the pointer has the lower register. In the graph the constant is allocated before the load. `wi1.py` says each site needs the load numbered below the constant (for example 27 in 15.5 to 25.5 in `020459cc`), which is the object band. No form of the inline changed the score (27 forms, tried in `020459cc`): a pointer local, a getter inline, the pointer as an inline argument, `u16`/`u8`/reference state types, `*(int *)((u8 *)p + 0x2c)`, `(*p).f`, a returned assignment, and SDK-style `if (0) OS_TPrintf(...)` traces before and after the store. The inliner drops all of these objects before vregs are assigned. Optimisation levels 0 to 4 for `02046070` also gave nothing better than 6.
- **`0206d43c` (12).** A beam search with three moves reaches the target. The smulbb result has to be numbered above the first `Align` load (29 above 33). ## Moving an object between numbering bands by spelling alone: four overlay matches (round vphase2)

This round goes on from round vphase. Each item below is a way to move one value into a different numbering band without junk. The bands are, from highest vreg to lowest: named locals, inline argument temps and inline locals, post-inline temps, loop-pass objects, CSE objects, split lifetimes, and `?:` objects.

- **Reusing a dead local gives a split lifetime.** Assign the value to a local whose earlier lifetime has already ended. The value then becomes a split-lifetime object near the bottom of the numbering, below the CSEs. It does not get its own named-local number.
- **Writing an expression again gives a CSE.** Don't hold a value in a local; write the expression (`alpha & 0x1f`) at each use. The value becomes one CSE object, and its number comes from where the CSE is created. That can be inside an inline expansion's band.
- **A checking inline form moves its local.** `if (m->res == NULL) return; res = m->res;` is the "checking" form; the plain form is `res = m->res; if (res == NULL) return;`. In the checking form `res` is a CSE of the two loads, not an inline local. Use whichever form fits at each call site.
- **A hand-inlined allocation keeps the result named.** `m = alloc(n); if (m != NULL) m = ctor(m);` assigns `m` more than once, so it stays a named object. A one-line helper inline would turn it into an inline temp.
- **Parameter types from the real SDK prototype matter.** `NNS_G2dGetAnimSequenceByIdx(void *, u16)` with `u16` inline index parameters keeps a `u16` loop counter as a named object. With `int`, it is replaced by a CSE of the extension.

### Matched

- `ov003_021d112c` (`src/ov003/ov003_021d112c.cpp`): the allocation is written out by hand (`m = func_0203dd9c(0xe8); if (m != NULL) m = func_ov000_0218fe1c(m);`). `func_ov000_02190a30(m, 3)` is called directly, not through the `GetAnm` inline. `long k2` is declared after `anm` and `m`. With `s32 k2` it is 121.
- `ov000_021688c4` (`src/ov000/Lo_021688c4.cpp`): the junk-free draft from round vphase was at 20. All three `PlayPart` sites use the checking form. The `a5` local is dropped, and each bit-field store reads `->alpha = alpha & 0x1f;`, which makes the CSE that round vphase needed inside the second expansion's band.
- `ov000_02176714` (`src/ov000/Lo_02176714.cpp`): from `vphase/6714/e1.cpp` (15). The `Items` loop is written out by hand in `case 1`. The table pointer is stored in the function's `VObj *o`, which is dead by then, so the table becomes a split-lifetime object below the `tbl[i].b` CSE. That is the first of the two exact moves round vphase found. The volatile accesses that e1 inherited still matter: without them it is 7.
- `ov003_021cd744` (`src/ov003/ov003_021cd744.cpp`): uses the real `u16` prototype above. `Ov003_Model_PlayPart` and `PlayPartChk` take `u16 idx` and `GetPart` takes `int idx`. The locals are `u16 i, count, mask`. The first call uses the plain form and the two loop calls use the checking form.

### Not matched

- `ov000_0217558c`: the junk-free draft (`vphase2/558c/z4.cpp`) is at **4**, all scheduling. It uses `x` again for `bx = xi + 0x5a` (split lifetime), declares `Model *m` first with a direct `Model_PlayPart(m, 1)`, and uses the checking form at the six later sites. In the first `SetPos` block, the ROM puts `mov r0, #0x18000` before `ldr r1, [r6, #0x5c]`. Fifteen variants of that block (statement order, temps, argument forms) did not change the order.

## Which source shapes make MWCC replace a local with an optimizer object: `func_020508f4` matches (round loopt)

Round cvcse found that where a compiler object takes a named local's place in the vreg graph, the creating call stack usually runs through `0x58fce4`, `0x58fdde` or `0x59b50b`, which round rgraph2 had filed as "loop passes". This round wrote toy files for each loop shape and logged, for every object, the phase that created it. One function matched from the rules (`func_020508f4`, 8 diffs to 0). The tools are in the scratchpad under `loopt/`:

- `tw.sh FILE` runs `lw.sh` and `cls.py`. It prints every vreg of the last function in the file with the phase that created its object: `named`, `inl-arg`, `inl-local`, `post-inl`, `LOOP58f-ce4`, `LOOP58f-dde`, `LOOP59b`, `LOOP561`, `CSE`, `split`, `?:`, and `param` for the parameters.
- `rd.sh FILE` dumps the last colour graph as `vreg reg obj`. With `PC=1` it also prints that function's pcode. `cc.sh FILE` prints the disassembly.
- `sc.py FUNC MOD FILES...` scores drafts four at a time. `dperm.py FILE FUNC MOD L1 L2 OUTDIR NAMES...` moves the declarations of `NAMES` (keeping their order) to every combination of positions inside lines `L1..L2` and scores each one.
- `re/` holds the cvcse `re2` tools, pointed at this clone (`an.sh` = match + dump + `want.py`). `ra.sh` now deletes the old `pcode_*.out` first, so a dump never mixes in files from an earlier, longer run.
- `scan.sh` runs `tw.sh` over every draft in `bfsweep/best1.txt`. `scan/summary.txt` lists the loop-pass objects in each one.

### The three object-making passes, and the spellings that avoid them

The global optimizer (`0x4f4a12`) creates objects in a fixed order: the `0x58f` pass, then `0x59b50b`, then CSE, then lifetime splitting. Objects created later get lower vreg numbers, so the band order from top to bottom is: named locals, inline objects, `58f` objects, `59b` objects, CSE objects, split lifetimes. In a toy with one of each, the numbers are `inline 24 > dde 23 > ce4 22 > 59b 21 > CSE 20`.

1. **`0x58fdde`: an assignment whose value is used.** Each of these creates a new object for the assigned value: `while ((c = F(&s)) != 0)`, `while (c = F())`, `if ((c = H()) > 3)`, `G(c = H())` and the chain `a->x = b->y = v`. The named local then has no node at all, or only a node for its other lifetimes. This is not a loop pass: it also does this outside loops. The same logic written as a separate statement keeps the named local. Examples are `c = F(&s); if (c == 0) break;`, the comma form `while (c = F(&s), c != 0)`, `for (c = F(&s); c != 0; c = F(&s))` and `do { c = F(&s); ... } while (c != 0)`.
2. **`0x58fce4`: a postfix `++`/`--` whose value is used, inside a loop.** `*dst++ = v`, `a[n++] = v`, `t = *p++`, `p++[0]` and `while (k--)` each create a new object for the variable. That object carries the variable through the whole function, including the assignments before and after the loop (`func_020508f4`'s `dst = line` outside the loop wrote the object). The same code as two statements, `*dst = v; dst++;`, keeps the named local, and it compiles to the same `strb rX, [rY], #1`. The prefix form `*++p` creates no object. A postfix value used outside a loop is folded and creates no object either. `p++` or `i++` as a statement of its own, including the third clause of a `for`, creates nothing.
3. **`0x59b50b`: loop-invariant code motion.** An invariant computation in the loop body is hoisted into a new object: `k * m`, `k + m`, `m << 3`, `1 << m`, and the promotion of a narrow invariant (`u16 mask` used in `mask & (1 << i)`, or a `u16`/`s16`/`u8` argument passed on as `int`). The same value computed into a named `int` local before the loop (`t = m << 3;`, `int mask = self->unk_66;`) stays a named local. Pointer plus constant (`b + 0x110`) is not hoisted, because it folds into the addressing mode, and neither are loads, because the loop may store or call.
4. **The loop test is duplicated, so an invariant in a `for`/`while` condition becomes CSE instead.** MWCC rotates `for` and `while` loops: a test at the top and a copy at the bottom. A `u16` bound converted to `int` (`i < k` with `u16 k`) or an expression (`i < n * 2`) therefore occurs twice and is merged by CSE. In a `do`/`while` loop the test occurs once, and the same bound is hoisted by `59b`. A named `int` local for the bound keeps it in the named block.

### Shapes that make no object

Toys of every one of these keep the locals named and create no loop object (`toy/c*`, `e*`, `g*`, `h*`, `i*`, `j*`, `o*`, `u*`, `x*`). There is no induction-variable strength reduction and no unrolling at `-O4,p`:

- counting up or down, and `<`, `<=`, `!=` or `>= 0` in the test;
- `int`, `u8` or `u16` counters (only conversions of invariants matter, above);
- `a[i]` indexing compared with a walking pointer (`p = a; ...; p++`). Each keeps its own variable, and `a[i].b` is recomputed as `i * 12` with `mla` in every iteration;
- `&a[i]` compared with `a + i`. The two give identical code. Either one used twice in an iteration becomes one CSE object. Assigned to a named pointer, it stays named;
- constant-trip loops (`for (k = 0; k < 4; k++)`). These stay loops.

### `func_020508f4` (8 to 0, `src/Main/Gfx/TextWin_14.cpp`)

The wrong pair was `dst` (the target puts it in `r5`) and `fn` (`r7`). `dst` was the `58fce4` object `@237` (vreg 31), created by `*dst++ = start[i];` in the inner copy loop, and so it was below every named local. Writing the copy as `*dst = start[i]; dst++;` puts `dst` back in the named block (36). That alone gives 9 diffs: `font` and `fn` are then swapped. The target needs the numbers ordered `dst > font > fn`, which means declaring them in that order. `dperm.py` over the 14 declarations found 286 orders that match. The file keeps the draft's order except that `dst` and `font` move up to just after `line` and `fn` moves down to just after `c`. The `goto test; do { ... test: if (*s == 0) break; } while (*s != 0);` shape stays, because a plain `while (*s != 0)` gives 20 diffs. The `while (start = s, (c = fn(&s)) != 0)` condition makes `c` a `58fdde` object (`@239`), and the target agrees with that.

### Applied to the other drafts

- `scan/summary.txt` shows which current best drafts contain these objects. Among the unmatched functions with 30 diffs or fewer, the only ones whose *wrong* nodes are `58f`/`59b` objects are `020508f4` (matched) and `ov003_021cd744`. In the others (`0203a984`, `02056e74`, `ov000_02171478`, `0218a670`, `ov011_021fc0b8`) the loop objects are dead by the final graph or already have the right register.
- **`ov003_021cd744` (28, not matched).** `mask` was the `59b` promotion of `u16 mask` (vreg 31). Declaring it `int` makes `mask` a named node (46), but the score goes to 35. A beam search (`gr.py`) on both graphs gives the same two-move answer: `mask` has to be numbered at 37.5 to 38.5, which is between the second `PlayPart` expansion's argument temp (`@65`) and its first local (`@66`). The second move is either the loop counter (CSE `@97`, 28) to the very bottom (the split band) or `self` to 28.5. No local or `59b`/CSE object lands inside an inline expansion's band. 100 type combinations for `mask`/`count`/`i`, every declaration order, wrapping the loop in an inline (with `mask` and `count` as locals or parameters), and giving `i` an earlier lifetime (`i = self->unk_5c;` before the first call) all score 28 or worse. The counter is a CSE object because every use of the `u16 i` is an `int` conversion. A toy with the same uses keeps `i` named, so the cause is still open.
- `0218a670` (12): its three `58fdde` objects are the `self->unk_11c = st->unk_18 = ...` chains. Splitting the chains, or the `lo`/`hi` chains, leaves the score at 12. The diffs are an instruction-order difference in cases 20 to 22 (the target stores `unk_0c[k] = 0` before the `pos[k]` stores), so they are not a register problem.
- Two other creators show up in the scans, and neither is a loop pass. `0x561ebb`/`0x5618bc` run under the same driver as `58f` (`0x4fedb6`) and walk expression trees recursively. They appear in functions with no loop at all (`02056e74`), and their objects were dead in every final graph checked. `0x5971a6` is called from the front end (`0x479xxx`), not from the global optimizer. ## How the instruction scheduler picks, and what it explains: no new match (round vphase3)

This round worked through the vphase2 leftovers and the PlayPart and NNS drafts. It also found how the mwccarm 1.3 instruction scheduler chooses its order, so a "scheduling only" difference can now be traced to the pcode list order that would give the ROM.

### The scheduler

- The list scheduler is at `0x50dce0`, which calls `0x50db70` once per basic block. It runs before register allocation and again after it (the call at `0x474e9b`). The machine model issues one instruction at a time.
- It builds a dependency graph by walking the block backwards. Each node stores its latency, ready cycle, height, deadline (largest height minus its own) and its count of predecessors. Ties are always broken by the block's list order, which is the order the pcode was generated in.
- The pick is at `0x50d9b0`. Before allocation a register-pressure flag is set (`0x65bb9c`). When that flag is set and the live count reaches 14, the scheduler takes the node with the lowest pressure score (`0x50ce40`): last uses make the score lower and new definitions make it higher. Otherwise it takes an urgent node first (deadline reached), then the one that frees more successors, then the greater height.
- The live count starts from the values live into the block, adds every definition and subtracts last uses. Definitions of physical registers (argument registers, call clobbers) only drop at their final use in the block, so a long block with many calls stays in pressure mode and keeps roughly source order. That is the "seven or more calls" effect from earlier rounds.
- Memory operations keep their order against volatile stores and against stores to locals whose address is taken.
- Tools (scratchpad `vphase3/sch/`): `sd4.sh FILE` dumps each block's input list, graph, every pick and the output. `mv.sh FILE SPEC OUT.o` moves pcode instructions (lines `src => dst`, move src right after dst) at scheduler entry, before or after allocation according to the vreg names used, so a target order can be tested without touching the source.

### What it showed

- `ov000_0217558c` (4): the ROM order is the normal-mode schedule. Ours is in pressure mode (live count 56 in an 87-instruction block that starts after `PlayPart(m, 1)`). Any real branch after the `0x340` text pair splits the block and gives the ROM order for the `SetPos` code. No construct that emits no code splits it: labels, `goto`, `do {} while (0)`, `switch (0)`, `if (1)`, an empty `if`, an inline with a constant-parameter `if`, an empty `for` and inline wrappers were all tried.
- `ov000_0219b808` (4): moving the `q->unk_30` load right after the `rot.x` load gives the exact schedule before allocation. The allocator then swaps `ip` and `lr`. Fixing that needs the load to get its vreg after `z`, but generating it there makes it depend on the `m` stores. The 119 inline parameter orders and the body variants did not do it.
- `ov014_02205634` (3): after allocation the registers already match. Only the `unk_84.x` store is in the wrong place. Moving that store anywhere before the `SQRTCNT`/`SQRT_PARAM` stores in the post-allocation list gives 0. Every pre-allocation list order tried (30 single moves, 18 store orders and 9 positions in the source) changes the other picks too.
- `ov009_02206084` (7): the ROM loads `pl->id` before the flag byte and stores it first. Writing `unk_90 = pl->id` before `unk_93_4 = 1` gets that order but changes the allocation of the next block (14).
- `ov000_02166180` (45): single moves at gaps between neighbouring nodes (`re/sw2.py`) and a beam search (`re/bm.py`) only reach 14 wrong nodes after four moves, from 21. Spelling variants were 45 or worse.
- `ov000_0214dd3c`: the plain-`Key` draft (70) reaches 2 wrong nodes once the first key is moved into the CSE band, but neither the beam search nor any spelling got past that. The `g[1]` draft is still the best at 28.
- PlayPart checking form and real `u16` prototypes: `ov000_021512b4` (34) and `ov000_02152f8c` (13) did not change.

## Source shapes that change how a block is scheduled: `ov014_02205634` and `func_0206e3a0` match (round sched)

This round looked for source constructs that change a block's scheduling without changing its code. The list scheduler (`0x50dce0`, round vphase3) runs twice. The first run is before register allocation, with the register-pressure flag set. The second run is after allocation, in normal mode. After the first run every block gets flag bit 8 ("already scheduled"). The second run only schedules blocks that have at least two instructions and do not have bit 8 set (it also skips blocks whose flags `& 0x11b` are set). So most blocks keep their pre-allocation order. A block gets a second, normal-mode schedule only when something clears bit 8 between the two runs. Three things do that:

- The allocator deletes a coalesced copy (`mov vA, vB` where both get the same register) from the block. The call is `0x5272b0` at `0x474cdf`; the instruction removal at `0x504b30` clears the bit.
- The branch optimizer (`0x5135b0`, through `0x512870`) deletes a branch to the next block.
- Two blocks are merged (`0x5116d0`, then `0x505060`). Block A merges into B when A's only successor is B, B's only predecessor is A, both have the same `& 0x111`/`& 0x112` flags and the same loop depth (byte `+0x2c`), and A's last instruction allows it. A call (instruction flags `& 8`) or a volatile memory access (`& 0x180`) at the end of A stops the merge. A branch at the end of A only merges if it goes to B.

So a scheduling-only miss is often a block that was rescheduled when the ROM's was not, or the other way round. Scratchpad tools (`sched/sch/`): `pb.sh SRC OUT.o post N` clears bit 8 on block `N` before the second run, and `pb.sh SRC OUT.o pre N` runs block `N` in normal mode before allocation. `pbscan.sh` tries every block in both modes and scores each result. A 0 from it names the block whose mode is wrong; the source then needs a lever that makes the same change.

### Matched

- `ov014_02205634` (was 3, now 0, new `src/ov014/ov014_02205634.cpp`). Forcing a post-allocation reschedule of the loop preheader gives the ROM. That block ends with the `SQRT_PARAM` store. Our draft wrote it through `vu64`, so the block's last instruction was volatile and could not merge with the `b` into the loop. The SDK's `CP_SetSqrt64` writes the parameter through a plain `u64 *`. With that spelling the block merges, bit 8 is cleared, and the second schedule moves `unk_84.x` before the `SQRTCNT` store as in the ROM. The stores stay in source order (`x`, `y`, `z`, then the sqrt).
- `func_0206e3a0` (was 2, now 0, new `src/Main/Lang/LangData_5.cpp`). Passing the cached `env` fields to `G3X_SetFog` produced a copy that the allocator coalesced and deleted. That cleared bit 8, so the block was rescheduled after allocation. The ROM keeps the pre-allocation order. Reading the same halfwords straight from the source pointer (`*(const u16 *)(p + 6)`, `*(const u16 *)(p + 4)`) removes the copy, and the block keeps its first schedule.

### Not matched, with the cause found

- `ov000_0217558c` (4): in the ROM the text part of the block is in pressure mode and was never rescheduled, while the `SetPos` part is in normal mode. We need a block boundary right after a call (a call ends a block that can never merge). An `if` with a real test, such as `if ((u32)&c & 3) xi = x >> 12;`, splits the block before allocation. But it ends in `tst`/`beq` and the branch optimizer merges it back. The merged block is then rescheduled and the text calls move (22). The ROM also wants `mov r0, #0x18000` before the `ldr` (a moved-pcode test gives 0). Leaving the text loop not unrolled gives 362.
- `ov000_0219b808` (4): the `q->unk_30` load has to come right after `rot.x`, and its vreg must have a higher number than `rot.z`'s. Of two vregs that compete for registers, the one with the higher number gets the lower register. Swapping vregs 115 and 118 and moving the load gives 0. Locals, inline forms and CSE spellings all stay at 4, 12 or 46.
- `func_0205c234` (2): loading after `args[3]` (non-volatile) leaves the address `ldr` one slot late. It is a tie between `strh` (class 1) and the next op (class 0).
- `func_0205e5c4` (2): stores to the same global through a literal address keep their order. Stores through a pointer base at different offsets do not. Swapping the `unk_14`/`unk_04` stores changes the allocation (6 to 15). All 36 placements and 120 permutations were tried, and the best was 6.
- `pbscan.sh` was run on the 24 best unmatched drafts with 1 to 12 raw differences, including `ov000_02171478`, `ov010_02200a00`, `ov009_02206084`, `ov000_021b3e90`, `func_0205c234`, `func_0205e5c4`, `func_02056e74` and `ov000_0219b808`. It forced each block, one at a time, into a post-allocation reschedule or a normal-mode first schedule. No function reached 0, and none improved on its base score. Their misses come from list order or register allocation, not from block mode. So the two levers above (removing a coalesced copy, and making a block's last store non-volatile so it can merge) are the only ones found this round.

## SDK inline forms in the unmatched drafts: `func_02068e68` matches (round sdkf)

This round went through the best draft of every unmatched function. It looked for hardware and SDK accesses: `REG_*` and raw `0x04xxxxxx` registers, DIV/SQRT/CP, G3 commands (direct or through `NNS_G3dGeBufferOP_N`), `MI_Cpu*`, `OS_*` IRQ/lock calls and DMA. Scratchpad: `sdkf/` (`scan.py` lists the bl targets and I/O literals of each unmatched function's target, `diffs.txt` has the first mismatching lines of every best draft at 30 or less, and `conv/` has a converter from the game-style `G3_Cmd1`/`G3_Vec` wrappers to `NNS_G3dGe*` forms).

This is the particle draw: `TexImageParam`/`TexPlttBase`, `PolygonAttr`, `MtxMode`, `PushMtx`, `Translate`, rotation by `MTX_Rot*33`/`MTX_Concat33`, `Scale`, `Color`, `SendDL`, `PopMtx`. The old draft hand-rolled every command as `NNS_G3dGeBufferOP_N(op, &local, n)` with function-level locals. It also needed a `(u32)p & 3` hack to keep `FX_SinCosTable_` in a register for the Y/Z rotations. The rewrite uses the NitroSystem inline forms (`nnsys/g3d.h`): `NNS_G3dGeMtxMode`/`NNS_G3dGePopMtx` pass the address of their own parameter, and `NNS_G3dGePolygonAttr`/`TexPlttBase`/`Color` each pack into their own temporary. It also uses `FX_SinIdx`/`FX_CosIdx` and `MTX_RotX33`/`Y33`/`Z33`. With these forms, and no hack, the register allocation matched the ROM at once: the constant `1` sits in `r5` and `type` in `r4`, and MWCC CSEs the table address for the Y/Z rotations by itself. Three things then fixed the stack slots and the load order:

With `NNS_G3dGeTranslate(x, y, z)` (an inline-local vector) the vector slots land below the matrices.

So the `else` branch writes its constant through a plain block local (`u32 texParam = 0x21200000;`) and not through `NNS_G3dGeTexImageParam`. Block locals rank with the function's own locals, above the inline temporaries.
