## The scheduler's pressure score, and a return value that sits in its own block: no new match (round nmZ)

No new match. Scratch files are in `scratchpad/nmZ/` (`ms.py` for this clone, `t/` the hzU pass dumper with `marks_main.txt` as `marks.txt` so it also dumps the passes after "move constant loads", `sch/` the bigN `sd7.sh`/`st.sh`/`tr.sh`, `640c/` and `ca14/` the variants).

### The pressure score (`0x50ce40`, mwccarm `dsi/1.3`)

The score starts at `0x10`. For each operand that is a use, the remaining-use counter of that register (`0x636868[class][reg]`) goes down by one; if it reaches 0 (a last use) the score goes down. For each operand that is a def (and not also a use) of a register whose remaining-use counter is not 0, the score goes up by `0x636878[class] − 0x636870[class]`. A def whose value has no use left in the block costs nothing. Registers marked kind 2 in `0x65af58` are skipped. Every call (`op157`) lists `r0`–`r3` as operands, so an argument register always has a later use in a block that contains another call: `mov r2, #0` for an argument costs exactly as much as a load, and the tie goes to list order.

### `ov010_0220640c` (6 / 2)

- The pre-allocation list of case 0 is `ldrh 0x98; ldrh 0x7e; …; stores; mov r0, #0x1e000; mov r1, v39; mov r2, #0; bl`. In pressure mode (live 20, limit 14) `mov r1, v39` goes first because it is the last use of the `1` register, then the `0x98` load wins the tie with `mov r2, #0` by list order. The ROM's `mov r1, r4; mov r2, #0` before both loads needs `mov r2, #0` listed before the loads or cheaper than them, and by the score above it is only cheaper if `r2` had no later use in the block, which the following calls rule out.
- Passing the inline's result as any of the three arguments (`f(0x1e000, 1, Jump(self))` returning 0, `f(0x1e000, Jump(self), 0)` returning 1, `f(Jump(self), 1, 0)` returning `0x1e000`) gives the same list: argument moves are always emitted at the call (6 / 2 each).
- So the ROM's `0` is not a fresh argument constant in the same block as the loads in our sense. It would have to be a value defined earlier in the block and coalesced into `r2` (a vreg holding `0` whose only use is that argument), and nothing in the case-0 source before the jump uses a `0`. Still open.

### `ov002_021eca14` (7 / 2): the `return TRUE` was its own block

- The masked misses are the case-1 tail: the ROM has `0x1f` in `r0`, the pointer and `v` in `r1`, and `mov r0, #1` after both stores. In ours the pre-allocation scheduler fills the `ldrh` latency slot (cycle 3) with `mov r0, #1`, because codegen emits `v0 = 1` in the same block as the stores, so `r0` is defined while `0x1f` is live and `0x1f` cannot get `r0`.
- `goto done; … return FALSE; done: return TRUE;` (the `ca14/r5.cpp` form) puts `v0 = 1` in a block of its own, and then the whole case-1 tail gets the ROM's registers and order exactly (`ldr r1; mov r0, #0x1f; ldrh r1; strb r0; str r1`). The score is 10 / 10 only because that block is laid out after the `return FALSE` block (`b` plus a second `mov r0, #1; pop`). Every form that puts the `return TRUE` right after the stores in source (`t1`: `goto fail` for the false paths and `return TRUE` after the `switch`; `if (0) { done: … }`; an inline returning `TRUE`; a block-local `BOOL r`; `s1`/`s2`: the `||`/`&&` forms of the `0x38` test) is merged with the stores block before scheduling and gives 7 / 2 again. A duplicated store sequence in both arms of the `0x38` test (for tail merging) is 28 / 21.
- So the ROM's source has a `return TRUE` block that is still separate when the first scheduler runs (more than one predecessor, or not adjacent at the first block merge) but is laid out directly after the stores. Which construct does that is the open question; the merge passes (`merge0`, `0x5135b0`, `0x52ad70`) are the place to trace next.

### `ov000_021b3e90` (7 / 1)

One shape tried: the `unk_d6 - 1 != unk_d4` exit as `if (…) { b6 = 0; } else { b6 = 1; … switch … }` with the single `return ret` at the end (`3e90/n1.cpp`) is 15 / 6: the false arm becomes a predicated `ldrbne/bicne/strbne; bne` to the shared exit, so the head merge of the `0x9c` load is lost too. Also wrapping the rest in `if (cam != NULL)` is 35 / 27.

  | compiler | 021763c8 | 0217a26c | 0217bd88 | 0217e9c8 | total |

In `021764c4` it forwards the stored `s8` into `subs r0, r0, #1` where the ROM stores it and reloads it (`sub`; `strb`; `ldrsb`; `cmp`), which is the store-forwarding difference that splits NitroSystem (`dsi/1.1`) from the game code.
- **The two blockers, in the pooled `menu/m1.cpp`.** `0217b324` is 45 / 14 (masked) under every `dsi` build, `dsi/1.1` and `dsi/1.6` included, 191 / 124 under every `2.0` build and 427 / 281 or worse under `1.2`. No version changes its register choice, so the spT/spW explanation (four pool values that must not be rematerialised) is not a version effect. `0217a1f8` is 0 under `1.2/sp3`/`sp4`, 3 under every `2.0` and `dsi` build, 5 under `1.2/base`..`sp2p3` and 9 under `1.2/b56`. No compiler matches both, and no compiler that matches `0217a1f8` keeps the TU.
- **What "the rest of the TU rules out `1.2/sp4`" means.** Under `1.2/sp4`, 91 of the 115 matched functions differ from the ROM (24 still match). Masked by register, most differences are large: `0217ef3c` 291, `0217df5c` 242, `0217d66c` 191, `02176714` 159, `0217c7b8` 153, `0217d0c4` 111, `0217adfc` 109, `0217a480` 107. The small ones show what is missing from that compiler, and none of them is a source spelling:
  - `0217bfe4` (1): `ands r0, r0, #0x10000` where the ROM has `tst` (the `dsi` peephole that drops an unused `ands` result).
  - `02178100` (2): the tail call's `ldr ip, =func` is scheduled before the `ldr r0, [r0, #8]` instead of after it.
  - `0217ad54` (2): `mov r3, #0` is placed after the `0x1000` store instead of at entry (the "move constant loads" pass, round hzU).
  - `0217a480`: the ROM's `mov r1, #0x79; mov r0, r7; sub r2, r1, #0x7a` for `func_ov000_0217a328(self, 0x79, -1)` is the `dsi`/`2.0` constant derivation (round cderiv). `1.2/sp4` gives `mvn r2, #0` there. That is the same instruction `0217a1f8` wants, and it is why `0217a1f8` matches under `1.2/sp4`: that compiler never derives constants. The two calls are the same shape (`(self, 0x78, -1)` in `0217a1f8`, `(self, 0x79, -1)` in `0217a480`), so one compiler can't produce both. Since `0217a1f8` sits between functions that load from the same string pool, it is in the same TU and can't have a version of its own.
  So the `1.2/sp4` result for `0217a1f8` is a side effect of a missing optimisation, not evidence of another build. No header inline form can turn `ands` into `tst`, move a scheduled `ldr`, or take the derivation out of `0217a480`.

For `0217a1f8` that means a `-1` that is not derived from the `0x78` in the same extended block, and for `0217b324` pool values that are not rematerialised. Changing the compiler fixes neither.

## Block merging, branch tail merge and a coalesced zero: no new match (round mgW)

No new match. Scratch files are in the scratchpad under `mgW/` (nmZ's `ms.py`, `t/` and `sch/` pointed at the mgW clone; `rd.py LO HI OV` disassembles a target range with branch targets; `ca14/gen.py` writes the `m*`/`g*` variants; `3e90/v*.cpp` the `021b3e90` variants).

### Merge 0 (`0x5116d0` and its test `0x504fa0`), exactly

For each block B in layout order, with P its layout predecessor (`B+4`): B is merged into P when P's layout successor is B, P has exactly one successor edge and it goes to B, B has exactly one predecessor edge, `P.flags & 0x111` and `B.flags & 0x112` are 0, the loop depths (`+0x2c`) are equal, and P's last instruction is not a call (`& 8`) or a volatile access (`& 0x180`); a last instruction that is a branch is allowed only if it jumps to B. The only writers of block flags `0x10` and `0x100` (`0x52b04b`, `0x52c50f`) run after scheduling, so before the first scheduler a source label only survives as a block boundary if it is **not laid out directly after its only predecessor, or has two or more predecessors**. That is why `ca14/t3.cpp` (`if (0) { done: return TRUE; }`, laid out straight after the stores) merges again and `r5.cpp` (`done:` after `return FALSE`) does not.

### No layout or jump clean-up after the branch tail merge

The branch tail merge (`0x52ad70`, a fixed-point loop over `0x52acd0` per block) runs after both schedulers. Tested on `021eca14` with the case-1 stores written twice (`ca14/m1`–`m7`, `g1`, `g2`):

- When two predecessors of the `return TRUE` join end with the same instructions, the copy that **falls through** into the join is kept and the other one is replaced by a `b` to it (`m1`/`m5`: the `p38 != NULL` arm becomes `b`; `m2`/`m6`/`m7`: the `p38 == NULL` arm does). With the copy laid out after the join (`g1`, by `goto`), the copy before the join is kept.
- The block left holding only that `b` is **never removed**, a conditional branch to it is not retargeted, and a `b` to the next instruction stays (`m5` ends `beq FALSE; b +4; stores`).
- In every variant each stores copy sits in a block without `mov r0, #1`, so the stores come out in exactly the ROM's registers and order; the score is 8 / 8 or 9 / 9 because of that one leftover `b` (and the `bne +8; b` pair where the leftover copy was the then-arm).

So the ROM's case-1 tail cannot come from a tail-merged duplicate either: that always leaves a branch the ROM does not have. Together with merge 0 above, the ROM needs a `return TRUE` block that is laid out right after the stores and has a second predecessor at merge 0 which leaves no instruction behind (a conditional branch removed or if-converted between merge 0 and the end). No source construct that does that was found. `021eca14` stays at 7 / 2 (`t1`/`c.cpp`); `r5` (10 / 10) and `m5` (9 / 9) are the forms with the right case-1 code.

### `ov000_021b3e90` (7 / 1): the target's `mov r0, r4` is `dp = 0`, head-merged

- The draft never initialises `dp` (it is read when neither key bit is set). The target's `r0` at the switch is 0: `dp` is `u16 dp = 0` semantics, and it lives in `r0` from the `d6 - 1 != d4` exit to the `if (dp != 0)` test.
- `dp = 0;` written just before the `d6 - 1 != d4` test (`3e90/vg.cpp`; also `return FALSE` or `return dp` in the exit, `vh`/`vi`/`vl`) gives **8 / 2 with every register as in the target**: the exit's `mov r0, #0` is a local-CSE copy of `dp`, so `dp` is coalesced into `r0`. The only miss is that `mov r0, r4` is in the compare block, and the pre-RA scheduler puts it in the `ldrh` latency slot.
- In the target it comes after `cmp` and after the `ldrb [r6, #0x9c]`, i.e. it is the second instruction head-merged (`0x5135b0`) from both successors: the exit block starts `ldrb r1; mov r0, r4` and the continue block `ldrb r1; mov r0, r4 (dp = 0)`. That needs `dp = 0` at the start of the continue block **and** `dp` coloured `r0`. With `dp = 0` in the continue block (`va`, `vb`, `vc`, `vj`, `vk`, `vm`–`vr`, every declaration order, `s32`/`u32`/`int`/`s16` types) nothing copies `dp` into `r0`, it gets `r2`, the `0x9c` value takes `r0`, and the score is 42 / 26 or worse. Still open: what gives `dp` a preference for `r0` when its definition is after the exit.

## Where MWCC derives constants, traced in the compiler: no new match (round cdZ)

No new match, and no source or `tools/` change. Scratch tools are in `scratchpad/cdZ/t/`: `dv2.sh FILE OUT` logs every derivation attempt (each candidate constant, every `K` in the table with its attributes, and the result of the builder), plus the return value of the store-load pass; `st.sh FILE OUT` logs only that return value, per function; `ph.sh` is round hzU's pass dumper pointed at this clone (`marks_main.txt` is now its `marks.txt`). Toys are in `scratchpad/cdZ/toy/`.

### The pass (mwccarm `dsi/1.3`)

- **Derivation is part of local CSE, in its last pre-allocation run** (`0x514b50(0)`, called from `0x474fc4`, between "CSE after code motion" and the copy propagation pass at `0x474bef`). The earlier CSE runs see the generic `op27` constants and derive nothing. Lowering (`0x521dd0`) turns them into `op171`, and this run is the first to see those. Round hzU's dump showed the change at `0x474bf4` only because the code between the marks jumps out to `0x474fc2` and back.
- `0x523d70` (the pass right after, run through the dataflow framework `0x5b0530` with descriptor `0x61746a`) is global copy and constant propagation into uses. It does not derive.
- **The table.** The CSE walks extended blocks (`0x514a70`: a block, then each successor that has only that block as predecessor, saving and restoring the table at each branch). Each constant instruction (`op171`, or `op548`) is first looked up for an identical one (`0x513f00`: then it becomes a copy). If there is none, `0x514140` walks the hash list for **the same opcode** (`0x636d44[op]`, newest first). A table entry `K` qualifies only if some register still holds its value (the holder list at `+4`; redefining the register removes it), the vreg map still points to it, and it has the same condition byte `+0x2a`, the same `+0x2b`, the same flag words `+0xc`/`+0x10` and the same operand count. The first `K` for which `0x510d40` builds an instruction wins. The original is removed and the derived instruction is entered under its own opcode (`sub` is `op287`), so it is never a `K` later.
- **What gets built (`0x510d40`, ARM path).** Nothing if the new constant is `mov`-encodable (`0x5101c0`). Otherwise, in this order: `sub new, K, #(K-new)`; `add new, K, #(new-K)`; `mov new, K, lsl #n` for `new == K << n` (n = 1..24); `lsr #n`; `asr #n`; `bic new, K, #(K^new)` when `new` is `K` with bits cleared; `rsb new, K, #(K+new)`. The shift forms are real: `g(p, 0x1ff, 0x3fe)` gives `ldr r1, =0x1ff; lsl r2, r1, #1`, and `g(p, 0x12345, 0x91a2)` gives `lsr r2, r1, #1` (`toy/k.c`). Round cderiv's "never a shift" only holds for its examples, where the new constant is not a shifted copy of `K`.
- **The loop refusal (`0x511570`).** If the function has loops at all (`0x65e27c`) and `K` is a `mov`-encodable constant (`0x5113e0`), the builder refuses whenever **`K`'s block or the new constant's block** is a block of any loop (`0x515880` walks the loop tree and the callback `0x511540` compares blocks). A loop elsewhere in the function changes nothing (`toy/g.c`: a loop before or after the call, or in the other arm, still derives). This is the exact form of round cderiv's "loop headers end the scope" and "hoisted constants are never derived".
- **Who can be a `K` (`0x510410`).** A `mov`-encodable `op171` whose destination is already a physical register is never entered. Coalescing before this CSE would therefore stop derivation for the whole function. The only coalesce that runs on lowered code before it (`0x474ba3`) runs only when the memory store-load pass `0x5221f0` changes something, and that pass returned 0 for every function in `Menu_021763c8`, `Menu_0217bd88`, `Menu_0217e9c8` and for every toy tried (stores and reloads through pointers, local arrays and structs, address-taken locals). So that path is not the lever in this code.
- **What does not count.** Types (`s16`, `s8`, pointer, `long long` arguments) and stores to `int`, `short` or `char` all give the same attribute words (`c=4000 10=40000000 2a=e 2b=0`). Calls between `K` and the new constant do not remove `K` (its holder is a vreg). A float `FX32_CONST(...)` is folded before codegen and derives the same way (`toy/h.c`).

### The targets

So a constant that is not derived although the difference is encodable means one of these: (1) `K` is not in the same extended block (a join between them, or `K` evaluated after it); (2) `K` or the new constant sits in a loop block; (3) every register holding `K` was redefined in between; (4) a different opcode or attribute word; (5) `K` was built straight into a physical register.

- **`ov000_0217a1f8` (3).** `0x78` and `-1` are built in the same block, one after the other, with equal attributes (`dv2` on the draft). The function has no loop and no join between them, and no natural form found changes the opcode or attributes. So none of (1)–(5) applies to any natural source tried, and the ROM's `mvn r2, #0` is still unexplained. One thing is now known: with derivation refused, the list order is `mov r0, r4; mov r1, #0x78; mvn r2, #0`. That is the ROM order, and it is what `1.2/sp4` produces. So the target needs only the refusal, not a different argument order. That rules out the reversed-evaluation explanations (`?:`, stack arguments), because they change the list. A `NULL` check of the creator written as a reload (`if (!X->f18) X->f18 = f; o = X->f18();`) keeps the reload in the output (15 diffs), so the ROM's source keeps the function pointer in a local, as the draft does.
- **`ov009_02208b24`.** Without round near4's `lim` two-definition local (junk), `0x19a` is built as `add r1, r4, #0x134` from the argument `0x66`, which stays in `r4` across both calls (84 diffs). The ROM loads `0x19a` from the pool after the calls. By the rule, the ROM's source has a join, a loop block, or a redefinition of `0x66`'s register between `VEC_MultAdd(0x66, ...)` and the `<= 0x19a` test, and the target shows no branch there. The call boundaries do not do it. Not solved.
- **`02049c80`.** Not reworked this round. Its `sub r0, r5, #1` returns are ordinary derivations from the zero in `r5`. With the rule above, the fresh `mvnhs r0, #0` on the `slot >= 5` path needs that block to be outside the zero's extended block, or the zero to be in a loop block. That fits round mainI's reading (`r4` is a variable, not the constant).

## One variable for the key delta and the new pitch: `ov000_021b3e90` matches (round mgX)

`ov000_021b3e90` matches and is now `src/ov000/Cam_021b3e90.cpp` (a new `complete` entry `0x021b3e90`..`0x021b4130` in ov000's `delinks.txt`). ### `ov000_021b3e90`: what colours `dp` `r0`

- The source writes `dp = 0;` at the start of the continue block (after `cam->unk_9c.b6 = 1;`, as mgW's `va.cpp`) **and uses `dp` itself for the new pitch**: `dp += cam->pitch; if (dp > 0x8000) { … t = 0x10000 - dp; … } else if (dp > 0x2800) { dp = 0x2800; } cam->unk_f8 = dp;`. mgW's drafts had a separate `u16 p = dp + cam->pitch`.
- Why it works, in the colouring model (`re/sim3.py`): `simplify` pushes every node with degree below 14 in ascending number order, so those are coloured in descending number order, and named locals are numbered below every temp. With a separate `p`, `dp` (node 50 in `va.cpp`) has only 12 neighbours, is pushed in the first sweep and is coloured after all the temps. The `0x9c` load and the case-0 temps take `r0` and `r1` first, so `dp` gets `r2` (42 / 26). With `p` merged into `dp`, its live range runs through the `0x8000` block and it has 23 neighbours (node 49 in `x1.cpp`). It goes onto the high list and is pushed in a later sweep, so it is coloured second, right after `ret` (`r4`) and before `dy`, `cam`, `self` and every temp, and takes `r0`. Then both successors of the `d6 - 1 != d4` test start `ldrb r1, [r6, #0x9c]; mov r0, r4`, the post-RA head merge lifts both instructions above the predicated exit, and the whole function matches.
- The general lever: **a named local is coloured before the temps only when its degree is at least 14 when `simplify` reaches it.** Two short-lived locals written as one longer-lived variable (the "reuse the variable" style) is one natural way to get there. Declaration order and types cannot do it, because they only renumber the local inside the object band.
- The old draft never set `dp` on the path where neither key bit is set. The match sets it in the continue block, which is what the target does.

## The LICM limit is an all-or-nothing gate on outermost loops: no new match (round lcA)

No new match. Tools are round hzY's, pointed at the lcA clone, in the scratchpad under `lcA/t/`. New: `lg.sh FILE OUT` prints, for every loop that loop-invariant code motion visits, its blocks, its child loop, its weight and (when it is checked) the instruction count and the verdict; `DET=1` also lists each counted instruction. `wt.sh` (`VREG=n`) watches one constant instruction's list links and prints the call stack of whatever moves it.

### Where LICM really is (mwccarm `dsi/1.3`)

Round hzU placed LICM inside the second `0x514b50` call. It is not there. When the loop analysis `0x517220(1)` returns non-zero, the driver jumps to `0x474f62`, which calls **`0x5196b0`** before coming back to the `AFTER LOCAL LOOP INVARIANT CODE MOTION` dump. (The `0x514b50` dump only looks like the place because the `0x474f62` detour sits between the two dumps.) `0x5196b0` walks the loop tree children-first (`0x519680`) and runs `0x5194f0` on each loop. That function moves invariant instructions to the loop's preheader (`0x5175a0` classifies each instruction, and `0x5184b0`/`0x5186c0` move it), and repeats until nothing changes. `0x5193a0` runs a second time over the same tree, because option `0x65ecad` is 0 under the game flags.

### The gate (`0x5a2540`)

Before any motion, `0x5194f0` asks `0x5a2540(loop)` whether the loop may be touched:

- A loop with **no child loop** is always processed.
- A loop with weight `+0x50` **above 8** is always processed. The weight is 8 per nesting level (8 for an outermost loop, 64 for a loop inside it), so any loop nested inside another loop always passes.
- Otherwise (an **outermost loop that contains another loop**), it counts the instructions in every block of the loop, inner loops included. It skips instructions with flag `0x10` (branches) and the rematerialisable constant ops of `0x50fcd0` (`mov #k`, pool address loads). If the count is **above 32**, the whole loop is skipped. Nothing at all moves out of it.

So there is no partial LICM inside one loop. hzU's `t3` "partial" case is two loops: the inner `j` loop (no child, always processed) moves its own `0`/`-1` into its own preheader, and the outer loop is refused as a whole (`t3v`: count 34/38). `f3`-style toys with a small outer body (count 7–9) move everything out of both loops. `toy/th*.c` confirms the threshold. With N statements `q[k] = p[2k] + p[2k+1]` plus `g(p, 77)` and an inner `h(j)` loop, the counts are 4N+7 on the first pass and 4N+9 on the second. At N=5 (27/29) `#0x4d` is hoisted. At N=6 (31/33) the first pass hoists `#0x4d`, but the second is refused, so the `q` pool load stays in the loop. At N=7 (35/37) `#0x4d` is built inside the loop.

### Applied to the two LICM targets

- **`func_020417e0`.** The outer `i` loop contains the `ClearEntry` `j` loop, and counts **65** on the first pass and 74 on the second (20 loads, 10 adds, 7 stores, 6 calls, ...). That is far above 32. The ROM's loop body is the same size, so the ROM's outer loop was refused as well. The target's `NULL` in preheader 34 therefore comes from step 4 ("move constant loads"), not from LICM, and the open question is only why the ROM's step 4 stops at 34 (`34->5`, block 5 `p=6` here). Dropping the inner loop (`d17/noclear.cpp`) only works because the outer loop then has no child and skips the count. It moves every constant out, which the target does not.
- **`ov011_021fd638`.** The outer `while (n != NULL)` loop contains the `Ov011Ent_Remove` loop and counts **37** (44 on the second pass), so it is refused. The inner loop is blocks `[14, 10]` and has no constants. The `e->unk_08 = 0` store is in block 13, the `break` path, which is outside the inner loop. So the target's inner-preheader `mov r7, #0` cannot be LICM output either. An accepted outer loop would have moved it out of the `while` loop altogether. As in `020417e0`, the fix has to come from step 4 refusing `82->9`, which needs block 9 above 10 (it is 8).
- **General rule for drafts:** a constant built inside an outermost loop that has an inner loop is moved by LICM only if the outer loop has 32 or fewer non-constant, non-branch instructions. Below that, everything invariant goes to the preheader. Above it, nothing does, and only step 4 can move it.

### `ov015_021fc40c`: what merges `Bob`'s `return 0`

The ph dumps of `hzY/c40c/y1.cpp` show this. At codegen, each case's `n < 5` block holds `mov v106, #0; mov v85, v106` (`Bob`'s result). After the **first local CSE** (`0x514b50` mode 0, extended-block scope), it is `mov v106, v96; mov v85, v96`, a copy of the entry zero. The `n < 5` block has a single predecessor, so it belongs to the extended block that starts at the entry and runs through the switch compare and the case block, and the zero is still available there. 32 zero instructions at codegen become 17 after this pass. So the merge happens in step 2, before LICM, coalescing and step 4. Keeping it separate needs either a join in front of `Bob`'s zero block (two predecessors), or no live zero earlier in that extended block. The case's own `SetV(&a, ..., 0)` already supplies one, so removing the entry `flip = FALSE` alone cannot do it.

The `Bob` spellings tried all keep the merge and all score the same as `y1` (141 / 58): a result variable with an `if`/`else if` chain (`vA`), `r = 0` first with nested tests (`vB`), `else if` returns (`vC`), a nested `?:` (`vD`), an `int` return (`vE`) and a `u32` return (`vF`). Reversing the tests so that `return 0` comes last (`vG`) is worse (170 / 85). None of them puts `Bob`'s zero after a join, and so far no natural `Bob` does. Still open.

## What makes the store-load pass fire, and why `0217a1f8` still can't use it: no new match (round cdB)

No new match, and no source or `tools/` change. Scratch tools are in `scratchpad/cdB/t/` (round cdZ's `st.sh`/`dv2.sh`/`ph.sh` pointed at this clone, plus `map.py OBJ PH`, which names the functions in an `st.sh` log by section order, and `sc.py`, a rough diff count against `rd.py` output). Toys are in `scratchpad/cdB/toy/`, and the whole-tree scan is in `scratchpad/cdB/scan/`.

### When `0x5221f0` returns nonzero

- **Scan.** `st.sh` over all 2013 source files (6534 functions) finds the pass changing something in only 7 files: `Main/Res/Stage.cpp` (`func_020590e8`, `func_0205c234`), `ov000/Sprite_021c8408.cpp`, `ov000/Stub_021c6140.cpp`, `ov000/Unit_0218b700.cpp` (`func_ov000_0218b7c0`), `ov002/ov002_021ddf18.cpp`, `ov006/ov006_021db258.cpp` and four functions in `ov013/ov013_02200fe8.cpp`. So this is rare in the game's code.
- **The memory objects it looks at.** `0x515e20` collects one entry per memory object referenced by a load or store (instruction flags `0x60006`, object at `+0x1c`). A struct object is split into its members (`0x515dd0`). The pass then works only on those objects.
- **Patterns that fire (toys `s2.c`..`s10.c`):**
  - **A scalar global stored on one path and reloaded after the join.** `G = x; if (x > 3) G = 0; return G;` and `if (GF == 0) GF = mk; return GF();` (the `0x5c234` shape: `StageRes_Last()` rereads `data_02149f04` after the conditional store). The same thing in one block (`G = x; return G;`) is already folded by the front end and returns 0. **A field of a global struct or array does not fire**: `GM.f18`, `GA[6]`, `*(Fn *)(GA + 0x18)`, `m->f18` through a pointer, a struct defined or `static` in the TU all return 0.
  - **A small local struct copied from memory, changed, and stored back.** `B f = s->c4; f.b1 = 0; s->c4 = f;` (bitfield words, as in `Unit`/`Stub`), or `*(u32 *)&f = 0; f.b1 = 1; s->c4 = f;`.
  - **A local struct written member by member, then one member changed, then copied out as a whole.** `v.x = p->x; v.y = p->y; v.z = p->z; v.y -= 5; *q = v;` fires. Without the change (`m1`), with only scalar reads afterwards (`m5`), with `V v = *p;` as the initialiser (`k1`), or with `&v` passed to a real call (`n2`), it returns 0.
  - Not firing: stores and reloads through a pointer parameter, `p->vt = &T; p->vt->f(p)`, address-taken scalars read as bytes, `const int &` arguments to an inline, struct arguments by value.
- **The effect is the one cdZ predicted.** `c1` in `toy/s4.c` (`F(p, 0x78, -1); if (GF == 0) GF = mk; return GF();`) gives `mov r1, #0x78; mvn r2, #0`, and without the `GF` lines (`c2`) it gives `sub r2, r1, #0x79`. The early coalesce makes `0x78`'s destination `r1`, so it is never entered as a `K`. This is now a real, natural cause (5) for a refused derivation.

### The targets

- **`ov000_0217a1f8` (3).** Writing the flag clear as a local bitfield copy (`LoBits t = LBIT(self, 4); t.b1 = 0; LBIT(self, 4) = t;`, `toy/a1_a.cpp` and variants `d`..`l`) makes the pass fire. The body then comes out exactly as the ROM's: `mov r0, r4; mov r1, #0x78; mvn r2, #0`, and the creator call is `ldreq; streq; blx r1` with no reload. But the local keeps its 4-byte stack slot: `push {r3, r4, lr}; sub sp, sp, #4` against the ROM's `push {r4, lr}`. Every spelling tried keeps the slot: a union, an inline taking or returning `LoBits`, `u32` through a `LoBits *` cast, and copy-in or copy-out through `*(u32 *)&`. The matched `Stub_021c6140` seems to lose its slot only because its `push {r3, lr}` padding absorbs it (toy `h4`). A 4-byte local in a frame of `{r4, lr}` needs `sub sp`. The other trigger, a scalar global, does not fit either, because the ROM reads the creator as `[data_ov000_021ccd34 + 0x18]`, a struct field, and a struct field does not fire. So the ROM's refusal is still unexplained by any natural source. The bitfield form is the closest result so far: everything matches except the frame.
- **`ov009_02208b24`.** The ROM's `mov r0, #0x66` goes straight into the argument register. That is what (5) produces when the pass fires: the `0x66` is never a `K`, and `0x19a` comes from the pool. But the pass returns 0 for the no-`lim` draft and for every variant tried (`toy/bv/`): case 3's `v` built member by member with or without a separate `v.z -= 0x5000`, case 6's `v3 = v` as a plain struct assignment, and both together. The ROM's case 3 already matches without the pass (the front end forwards `v` into the `unk_b8` stores). So no other part of the body is known to supply the trigger. Not solved. The scan rules above are the shapes to look for.
- **`02049c80`.** Not reworked this round.

## Two structural levers on `ov000_02191f18`: 75 to 17 masked, saved as `NONMATCHING` (round bgC)

No new match. `func_ov000_02191f18` (the animation-event command interpreter, 0xb10) went from 395 / 118 (75 with branch targets and pool offsets masked, `ovbig8/d/1f18_best.cpp`) to 314 / 17 (17 masked). The draft is now a `NONMATCHING` block at the end of `src/ov000/Shadow_02191ec4.cpp`. Scratch files are in `scratchpad/bgC/1f18/` (`w1.cpp` is the saved draft). `bgC/ms.py` is `r43t/msp.py` pointed at the bgC clone; `MSHOW=1` prints the pc-masked aligned diff, and `MSHOW=r` also masks registers.

- **Stores of loaded values through an inline's parameters.** In cases 7 and 23 the target loads `p[1]`, `p[4]`, `p[3]`, `p[2]` and only then shifts and stores them to `actor + 0x9c..0xa8`. Four `LFLD(s32, actor, 0x9c) = p[1] << 4;` statements interleave load and store, because a store through a cast pointer is in the generic alias set and every later load waits for it (round aliasW). Passing the four values to `static inline void SetOfs(u8 *a, s32 w, s32 x, s32 y, s32 z)` evaluates them first, so the loads come first and the scheduler orders them like the target (75 to 59). When the target loads a whole group before the stores, look for an inline or a function call with the values as arguments.
- **`?:` for the scale, after hzX's predecessor rule.** Each of the six hit cases has `if (k) c = FX(c, sc);`. In that form the join's first predecessor is the test block, so step 4 of the constant-hoisting pass (round hzU) never looks at the multiply arm. The `0` and `0x1000` arguments then go to the entry (`mov r5, #0`, `mov r4, #0x1000`). Written as `c = k ? (u16)(((s64)c * sc + 0x800) >> 12) : c;`, the walk sees the multiply arm (pressure 13), both groups are refused, and each case builds its constants itself, as in the target (59 to 18). The `(u16)` cast has to be inside the arm. With it outside, the `lsl/lsr #16` lands at the join (62). Round ovbig8 kept those constants local by splitting the six `0x1000` arguments into `0x1000` and `0x1001`, which changes the values. That is not needed any more.
- **Smaller:** case 6's `u16 d = (u8)(u16)p[0];` gives the target's `ldrh` and the target's `cmp` placement (18 to 17).
- **What is left (17):** the `k` flag. The target builds `mov #0` after the `unk_ce` load and loads `c` after `movne #1`. Ours materialises `k` as `movne/moveq`. The kearly form (`k = FALSE;` before `if (h < 0)`) gives the target's `mov #0`/`movne`, but the scheduler then moves the `k` zero and the `c` load to the top of the block (33). A nested `if` and `h = h < 0 ? 0x64 : h` change nothing.
- **`ov000_021b9b14`:** the "best" draft (`giantsB/d/9b14mv1/best.cpp`, 89 / 14) holds three `(u32)self & 3` two-definition hacks. Without them, and with `sprB->depth` stored after `sprA`'s virtual calls as in the target, it is 101 / 30 (`bgC/9b14/h2.cpp`). Most of what is left is the `dp` pool constant, which the target keeps in `r5` across the calls and we rematerialise (round spT). Not saved.

## Why `0217a1f8` can't get the store-load pass, and a natural trigger for `02208b24`: no new match (round cdC)

No new match, and no source or `tools/` change. Scratch is in `scratchpad/cdC/` (`t/` is round cdB's tool set pointed at this clone; toys in `toy/f1.c`..`f5.cpp`; the `02208b24` variants in `toy/bv/`, best draft `toy/bv/d2.cpp`).

### Which objects the pass can use (`0x5221f0`)

- **Globals: only a whole 4-byte object at offset 0.** The candidate check calls `0x574f80(obj)` (true, so rejected, when the object's kind byte `+0x30` is 2, a split struct) and `0x575d60(insn, obj)`, which requires that the access size (`0x50fde0`) equals the object's size (`obj+0x1c`). `toy/f4.c`: `extern struct { Fn f; } G1; ... G1.f` (a 4-byte struct, offset 0) fires, while `(&GF)[6]` on a 4-byte scalar and `*(Fn *)(X4 + 0x18)` on a 4-byte array do not. So no declaration of `data_ov000_021ccd34` can make `ldr r1, [r0, #0x18]` fire, because the access is at offset 0x18 and the object is the TU-shared task struct (other TUs use its fields at 0, 4, 0xc, 0x10, 0x14 and 0x18). MWCC has no data pooling switch (`strings` lists only `pool_strings` / `constpool`), so the field cannot be a scalar addressed from a pooled base.
- **Locals: every local the pass works on keeps its frame slot.** The slot is reserved when the local is still a memory object. The pass then removes every access, but it does not give the slot back. `toy/f1.c`/`f3.c`: the copy-modify-store shape with a call keeps `push {r3, r4, lr}; sub sp, #4` for `B`, `register B`, a one-word struct, a one-element array, a `u32` changed through `(B *)&t` and a union. Two such locals in separate scopes take 8 bytes (`a6`). The slot is invisible only when the frame already has a padding word for it (`t1`: `push {r3, lr}`, where `r3` is the slot). A leaf (`t3`) gets `stmdb {r3}; sub sp, #4`.
- **Argument-side checks (`toy/f5.cpp`).** A variadic callee, a member function, a call through a function pointer, `short` parameters and a `(char)0x78` cast all still derive `sub r2, r1, #0x79`.

### The targets

- **`ov000_0217a1f8` (3): closed for the store-load route.** The ROM frame is `push {r4, lr}`: 8 bytes with no padding word, so any local trigger adds `sub sp, #4`. The only global in the body is the `+0x18` field, and a field can't pass `0x575d60`. Every other store is through `self` or a returned pointer, and those never fire. So under `dsi/1.3` no natural source can make this pass the cause of the ROM's `mvn r2, #0`. What remains is (1)–(4) from round cdZ, which rounds cdZ/menuN found nothing natural for, or a different compiler build for this function (round cvY: `1.2/sp4` gives the ROM code, but the TU's other functions need `dsi/1.3`). The pooled `scratchpad/menu/m1.cpp` still can't land: `0217a1f8` is unchanged, and `0217b324` remains a blocker either way.
- **`ov009_02208b24`: a natural trigger in case 5. The `0x66` / `0x19a` code now matches (33 to 21 diffs).** Case 5 copies the target object's position into `unk_b8`, then into `pos` with `y` raised by `p->end.y`. Written with the function's vector local, `v = FLD(Ov009Vec, o, 0x88); self->unk_b8 = v; v.y += off; self->pos = v;`, that is cdB's third shape (a local struct, one member changed, copied out whole). The pass fires, and the `0x66` goes straight into `r0` (`mov r0, #0x66`). `0x19a` is then loaded from the pool after the calls, exactly as in the ROM. `v` already has its slot in this frame (`sub sp, #0x24`), so the frame is unchanged. A new local `q` instead of `v` does not fire (40). The best layout (`toy/bv/d2.cpp`, 21) reads `rot[1]` first, then `v`, then `off = p->end.y` before the stores. Its case 5 has the ROM's registers (`y` r3, `off` r1, `x` r4, `z` r2), but the order is `ldrh; strh; ldr 0x8c; ldr off` against the ROM's `ldrh r2; ldr r1, off; strh`. Other placements of `off` move the order and break the registers (`c3`, `d1`, `e1`..`e5`: 22–28). Case 3's `FX_Mul` pair also shifts by one register (`r8`/`r3` against `r3`/`r5`, `ip`). The draft still needs round near4's junk: without `if ((u32)self & 3) spd = p->end.x;` it is 33, and with `v3 = v` in place of the `Ov009Blk12b` copy the pass stops firing (153). So it is not saved.

## The degree lever needs the wrong node to be a named local: no new match (round dgA)

No new match, and `tools/` is unchanged. Scratch files are in `scratchpad/dgA/` (mgX's `re/`, `pipe.sh`, `ms.py` and lcA's `t/` as `tt/`, pointed at the dgA clone; one directory per target with its `base.cpp`, the variants and the `pipe.sh` dumps). Three new model scripts are in `dgA/re/`. `tr.py RA.out ROUND nodes…` replays round mgX's `simplify` and prints, for each node, the pass in which it is pushed and its degree at that moment. `dg.py RA.out "{want}"` adds a fixed degree offset (−12 to +40) to one node at a time and recolours: it asks whether any single node crossing the K = 14 line would fix the function. `edge.py RA.out "{want}"` removes or adds one edge at a time. Scores are `ms.py` raw / masked.

### What the lever can and cannot reach

- In mgX's model the colouring order is set by the pass in which `simplify` pushes a node. Low nodes are pushed in ascending order inside a pass, and each later pass is coloured first. A node is coloured before another only if it is pushed in a **later pass**, or later in the same pass. A degree change moves a node across passes, so it only helps when the right colouring needs a node to move from one pass to another.
- **`ov000_021512b4` (23 / 0): impossible by degree.** `tr.py` on `smW/12b4/b2.cpp`: the `-0x191a` constant (76) and `bx` (47) are both pushed in pass 2 (degree 8 and 9: only precoloured neighbours and `self` are left), and `self` (16) alone in pass 3. The target needs the colour order `self`, `bx`, constant. So `bx` would have to be pushed after 76 but before `self`. If `bx` stays high through pass 2 (`dg.py`: +5 or more), it is pushed in pass 3 together with `self`, in ascending order, so it is coloured *before* `self`. It takes `r4`, and `self` moves to `r5`. `self` has only 7 precoloured neighbours plus `bx`, so it can never be pushed in a fourth pass. No degree offset on any node fixes it. Merging the first `x`, `cx` and `bx` into one `x` gives 30 / 0 (`dgA/12b4/m1.cpp`). `cx` merged into `bx` gives 36 / 0, and the first `x` with `bx` 30 / 0. MWCC splits each assignment into its own web, so the merge only adds renumbering.
- **`ov000_0219b808` (4 / 0, `ovlo12/d/b808/f.cpp`): it is not a colouring-order problem.** The two wrong temps are the `rot` copy loads in `Send` (116, 117; the target has `r1`, `r3`). In our graph 117 interferes with precoloured `r3` (the `mov r3, #1` argument is already live), so no colouring order can give it `r3`. ### Rule for picking lever targets

Use the lever only when `want.py` names a **named local** (object band) among the wrong nodes, and `tr.py` shows that it has to move into a later (or earlier) `simplify` pass than it is in now. Then check with `dg.py` that a degree offset on it fixes the function before writing source. When the wrong nodes are only temps, or a node interferes with the register the target gives it, variable merging can't help.
## A `?:` exposes the arm that refuses a stack address's hoist: `ov014_0220f3f0` matches (round bgE)

`func_ov014_0220f3f0` (0x400, the box-distance helper of `func_ov014_0220f20c`) matches without the `VOLR` reads. It is appended to `src/ov014/ov014_0220f20c.cpp`, whose `.text` range now ends at `0x0220f7f0`. Scratch files are in `scratchpad/bgE/` (`ms.py`/`nm.py` pointed at the bgE clone, `t/` is round hzX's `mcl.sh` tool set pointed at the bgE clone, the draft is `f3f0/v1.cpp`).

- **What the "hoisted `&ax`" really was.** `mcl.sh` shows that `add vN, sp, #k` (op170, the address of a stack object) is grouped by the move-constant-loads pass (round hzU) like any constant. In our draft the `&ax` group has 6 instances (the `MTX_MultVec33` and `VEC_Normalize` arguments of each axis) and walks all the way to block 1. It is then a long-lived rematerialisable value with a negative spill cost (round spT), so it is spilled and rebuilt at each use, which is why every `&ax` was a fresh `add r0, sp, #0x48`. The ROM's `add r6, sp, #0x48` before each `ble` is the next axis's instance, moved one step up to the `d > 0x1000` test block and then refused. So the target's walk out of that test block hits pressure above 10.
- **The lever.** The test block is the join of `if (e != 0) { ... d = ...; }`, whose first predecessor is the condition block (pressure 9 in ours), so the walk never sees the body, which holds the 64-bit dot product and two calls. Written as `s32 d = e != 0 ? Ov014_AxisDist(&ax, a, b, e) : 0;`, with the normalise, dot, `FX_Div` and `abs` in a `static inline`, the body becomes the join's first predecessor, the step is refused, and `&ax` stays in `r6` for the next axis, as in the ROM (52 / 22 to 0). With `d = 0; if (e != 0) d = Ov014_AxisDist(...);` it stays at 38 / 22. This is round hzX's predecessor-order rule, applied to a stack address instead of a literal.
- **Rule of thumb:** when the target keeps `add rN, sp, #k` in a callee-saved register over a short stretch, and ours rebuilds it at every use, ours probably hoisted it too far and rematerialised it. Look for the join whose step the target refuses and try the `?:` form there.
- **Not solved:**
  - `ov010_02204030` (22 / 10, `sdkf/4030/p10.cpp`). Lever 1 does not reach the entry block. The four forms tried all stay at 22 / 10: `v.z` first with the sin/cos values in locals before the zero stores, the sin/cos values computed before `VEC_Set`, the zeros stored inside an inline that takes the sin/cos values as parameters, and a chained `v.x = v.y = 0`. A `VEC_Set` variant that takes the matrix and calls the rotation scores 24 / 12. The scheduler still puts the zero stores first.
  - `ov010_02201064` (180 / 22 without `volatile`, on `honL/1064/h1.c`). The `0x2e` reload stays shared under a `u16 *st = &self->0x2c` pair pointer (180 / 22), the `?:` form `0x2e = k ? 0 : 0x2e + 1` (189 / 30), `+ (u16)1` (184 / 24) and the swapped test with the arms swapped (186 / 28).
  - `ov003_021cd91c`, `0206d43c`, `02043100`: re-read. Their misses are in scheduling or colouring inside one block (the case-10 alpha stores, the register-only `0206d43c`, the `ldm` in `02043100`), with no load/store group or join for the three levers. Not retried.

With `k` first, `k` is coloured before `sc` and takes `r0`, and `sc` is left with `ip`/`lr`, as in the target. Of the 24 orders of `h`/`sc`/`k`/`c`, all 12 with `k` before `sc` give the same result. ## The hoisting lever on the spill near-misses: no new match, `ov011_021fc0b8` is one refused step (round hzZ)

No new match. Tools are round hzY's `mcl.sh`/`mcl.py`, pointed at the hzZ clone, in `scratchpad/hzZ/t/`. New: `mclf.sh`/`mclf.py` is `mcl.sh` with `FORCE="from:to,..."`, which forces the pressure check of those step(s) to fail (block numbers apply to every function in the file), so a "what if this hoist were refused" object can be scored with `OBJ=... msp.py`. `hzZ/sw.sh SRC FUNC MOD NAME` makes a `NONMATCHING` copy of a source file, scores the function and prints the move-constant-loads groups of 5 or more with their moves and refusals.

### `ov000_0217b324` (45 / 14 masked): not a hoisting problem

`mcl.sh` on `spT/b324/base.cpp` (`hzZ/b324/mcl_base.txt`): the whole time section, from the `0xb2` message to the `0xb1` message, is one block (69). Its three `"%.2d"` addresses and the `0x36b06e71`, `0x34bc0`, `0x91a2b3c5`, `0xe10`, `0x88888889` constants are each **one** instance (first local CSE merges the three `"%.2d"`), so their groups have count 1 and the pass never moves them. The ROM also loads each of them once. So both builds give the same long-lived values, and the difference is only which of them colouring spills (rounds spT/spW). The groups that do move (the zero, count 15; the heap-global address `op170`, count 13; the `4`, count 6) move inside the `FREE_SLOT` chain or in the `items` loop, and none of them passes through block 69. No `?:` or statement change can reach it through this pass.

### `ov011_021fc0b8` (13 / 3): 11 of the 13 diffs are one hoist step

- In case 2 the zero of `Ov011Ent_Remove`'s `e->unk_08 = 0` (block 59, the `break` path) is in the zero group (24 instances). Ours moves it `59 -> 57 -> 56 -> 94 -> 55 -> 54 -> 53 -> 52` and stops at `52 -> 47` (pressure 15), so it ends in `sl` above the `s != NULL` test. It adds 1 to blocks 53 and 54 on the way. Then the `1` group (9 instances) tries `on`'s `1` in block 54, and `54 -> 53` sees 11 and is refused, so ours builds `mov r5, #1` in the `Act` block.
- The ROM has `mov r6, #0` at the inner loop head (block 56, the `bne` target) and `mov sl, #1` above the `s != NULL` test. So in the ROM the zero stopped at 56 (`56 -> 94` refused) and the `1` then went `54 -> 53 -> 52`.
- `FORCE=56:94` gives exactly that: the `1` moves to 52, every register matches, and the score is **2 / 2** (from 13 / 3). What is left is the order inside block 56: ours `cmp r0, r8; mov r6, #0`, the ROM `mov r6, #0; cmp r0, r8`. A moved constant is appended at the end of the dominator, so a moved zero always comes after the compare. `FORCE=57:56` (zero stopped in the `k == n` body) also gives 2 / 2, with the `mov` in the body, and post-RA head merge does not lift it.
- Why the ROM refuses `56 -> 94` is still open. The walk from block 56 starts at its first predecessor, which is the preheader 94 itself (pressure 8). The other predecessor, the latch 60, is 8, and 56 is 9. So neither the `?:` predecessor-order lever nor a pressure difference of 1 explains it. The ROM would need 11 in the preheader. Its live values there (`self`, `a`, `e`, `k`, `n`, `found`, and the hoisted `1` of the `021d7a44` argument in `r4`) are the same as ours. The ROM's `mov` before the `cmp` also suggests that the ROM's zero was in block 56 before scheduling rather than appended there. `ov011_021fd638` has the same `Ov011Ent_Remove` and the same unexplained early stop (round hzY: `82 -> 9`, pressure 8). So the real inline probably has a different shape. Tried, all 13 / 3: guarded `do`/`while`, a `while` with `n = n->next` at the end, `if (!e->b0) return;` with a `return` in place of the `break`, and `if (k != n) continue;`. A search loop followed by the removal after it is 27 / 21.

### The sweep

- **`ov000_021743bc` (123 / 2).** The `0`/`1` (to the entry) and the `0xffffe353`, `4`, `0x8000`, `op170` groups (stopped at `16 -> 11` or `25 -> 23`) are placed exactly where the ROM has them. **Rule for picking targets for this lever:** run `sw.sh` first. The lever only applies when a constant group of 5 or more moves through the place where the ROM's code differs. A spilled pool value with one instance (as in `0217b324`) is a colouring problem, not a hoisting one. ## `ov011_021fc0b8` stops in the preheader, not the loop head: no new match (round hzR)

No new match, and no source change. Tools are round hzZ's, pointed at the hzR clone, in `scratchpad/hzR/t/`. New: `hzR/ev.sh FILE` prints the score and the `0`/`1` moves of `021fc0b8`; `t/lv.sh FILE OUT` (`BLK=55,94`) prints each listed block's live-out set as the pressure pass (`0x5b1040`) sees it; `t/mclo.sh` also prints the order in which the pass visits blocks; `hzR/rd.py MOD LO HI` disassembles a ROM range with real branch targets.

- **Round hzZ misread the ROM.** The ROM's `mov r6, #0` is at `0x021fc668`, and the latch branches back to `0x021fc66c` (the `cmp r0, r8`). So the zero is in the inner preheader (block 94), not in the loop head, and the "`mov` before `cmp`" order is just the preheader falling through into the head. `FORCE=94:55` (refuse the step from the preheader to the `n != NULL` guard) gives **0 / 0**. `ov011_021fd638` is the same: its zero is at `0x021fd6c8` in the preheader, the latch branches to `0x021fd6cc`, and `FORCE=82:9` on bgH's draft takes it from 27 / 5 (24 / 2 masked) to 22 / 0. The diffs left are register diffs further down, not hoisting.
- **What the refusal needs.** The walk for `94 -> 55` checks only block 55, because 94 has one predecessor. Block 55 is at 8: its live-out set is `k` (r0), `sp`, `self`, `a`, `head`, `n`, `e` and `found`. A refusal needs 11 or more, or block 55 empty. The pressure is real liveness after coalescing. The "+1 per hoisted constant" cannot help: in a group, `0x526390` adds at most 1 to each block, because flag `0x8000` is cleared once per group and not once per move, and no move walks through 55 before 55 is visited. The pass visits blocks in reverse layout order (`0x65e204`), so a dominator is always visited after its children. The only empty blocks left when the pass runs are the loop-exit pads (`0x5158b0`), and those are made only for loops with a single exit target (`0x515a20`). The `break` path gives this loop two exit targets, so it has no pad.
- **Tried, all 13 / 3 with the step still `94 -> 55 p=8`:** `while` with `n = n->next` at the end, a guarded `do`/`while`, `if (!e->b0) return;`, `e->b0 && (n = e->unk_04) != NULL`, `continue`, `goto`, `n == k`, a separate `Free` inline, `Remove` as a member function (`this` from `self->ent`), the removal statements swapped, an extra copy of `a` in `Act`, and `Remove(self->ent, ...)` (15 / 5). A class `operator delete` for the free drops the null check (44 / 35). Without the `break` (a diagnostic, not the original code), loop-invariant code motion puts the zero in 94 and the pass still moves it out (`94->55 p=7`).
- **Open.** In both functions the ROM's source makes the guard block reach pressure 11, or puts an empty block between the guard and the preheader. Its final code is identical to ours, so any extra live values would have to be copies that the register allocator merges later. None of the natural inline shapes does this. The same shape fixes both functions.

**Rule:** before trying to explain a stop, read the ROM with real branch targets (`rd.py`). A `mov` just before a loop head's first instruction may be in the preheader. Check which block the back edge targets.

The secondary sweep found no single-step candidate. The unowned in-tree `NONMATCHING` functions (`020459cc` 9 / 0, `02046070` 6 / 0, `02047724` 15 / 0, `ov002_021d1f70` 35 / 0) are 0 with registers masked. In `02046070`, the `sysState` pointer and value registers are swapped twice. Writing the store out directly, reordering the `bssid` stores, inverting the test or dropping the `const` from `bssid` gives no gain or makes it worse.
## The fake `k` parameter was a block-scope local and an `if`/`else` flag: no new match, `0216715c` to 124 / 58 (round bgJ)

No new match. `func_ov000_0216715c` now has an honest `NONMATCHING` draft at the end of `src/ov000/Lo_02166be8.cpp` (whose `.text` ends at `0x0216715c`, right before it), with the real `(self, p)` signature: 124 / 58, 113 / 45 with branch targets and pool offsets masked. Before this round the clean draft (`ovmid2/n/best/715c_clean_114_48.cpp`) was 125 / 61, but only because of a fake third parameter `k`. With `k` as a local it was 135–138 / 61. Scratch is in `scratchpad/bgJ/` (bgG's `ms.py`, `nm.py`, `dd.sh`, `pipe.sh` and `re/`, plus bgE's `t/` pass dumpers, all pointed at the bgJ clone; `objs.sh FILE` prints the named and temp objects of the last colouring graph with their node numbers; `715c/base2.cpp` is the saved draft, `715c/perm.py` sweeps statement orders).

- **What the parameter was buying.** Parameters are numbered first (`p` 17, `k` 18). Then come the front end's temps, highest id first, and then the named locals in reverse declaration order. The ROM colours `k` (`sb`) before the `f_0` web (`r6`). With `f_0 = (r == ...)` / `f_0 = a && b`, each arm creates a boolean-materialisation temp (`@236`, `@235`, …). Those are created last, so they get the lowest numbers, below every local (`objs.sh`: the `f_0` web is node 18). So no declaration slot for `k` can help: all 27 slots give 135–138, and so do inline returns for `k`.
- **The fix.** Write `f_0` as `if (cond) f_0 = TRUE; else f_0 = FALSE;` in both arms. `f_0` is then a named local (node 35), and `k` can be a plain `s32 k = ...;` at block scope in the loop (node 32). The result is 125 / 61, the same as the fake-parameter draft, with no fake parameter. The `f_0 = FALSE; if (...) f_0 = TRUE;` form is worse (151–153 / 70). **Rule:** when a fake parameter "fixes" colouring, look at `objs.sh`. If the node it displaces is a `@` temp, the real source probably has that value as a named variable rather than a temp.
- **The lerp fold.** `Lerp(x0 << 12, x1 << 12, s)` lets the front end fold `(x1 << 12) - (x0 << 12)` into `(x1 - x0) << 12`. The ROM has `lsl sl, r0, #12; sub sl, sl, ip, lsl #12`. Writing `x0 <<= 12; y0 <<= 12;` as statements and then `Lerp(x0, x1 << 12, s)` gives the ROM's form (125 / 61 to 124 / 58). Shifting `x1` at its assignment (`L1.cpp`) also gives the ROM's form but spills `mgr` (143 / 116). Statement order of the inner block is normalised: all 300+ valid orders give the same hash.
- **Left (not solved).** The outer loop's sine temp is `r6` in the ROM, `r1` in ours. Its neighbours leave `r1` free, so in the ROM it must be live much longer, or be coalesced. The entry `0xc88` and `oam` word-0 temps are `r5`/`r4` in the ROM, `r4`/`r2` in ours, because the ROM loads both `oam` words before storing either. A flat 8-byte bitfield struct gives the same code. Most of the rest is inner-loop colouring (`e2` should be `sb`).
- **`ov009_02204a10`: not solved, unchanged.** In the ROM's last loop, `[sp, #0x10]` (`self + 0x10c`) and `&v` are both spilled: `&v` is rebuilt at each use as `add r0, sp, #0x78`, and `fp` is used as a temporary. Ours keeps `&v` in `fp` and uses `lr`. So the ROM is over the limit by about two values in round 1, not one. The `0x666` and `0` groups are not what moves it (`t/mcl.sh` on `4a10/h0.cpp`). The ROM also keeps `g.x` in a register past the `z` product (`str r3, [sp, #0x48]` comes late), but a `SetVec(&g, x, 0, z)` inline gives the same hash (182 / 187 honest, 50 / 27 with the `volatile`). - **What is left there (the `ret = NULL` slot) is a scheduling question, not a colouring one.** The target's `mov r1, #0` after `ldr r4, [r1]` is a post-allocation WAR on `r1`, so before allocation the zero came after the dereference. Our pre-RA list puts it in the load's latency slot (`sd7`: the only ready instruction at cycle 1). `ret = NULL` above the `unk_20` test is CSE'd into `mov r1, r0` (16 / 3); the head-merge form (`ret = NULL` in both arms) now gives the right placement but leaves the extra `b` (47 / 17); `mgr` locals, declaration initialisers and every placement of the statement stay at 3. `cxxperm` (15 min, 15,896 compiles) found nothing below the base.
- **Rule: the final peephole drops a compare that repeats the predecessor's last compare** (the `bgt`/`bge` pair of a switch tree on the same value), but only when that compare is the last instruction before the branch in the post-allocation list. `021fe2a4`'s target keeps `cmp r2, #0x14` twice. In the pcode just before `FINAL PEEPHOLE` (`t2/ph.sh`), the draft with the old `s32 i = flag;` has `cmp; mov r6, sb; b`, and the cmp survives; with an honest `for (i = 0; ...)` the entry has only three cheap instructions for three latency slots (`mov #0` twice and `flag`), all scheduled before the `cmp`, and the second `cmp` goes. So the target's entry block had at least four cheap instructions before scheduling, one of them later coalesced away. A dead `i = 0` is removed too early to count.

Block 44's own pressure is 9, plus 1 from the `> 0x78` zero walked through it first. Spelling the `Mul64`/`021d9dbc` statements differently (direct `s64` expression, a `pos` pointer local, cast changes) leaves it at 9. Every other compiler is worse (`dsi/1.1` 248, `dsi/1.6` 323, `2.0` 574, `1.2` 618 or more, for `021fc0b8`). The command-line `-opt` sub-options (`noloop`, `nocse`, `noprop`, `nolifetimes`, ...) change nothing; only `-O`/level/space flags and `#pragma`s do. `-O4,s`, `-O3`, `-O2`, `optimization_level 3`, `optimize_for_size`, and the `opt_loop_invariants`/`opt_propagation`/`opt_common_subs`/`opt_strength_reduction`/`opt_dead_assignments`/`opt_dead_code` pragmas all make both functions worse (25 to 532 diffs). `-inline on/auto/all/smart/deferred/level=0..8/nobottomup`, `-ipa file`, `-proc v5te`, `-str reuse`, `-enum min`, `-RTTI on`, `-Cpp_exceptions on`, `-nointerworking`, `-sym off`, `-g`, `-constpool` and the pragmas `peephole`/`scheduling`/`opt_lifetimes`/`register_coloring`/`global_optimizer off` change neither. The limit is 10 in every check. So no version or per-TU pin applies.
- **Where the pressure would have to come from.** With `PT=1`, every move adds 1 to the pressure of its target block (block 55 goes from 8 to 9 after `94 -> 55`). Call clobbers are not counted (block 54, which has three calls, is at 7). The ROM's `1` still goes `54 -> 53 -> 52`, and that check reads block 53 (10 in ours, so it must stay at 10 or less). So the 3 extra live values the ROM needs at the guard can't be live in block 53. They have to be defined in block 54 or 55 (after the `!s->b0` test) and live out of 55, and they must leave no instruction in the final code. Only copies of `e`, `k`, `head` or `n` that the allocator later coalesces and deletes would do that. Constants can add at most 1 (the `NULL` of `02201214` would, if it were a movable instance), and the zero group (24) is always handled before the `1` group (9).
- **The front end removes the copies that this would need.** A local copy of `a` or of `ent` in `Ov011_Act` (`u8 *b = a`, `Ov011Ent *e2 = ent`) gives the same IR. The same is true of a list sub-struct with a member `Remove` (`this` = `&e->unk_04`), a template `TList<T>::Remove` returning `BOOL`, a `T **pp` head pointer, `pp = &(*pp)->next` iteration, a `head` local, a typed `k` local, `Remove` returning `BOOL`, a node type with a destructor and a class `operator delete` (`delete n` keeps the null check), and a `while` outer loop or a `continue` form of the `s` test. All of them give 13 / 3, with `94 -> 55` at 8. These are worse: `n = e->b0 ? e->unk_04 : NULL` or a `Head()` inline (16 / 6, because the guard becomes a join and `head` is reloaded), a `found`-flag loop (95 / 48), search then remove (57 / 49), `next` prefetch (44 / 33), `found = s` after `Act` (90 / 9, still 8 at the guard), and `found == NULL` in the outer loop's condition (172 / 107).
- **`021fd638`.** `FORCE=82:9` on the draft still gives 22 / 0 (from 27 / 5). Its guard (block 9) is also at 8: `k`, `head`, `n`, `self`, `a`, the outer `n`, `next` and `sp`. (`lv.py` also prints two vreg numbers that are not in the IR, `v960` and `v973`. These are leftover bits above the function's last vreg.) It needs the same 3 values from the same inline, so a fix for `021fc0b8` should carry over to the draft unchanged.

**Rule:** a pressure refusal that the ROM needs has to come from values that are live in the blocks of the refused step and in no block that a later allowed step reads. Work out that window with `PT=1` before writing source forms. Here the window is blocks 54–55, between two calls and the guard, and only copies that the allocator deletes fit in it.

- **`02049c80`: why `-1` sits in `r4`.** Derivation runs before move-constant-loads (the pass order is in `t/passnames.txt`). `mcl.sh` on the clean draft (`9c80/c0.cpp`, 57 / 26 with `ms.py`) shows a `-1` group of only 4 (the `id < 0` return and the three `!= -1` tests), because every arm return was already derived from the `result = 0` zero. With the threshold at 5, nothing is hoisted, and each test builds its own `mvn`. In the ROM the `slot >= 5` return is a fresh `mvn`, so it is the fifth instance, and the `result < 0` and `!useSlot` returns are `zero - 1`. Putting the slot check in front of the zero gives exactly that: `if (useSlot && slot >= 5) return -1; result = 0; if (!useSlot) ...` (`9c80/v1.cpp`). Every derivation, the hoisted `-1` (`cmp r8, r4`, `sub r0, r4, #0x7f`) and the whole register allocation (`r6` mgr then handle, `r5`/`r7` zero/result, `r8`, `sb`) come out as in the ROM, at 26 / 24 (85 by `match.py`, because it is shifted). It is saved as `NONMATCHING`. What is left: the ROM tests `useSlot` once and has the slot check inside the `useSlot` arm, after the zero. MWCC does not thread the second test (`&&`, nested `if`, `!= 0`, the slot test merged into the `id < 0` test: 85–93). With the check inside the arm (`v2`, `result = 0` in the `!useSlot` arm) the `-1` is hoisted, but the `result < 0` return takes `r4` instead of `zero - 1` (45 / 19). So the ROM needs a zero in the `useSlot` arm between the slot check and the `result < 0` return, or a `slot >= 5` block outside the zero's extended block. A dead `result = 0` is removed before derivation. Re-reading the slot, `return result`, `== -1` and a chained assignment give 74–88 raw.

Only `lsl r3, r2, #26` (a `mov` constant) breaks it. Ways to stop `1`/`5` being folded, each on plain single-definition locals: `#pragma opt_propagation off` gives the target's idiom in a toy (`toy/p_opt_propagation.c`), but in the function it adds entry guards to every counted loop and hoists the locals (357). `asm { mov one, #1 }` statements give it in a toy too (`toy/e.c`, and the `mov` is scheduled freely), but in the function they turn off loop rotation (344). A non-inlined helper that takes `one`/`five` as parameters gives exactly the idiom (`toy/g.c` `Rd2`), but the ROM has no call there, and inlining always folds them (`-inline auto`, `-inline deferred`, `-ipa file`, `static inline`). In toys, the other `opt_*` pragmas and `const`, `static const`, global `const`, local array, struct and union forms all fold too, and `optimization_level 1` keeps the locals but drops loop rotation. The junk draft scores 27 under every `dsi/*` compiler, and the 1.2 and 2.0 compilers reject its `__typeof__`. The SCFG address `((((x & 1) + 5) << 18) - 13) << 5` is `0x02000000 + (x + 1) * 8 MB - 0x1a0` (the ROM header copy at the end of main memory, plus `0x60`). No natural spelling folds the base into `+5`. A 32-byte-element index gives `(x + 1) << 18`, then `- 13`, `<< 5`, `+ 0x2000000`.

The ROM's `r1`/`r3`/`r2` mean something coloured `r0` interferes with all three, but nothing in the ROM's loop reads `r0`. ## A zero set in both arms of a test is head-merged after allocation: `ov000_0218cfc8` matches (round scA)

`func_ov000_0218cfc8` matches and is now the first function of `src/ov000/Actor_0218d17c.cpp` (its `.text` starts at `0x0218cfc8`; the bgH `NONMATCHING` block is gone). Scratch files are in `scratchpad/scA/` (bgH's `sch/`, `t/`, `t2/`, `re/`, `perm.py`, `ev.sh` pointed at the scA clone; `cfc8/h3.cpp` is the match).

### Scheduler rules (mwccarm `dsi/1.3`, read from `0x50dce0`/`0x50d9b0` and the `sd7` dumps)

- **Which blocks.** `0x50dce0` walks every block and schedules it when it has 2 or more instructions and none of the flags `0x11b`; afterwards it sets bit 8. That is the same loop for the pre-allocation run (pressure flag on) and the post-allocation run, so in the second run only blocks whose bit 8 was cleared in between are rescheduled (round sched).
- **Cycle model.** One instruction per cycle. A node is ready when all its predecessors have issued and their latencies have passed (`ldr`/address/pool loads 2, `ldrh`/`ldrb` 3, ALU and moves 1, branch 3). When nothing is ready the cycle advances with no pick. So a latency slot is always filled by any ready node, however low its height: a `mov rX, #k` with no inputs fills the first slot after a load in its block. No source order or height trick keeps a dependence-free constant out of that slot.
- **Pick order** (normal mode, live count below 14): urgent node first (deadline reached), then the one that makes more successors ready (`c` in the dump), then the greater height, then list order (the order codegen emitted). In pressure mode (live count 14 or more) the lowest pressure score wins first (round nmZ), then list order.
- **What runs after it.** Move constant loads (`0x526af0`) runs *before* the pre-allocation scheduler (`0x474c68` against `0x474cb6`), so a hoisted constant is scheduled like any other instruction. The post-allocation head merge (`0x5135b0`, between `BEFORE PEEPHOLE OPTIMIZATION` and `FINAL PEEPHOLE`) runs after it, and it puts the merged instruction **after** the block's compare, just before the branch (`t2/ph.sh` on `h3.cpp`: `ldr; ldr; cmp; mov r1, #0; b` in the final-peephole dump). It clears bit 8, so the post-allocation scheduler then moves the `mov` above the `cmp`, but it can't move it above the load that still reads the same register (WAR on `r1`).

### `0218cfc8`

- The ROM's `ldr r1, =data_ov000_021ccd68; ldr r4, [r1]; mov r1, #0` has the zero in `r1`, after the dereference. By the rules above no pre-allocation order of that block gives this, because the zero would fill the load's slot and interfere with the address. So the zero was not in that block before allocation. It came from the head merge: **both successors of the `data_ov000_021ccd68 != NULL` test started with `ret = NULL`.** Those two blocks are the `id != 0xffff` test and the "no manager" arm.
- Source: `if (data_ov000_021ccd68 == NULL) { ret = NULL; } else { ret = NULL; if (id != 0xffff) { ...lookup... } }`. This is the inlined shape of a `FindActor` that returns `NULL` early when there is no manager. bgH's `key`/`g2`-before-`next` declaration order (round bgD lever) is kept. The comma form `else if (ret = NULL, id != 0xffff)` also gives 0. bgH's head-merge try (`hm1`, 47 / 17) put the second `ret = NULL` after *both* tests, so the successors of the first test did not start with the same instruction.
- The same body as a `static inline` with `return NULL;` scores 8 / 0. The inline's locals are created after the function's own, so `key`/`g2` are numbered below `next` again and get `r7`/`r6`. No order of the inline's five locals helps. Declaring `prev`/`next` at their first use is worse (25 / 9).
- **Rule:** when the ROM has a constant right after a load and before the compare that ends the block, in a register the load's address just used, look for that constant at the start of both successors of the branch, not in the block itself.

## A sweep for head- and tail-merge marks finds none left to fix: no new match (round scB)

No new match, and no source or `tools/` change. Scratch files are in `scratchpad/scB/`. scA's `sch/`, `t/`, `t2/` and `re/` tools point at the scB clone, and `sd7.sh`, `t/mcl.sh` and `t2/ph.sh` pass `-DNONMATCHING`. `hm.py MOD FUNC` scans the ROM copy of a function. `sw.py MOD FUNC SRC` compiles a draft with `-DNONMATCHING`, diffs it against the ROM and prints the marks that sit within 3 instructions of a register-masked diff. `drafts.lst` is the list of best drafts that was swept.

### The marks

- **`HMS`/`WAR`.** A cheap instruction (`mov`, `add`, ...) whose register an earlier instruction of its block reads, whose result the block does not use, and with an idle cycle before it in the in-order cycle model. `HMS` means it is one of the last three instructions before a conditional branch: this is scA's head-merge signature. Argument registers in blocks that hold a call are skipped, because they are precoloured before allocation.
- **`HM2`.** Both successors of a conditional branch start with the same instruction, so that pair was not head-merged.
- **`LATE`.** An instruction that issues after an idle cycle it could have filled, held back by a WAR on its register.
- **`MOVE`.** The same masked instruction is deleted on one side and inserted on the other, across a branch.

### Result

The sweep covered the 17 in-tree `NONMATCHING` drafts and the 22 best scratch drafts of the functions no other worker owns. Every ROM head-merge site in them is already reproduced by the draft:

- `020417e0`: `add r0, r6, #0x88; add r1, r6, #0x4c` before `bne`, the arguments of both `0201e520` calls.
- `0218867c`: `mov r1, #1` after `cmp r1, #0`, from the two `vfunc_38(1)` arms.
- `021ff24c`: the count zero after `cmp r3, #0`.
- `02053254`: the bit-field load after `cmp r2, #0x1000`.

`ov000_0218cfc8` stays the only head-merge fix. The other register-masked diffs are list order, pressure refusals or allocation. Three of them were traced further:

- **`ov006_021e7004`: the `smull` before `t->x` is a block-boundary question.** Before allocation, the post-call code is in the same block as the `FX_Atan2` call. By the pick at cycle 15 every node is past its deadline, so `c` decides, and the `t->x` load (`c1`, `h13`) beats the `dz` `smull` (`c0`, `h17`). If a block starts after the `yaw` store, `smull` is urgent at cycle 6 (`dl 3`) and `t->x` is not (`dl 7`). That gives exactly the ROM's `posZ, t->z, posX, sub, smull, t->x`. A test branch there (`if (keys == NULL) return;`) confirms it. No form that emits no code was found to start that block. These stay at 24–30: the `yaw` store in a `static inline`, the sqrt and wait loop in a `Dist(sq)` inline, and a `DistXZ(self, t)` inline (with or without a `d` local).
- **The other `021e7004` miss.** The `hp` `lsr #16` is the tail-merged truncation of both `HalfAngle` arms (both arms end with it in the pre-final-peephole dump, `t2/ph.sh`). Its final position comes from a scheduler run after if-conversion. These do not move it: all 20 dependence-legal orders of the `dp`/`dy`/`hp`/`hy`/`p`/`y` statements (24 / 13 is still the best), and `HalfAngle` as `?:`, as an inverted `if`, with an `r` local, or with an `s32` return or argument.
- **`ov000_0218867c`: the entry order of `mov #1` and `mov #0x64` is the order of the move-constant-loads groups.** Groups are handled by instance count (`17, 7, 7, 5, 4, ...`), and the group handled later lands first in the entry block. `1` and `0x64` both have 7 instances, and `1` is handled first. Passing 2 in one `vfunc_38` arm (a test only) drops the `1` group to 6 and gives the ROM's order. So before that pass the ROM had one `1` fewer or one `0x64` more, or it broke the tie the other way. Four spellings of the case-1 `p != NULL` store stay at 28 or get worse.

**Rule:** a head merge leaves a mark that can be read from the ROM alone: a cheap instruction just before the branch, held behind a reader of its register. Run `hm.py` on the ROM before reworking a draft. If the draft's output already has the same instruction in the same place, the miss is somewhere else.

### Round scC

No new match, and no source change. Scratch files are in `scratchpad/scC/` (scB's `hm.py`/`sw.py`/`t/`/`t2/`/`sch/` and tmA's `tmA/` tools pointed at the scC clone). New: `dv.py MOD FUNC SRC [OBJ]` prints a side-by-side diff; `t/mcg.py` (run as `MCPY=mcg.py t/mcl.sh ...`) adds a `LIST` dump of the constant groups in their pre-sort order, plus two diagnostic overrides, `FORCE=op170:17:12` (refuse that one move) and `TIE=1,2` (swap two entries of the sorted group array); `hs.py` emulates the group sort from a `LIST` dump; `hsx.py` lists the single changes that flip `1` and `0x64`; `pr.sh` prints a `0218867c` draft's score, the `17 -> 12` pressure and the group order; `t/mcra.py` is `mcg.py` plus tmA's colouring dump in one run.

- **Rule: move-constant-loads orders groups of equal count by MSL's heapsort, not by source order.** `0x526870` walks the blocks in list order and puts each new group (`op170`/`op171`/`op547`, equal operands) at the *front* of a linked list. `0x5262a0` copies that list to an array and calls `qsort` (`0x4792b0`, a Numerical-Recipes heapsort) with a comparator (`0x526280`) that compares counts only. So the order of tied groups depends on the whole list: how many groups there are, their counts, and the order they are found in. `hs.py` reproduces the dumped order exactly (all 15 groups of `0218867c`, and every function in `0214dd3c` and `021e7004`).

So the tie is not a sign of one fewer `1`. With both overrides on (`TIE=1,2`, `FORCE=op170:17:12`) and `p` declared before `n_0` in case 1, the draft's only register-masked diff is the case-1 tail order (`mov r1, #1` before the `data_02fe1534` load). A shared `Ang(y, x, neg)` inline for yaw and pitch is folded early and gives the base code, or 29 / 14 when used for pitch too. `if (1) {` gives the base code. - **Rule: MWCC orders the operands of a 64-bit multiply by register need, not by source order.** `smull lo, hi, Rm, Rs` takes the source's first operand as `Rm` when both sides need the same number of registers. If one side is a single value (a variable, or a variable combined with a constant: `b << 12`, `b - 0x1000`, `-b`, `b & 0xff`) and the other needs two (`b - a`, `(b << 12) - a`, `T[i]`), the single value goes into `Rm` whatever the source says (`toy/t1.c`–`t3.c`). So `FX_MUL(b - a, s)` and `FX_MUL(s, b - a)` compile the same way, and both put `s` in `Rm`. To get the ROM's `smull …, diff, s`, the difference must be a single value already: a local inside the inline (`s32 d = b - a;`), not a temp.
- **`ov000_0216715c`.** The ROM's lerp is `smull r1, r0, sl, r2`, with the difference in `Rm` and the sine in `Rs`. The draft has them the other way round. `static inline s32 Lerp715c(a, b, s) { s32 d = b - a; return LO_FX_MUL(d, s) + a; }` fixes the order (124 / 58 to 116 / 66, 113 to 109 with pool and branch offsets masked). But the loads of the inner block then schedule further from the ROM, so the register-masked count goes up, and the in-tree draft is unchanged. Swapping the operands, `a + …`, a spelled-out `(s64)` product and `FX_MUL` all give the base or the same result. Block-scope `dx`/`dy` locals (157), `b -= a` (144) and `x1 = (x1 << 12) - x0` statements (143) are worse. All 130 slots of `s`/`x0`/`y0`/`x1`/`y1` give 116 / 66. A named `s` for the outer sine (`k`, the `r6` temp) is forward-substituted (no change).
- **The sweep.** 23 of the 52 unmatched functions multiply in the ROM. Excluding `021b9b14` (scD) and `021fbda0` (a `.data` ownership problem), every best draft already reproduces the ROM's multiply forms. That covers the zero-register high words (`mla …, rZ` / `adc …, rZ` in `021fc40c`, `02201064`, `0220640c`, `021fe2a4`, `021cd91c`), the folded ones (`0216c310`, `0218867c`, `02053254`) and the `smlal` squares (`02206084`, `021fc7e0`, `021e7004`). No function cleaned; no source change. - **Rule: the trick is never a constant-group or tie effect.** In all 15 functions the `GROUP` lists of the trick file and of the literal draft have the same counts on each side of the 5 threshold and the same order where it matters (`grp/*.txt`). The second definition is a multi-definition register, so it is not movable, and it never changes which group is hoisted. Don't look for a missing or extra constant use.
- **What it does instead.** It does one of four things. (A) It adds a block boundary that is still there for the pre-allocation scheduler and for local copy propagation. After allocation the dead arm's `mov` is a redundant reload of the same register, the post-allocation CSE deletes it, and the `tst`/`beq` folds. The blocks then merge, bit 8 is cleared, and the merged block is scheduled again after allocation (round scA). (B) It keeps a constant or a load as a named object (low node number), so it is coloured after the codegen temps (round bgJ). (C) It makes one arm differ at the first post-allocation head merge. (D) It hides a one-instruction arm from the final peephole's "speculate above the compare" step. **Rule:** before trying spellings, compare `sch/sd7.sh` (is the block rescheduled after allocation?), `objs.sh` (is the variable a node?) and `t3/ph.sh` (head-merge and peephole stages) between the trick file and the literal draft. That tells which of A–D the trick buys. A plain statement or declaration reorder only helps in case B.
- **Per function (literal draft score in brackets):**

In one block, the pre-allocation scheduler (pressure flag on) always picks the `add`, because it is the last use of `y`. That happens in every source order, and that pick is the ROM's miss. With the boundary, list order wins. Any form where LICM hoists `y + 0x14` (in the loop, in the call, an inline `PlaceDigits(self, x, y + 0x14)` whose argument is substituted) gets the ROM's order. But the LICM vreg is the highest-numbered node, so it is coloured first (`r4` where the ROM has `r8`: 26 or 29 / 0, `0ff8/h*.cpp`, `g*.cpp`).
  - `ov013_022001b8` (3 / 3), D. With `m = FALSE` alone in its arm, the final peephole moves `mov r3, #1` above `cmp`. The trick keeps the arm two instructions long until the final peephole, so `52ad70` predicates both arms (`movne`/`moveq`). Both arms setting the same call arguments first (`b = 0x1000; z = 0; m = ...`, `01b8/a5.cpp`, 1 / 1) gets the head merges and the predication right. But the local CSE then turns `m = FALSE` into `movne r3, ip`, a copy of `z`. All 72 statement orders in the two arms stay at 1 or worse (`01b8/p/`).
  - `ov003_021ddce4` (3 / 3), C. `hm1` merges *every* identical leading instruction (`ldrh` and `bic #1`). `hm2` merges the `ldrh` and then predicates the arms. The ROM's arms therefore still differed at `hm1`, and the trick's `tst` is that difference.

The boundaries are before the `FX_Atan2` call (`9f80`, where the `smull` moves ahead of `ldr r2, [r5]`) and after `func_020627dc(0x8001)` (`b818`, where `mov r4, #1` moves behind `mov r1, #0x52`).
